akhfash:2-2.t: He said: ﴿أَنَّ لَهُمْ قَدَمَ صِدْقٍ﴾. "القدم" here means precedence (al-taqdīm), as you say: "هؤلاء أَهْلُ القَدَمِ في الأَسلام" (these are the people of precedence in Islam), i.e. those who sent forward good and so had precedence in it.

akhfash:5-5.t:
He said: ﴿وَقَدَّرَهُ مَنَازِلَ﴾, doubled; he made (وَقَدَّرُهُ) one of the verbs that take two objects, as though it were "وجعله منازل" (and He made it stations). And He said ﴿جَعَلَ ٱلشَّمْسَ ضِيَآءً وَٱلْقَمَرَ نُوراً﴾, making the moon itself the light, just as you say "جَعَلَهُ اللهُ خَلْقاً" (Allah made it a creation) when it is "created", and "هذا الدِرْهَمُ ضَرْبُ الأَمِير" (this dirham is the emir's minting) when it is "minted". And He said ﴿وَقُولُواْ لِلنَّاسِ حُسْناً﴾, making "الحسن" (goodness) the thing done, like "الخلق" (creation).
And He said ﴿وَقَدَّرَهُ مَنَازِلَ﴾ although He had mentioned the sun and the moon, just as He said ﴿وَٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَحَقُّ أَن يُرْضُوهُ﴾.

akhfash:9-9.t: He said: ﴿يَهْدِيهِمْ رَبُّهُمْ بِإِيمَانِهِمْ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِهِمُ ٱلأَنْهَارُ﴾. It is as though He made (تَجْرِي) a new beginning, cut off from what precedes.

akhfash:12-12.t:
He said: ﴿كَأَن لَّمْ يَدْعُنَآ إِلَىٰ ضُرٍّ مَّسَّهُ﴾ and ﴿كَأَن لَّمْ يَلْبَثُوۤاْ إِلاَّ سَاعَةً﴾. This is frequent in speech. It is the heavy "كَأَنَّ", but a pronoun is implied in it, so it is lightened, just as (أَنَّ)* is lightened with a pronoun implied in it; it is really "كَأَنْهُ لَمْ". The poet said [in the khafīf metre, and it is the two hundred and twenty-eighth poetic witness]:
*وَيْ كَأَنْ مَنْ يَكُنْ لَهُ نَشَبٌ يُحْبَبْ وَمَنْ يَفْتقِرْ يَعِشْ عَيْشُ ضرِّ*
(Ah, it seems that whoever has wealth is loved, and whoever becomes poor lives a life of hardship.)
And as he said [in the hazaj metre, and it is the two hundred and twenty-ninth poetic witness]:
[وصَدْرٍ مُشْرِقِ النَّحْرِ] * كَأَنْ ثَدْياهُ حُقّانِ
(And a bosom with a radiant throat, as though its breasts were two round caskets.)
i.e. "كَأَنْهُ ثَدْياهُ حُقَّانِ". Some recited "كَأَنْ ثَدْيْيهِ", lightening it and making it govern, without implying anything in it, as He said ﴿إِن كُلُّ نَفْسٍ لَمَا عَلَيْهَا حَافِظٌ﴾: he intended the meaning of the heavy form, so he made it govern as the heavy form governs, and did not imply a pronoun in it.

akhfash:19-19.t: He said: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ ٱلنَّاسُ إِلاَّ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً﴾: as the khabar of "كان", just as He said ﴿إِن كَانَتْ إِلاَّ صَيْحَةً وَاحِدَةً﴾, [i.e.]* "it was nothing but a single cry".

akhfash:22-22.t:
He said: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا كُنتُمْ فِي ٱلْفُلْكِ وَجَرَيْنَ بِهِم﴾. He said ﴿وَجَرَيْنَ بِهِم﴾ only because (الفُلْكَ) may be singular or plural; He said ﴿فِي ٱلْفُلْكِ ٱلْمَشْحُونِ﴾, where it is masculine. As for (حتَّى أَذا كُنْتُمْ في الفُلْكِ), its apodosis is His words ﴿جَآءَتْهَا رِيحٌ عَاصِفٌ﴾.
As for His words ﴿دَعَوُاْ ٱللَّهَ﴾, it is the apodosis of His words ﴿وَظَنُّوۤاْ أَنَّهُمْ أُحِيطَ بِهِمْ﴾. He said ﴿بِهِم﴾ although He had said ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ only because it is permissible to mention someone absent and then address him when you mean him, and to address and then put him in the wording of the absent, as in the poet's words [in the ṭawīl metre, and it is the one hundred and tenth poetic witness]:
أَسِيئِي بِنا أَوْ أَحْسِنِي لا مَلُوَمةً * لَدَيْنا وَلا مَقْلِيَّةً أَنْ تَقَلَّتِ
(Treat us ill or treat us well: you are not blamed by us, nor hated if she turns away in hatred.)

akhfash:23-23.t: He said: ﴿إِنَّمَا بَغْيُكُمْ عَلَىٰ أَنفُسِكُمْ مَّتَاعَ ٱلْحَيَاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾, i.e. "and that is the enjoyment of the life of this world". He meant: "your enjoyment is the enjoyment of the life of this world".

akhfash:24-24.t:
He said: ﴿كَمَآءٍ أَنزَلْنَاهُ﴾, meaning "like the likeness of water".
And He said ﴿وَٱزَّيَّنَتْ﴾, meaning "وتَزَيَّنُتْ" (and it adorned itself), but the tāʾ was assimilated into the zāy because the two points of articulation are close; when its first letter became quiescent, a connecting alif (alif al-waṣl) was added to it. And He said ﴿وَٱزَّيَّنَتْ﴾, doubled — "ازَّيُّناً" if he means the maṣdar — and it is from "التَزَيْنِ" (adornment). He added the alif when he assimilated only so as to join the speech, since one cannot begin with a quiescent letter.

akhfash:26-26.t: He said: ﴿وَلاَ يَرْهَقُ وُجُوهَهُمْ قَتَرٌ وَلاَ ذِلَّةٌ﴾, because it is from "رَهَقَ" "يَرْهَقُ" "رَهَقاً". [Translator's note: the past tense is usually vocalised «رَهِقَ»; translated as written.]

akhfash:27-27.t:
He said: ﴿جَزَآءُ سَيِّئَةٍ بِمِثْلِهَا﴾: the bāʾ is added, just as it is added in your saying ﴿بِحَسْبِكَ قولُ السُوءِ﴾ (enough for you is evil speech). [Translator's note: this is an Arabic idiom, not a Qur'anic quotation, though the source places it in ﴿…﴾.]
And He said ﴿كَأَنَّمَا أُغْشِيَتْ وُجُوهُهُمْ قِطَعاً مِّنَ ٱلْلَّيْلِ مُظْلِماً﴾: the ṭāʾ is quiescent [Translator's note: the source says «العين», i.e. the ʿayn-position of the root, which is the ṭāʾ] because it is not the plural of "القِطْعَة" but "قِطْعٌ", a noun on its own. The generality of people read (قِطَعا), meaning by it the plural of "القِطْعَة". The first is supported by His words (مُظْلِماً), because "القِطْع" is singular, so "المُظْلِم" can be its adjective. Those who read "القِطَع", meaning the plural, said: "We make مُظلِماً a ḥāl of اللَيْل (the night)". The first is the clearer of the two ways.

akhfash:28-28.t: He said: ﴿مَكَانَكُمْ أَنتُمْ وَشُرَكَآؤُكُمْ﴾, because it has the meaning "انتْظِروا أنتم وشركاؤكم" (wait, you and your partners).

akhfash:30-30.t: He said: ﴿هُنَالِكَ تَبْلُواْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَّآ أَسْلَفَتْ﴾, i.e. it will experience. Some read (تَتْلُو), i.e. it will follow it.

akhfash:31-31.t:
He said: ﴿أَمَّن يَمْلِكُ ٱلسَّمْعَ وٱلأَبْصَارَ﴾. If you say: "How did (أَمْ) come before (مَنْ)?" — it is because (مَنْ) is not originally interrogative; it merely makes the alif unnecessary. That is why (أَمْ) was put before it, just as the interrogative particle was put before (هَلْ); the interrogative is originally only the alif. And (أَمْ) enters for a meaning that is indispensable. The poet said [in the ṭawīl metre, and it is the two hundred and thirtieth poetic witness]:
أَبا مَالِكٍ هَلْ لُمْتَنِي مُذْ حَضَضْتِنَي * عَلَى القَتْلِ أَمْ هَلْ لامَنِي لَكَ لائِمُ
(Abū Mālik, have you blamed me since you urged me to the killing, or has any blamer blamed me on your account?)

akhfash:38-38.t: He said: ﴿فَأْتُواْ بِسُورَةٍ مِّثْلِهِ﴾. This is — and Allah knows best — "on the likeness of its sura", and he dropped "the sura", just as He said ﴿وَسْئَلِ ٱلْقَرْيَةَ﴾, meaning "the people of the town".

akhfash:50-50.t: He said: ﴿مَّاذَا يَسْتَعْجِلُ مِنْهُ ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ﴾. If you wish, you may make (ماذا) a single noun with the status of (ما); and if you wish, you may make (ذا) have the status of "الذي" (which).

akhfash:53-53.t: He said: ﴿وَيَسْتَنْبِئُونَكَ أَحَقٌّ هُوَ﴾, as though He said "and they say: is it true?".

akhfash:58-58.t: He said: ﴿قُلْ بِفَضْلِ ٱللَّهِ وَبِرَحْمَتِهِ فَبِذَلِكَ فَلْيَفْرَحُواْ هُوَ خَيْرٌ مِّمَّا يَجْمَعُونَ﴾. Some read (تَجْمعَون), i.e. "what you amass, O company of unbelievers". Some read (فَلْتَفْرَحُوا); it is a poor dialect of the Arabs, because this lām enters only in a position where "أَفْعَل" (the direct imperative) cannot be used. They say "لِيَقُلْ زَيْدٌ" (let Zayd say) because you cannot use "أَفْعَل" [for an absent person]. The lām does not enter when you address a man: you say "قُلْ" (say) and do not need the lām. His words ﴿فَبِذَلِكَ﴾ are a badal (substitute) for His words ﴿قُلْ بِفَضْلِ ٱللَّهِ وَبِرَحْمَتِهِ﴾.

akhfash:61-61.t: He said: ﴿وَمَا يَعْزُبُ عَن رَّبِّكَ مِن مِّثْقَالِ ذَرَّةٍ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ وَلاَ فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَلاَ أَصْغَرَ مِن ذٰلِكَ وَلاۤ أَكْبَرَ﴾, i.e. "and nothing smaller than that nor greater escapes Him", with the nominative. Some read (وَلا أصغرَ من ذلِكَ ولا أَكْبَرَ) with fatḥa, i.e. "nor of anything smaller than that nor of anything greater"; but it is "أَفْعَلَ" and is a diptote [so its genitive appears with fatḥa]. This is better in Arabic and more frequent in reading, and that is how we read.

akhfash:71-71.t:
He said: ﴿فَأَجْمِعُوۤاْ أَمْرَكُمْ وَشُرَكَآءَكُمْ﴾, and some read (وشُرَكاؤُكُمْ). The accusative is better, because you do not make an overt nominative noun follow a nominative pronoun [i.e. conjoin it to it]; but it has become acceptable here because of the separation between them, as He said ﴿أَإِذَا كُنَّا تُرَاباً وَآبَآؤُنَآ﴾, where it is good because He separated them by His word "تراباً". Some read (فَأَجْمِعوا), because they took it in the sense of "العَزْمِ" (resolve), since the Arabs say "أَجْمَعْتُ أَمْرِي", i.e. I resolved to say such-and-such, i.e. I determined upon it. And we read with the cut (hamzat al-qaṭʿ) alif. [Translator's note: the two forms (فَأَجْمِعُوا) are printed identically in the source; the variant is presumably «فَاجْمَعُوا» with a connecting alif.]
And He said ﴿ثُمَّ لاَ يَكُنْ أَمْرُكُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ غُمَّةً﴾: (يَكُنْ) is jussive by the prohibition.

akhfash:77-77.t: He said: ﴿أَتقُولُونَ لِلْحَقِّ لَمَّا جَآءَكُمْ أَسِحْرٌ هَـٰذَا﴾: this is by way of quoting (ḥikāya) their words, because they said "Is this magic?", so He said (أَتَقَوُلُونَ) (أَسِحْرٌ هذا).

akhfash:78-78.t: He said: ﴿لِتَلْفِتَنَا﴾, because you say "لَفَتُهُ", so "أَنَا أَلِفْتُهُ" "لَفْتَاً", i.e. I turn him away from his due.

akhfash:81-81.t: He said: ﴿مَا جِئْتُمْ بِهِ ٱلسِّحْرُ﴾; he says: "That which you have brought is magic". Some read (آلسِّحْرُ) with the interrogative.

akhfash:83-83.t: He said: ﴿عَلَىٰ خَوْفٍ مِّن فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَئِهِمْ﴾, meaning the chiefs of the offspring (al-dhurriyya).

akhfash:88-88.t:
He said: ﴿رَبَّنَا ٱطْمِسْ عَلَىٰ أَمْوَالِهِمْ وَٱشْدُدْ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ فَلاَ يُؤْمِنُواْ﴾: he put it in the accusative because the answer to a supplication with fāʾ is accusative; likewise in supplication when they disobeyed.
And He said ﴿رَبَّنَا لِيُضِلُّواْ عَن سَبِيلِكَ﴾, i.e. "so they went astray", just as He said ﴿فَٱلْتَقَطَهُ آلُ فِرْعَوْنَ لِيَكُونَ لَهُمْ عَدُوّاً وَحَزَناً﴾, i.e. "so he became". They did not pick him up in order that he become an enemy and a grief to them; [but] they picked him up and he became so. This lām comes in this meaning.
And His words ﴿فَلاَ يُؤْمِنُواْ﴾ are conjoined to (ليضلوّا).

akhfash:92-92.t:
He said: ﴿فَٱلْيَوْمَ نُنَجِّيكَ بِبَدَنِكَ﴾, and some read (نُنْجِيك). His words ﴿بِبَدَنِكَ﴾ mean: with no spirit in it.
Some said: (نُنُجِّيكَ) means "We shall raise you up on a height (najwa) of the land". Their saying that "البَدَن here is the coat of mail (الدِرْع)" is nothing and has no meaning.

akhfash:97-97.t: He said: ﴿وَلَوْ جَآءَتْهُمْ كُلُّ آيَةٍ﴾: He made the verb of "كلّ" feminine because He annexed it to "آية" (sign), which is feminine.

akhfash:99-99.t: He said: ﴿لآمَنَ مَن فِي ٱلأَرْضِ كُلُّهُمْ جَمِيعاً﴾: He brought His words (جَمِيعاً) as tawkīd (emphasis), just as He said ﴿لاَ تَتَّخِذُواْ إِلـٰهَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ﴾, where in His word ﴿إِلـٰهَيْنِ﴾ there is already an indication of "two".

akhfash:103-103.t: He said: ﴿كَذَلِكَ حَقّاً عَلَيْنَا نُنجِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾; he says: "Thus do We save the believers — a duty upon Us".

akhfash:105-105.t: He said: ﴿وَأَنْ أَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفاً﴾, i.e. "and I have been commanded to set your face to the religion".

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿وَلَوْ يُعَجِّلُ اللَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ الشَّرَّ اسْتِعْجَالَهُمْ﴾ i.e. like their hastening (كَاسْتِعْجَالِهِمْ) ﴿بِالْخَيْرِ لَقُضِيَ﴾ read with the verb built for the object (passive) and for the agent (active) ﴿إِلَيْهِمْ أَجَلُهُمْ﴾ read with the nominative and the accusative, by His destroying them; but He grants them respite. ﴿فَنَذَرُ﴾ We leave ﴿الَّذِينَ لَا يَرْجُونَ لِقَاءَنَا فِي طُغْيَانِهِمْ يَعْمَهُونَ﴾ wavering back and forth in bewilderment.

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿وَإِذَا مَسَّ الْإِنْسَانَ﴾ the disbeliever ﴿الضُّرُّ﴾ illness and poverty ﴿دَعَانَا لِجَنْبِهِ﴾ i.e. lying on his side ﴿أَوْ قَاعِدًا أَوْ قَائِمًا﴾ i.e. in every state. ﴿فَلَمَّا كَشَفْنَا عَنْهُ ضُرَّهُ مَرَّ﴾ upon his disbelief ﴿كَأَنْ﴾ lightened (mukhaffafa) [from كَأَنَّ], and its noun is omitted, i.e. كَأَنَّهُ ("as if he") ﴿لَمْ يَدْعُنَا إِلَى ضُرٍّ مَسَّهُ كَذَلِكَ﴾ just as supplication in hardship and turning away in ease were made to seem fair to him ﴿زُيِّنَ لِلْمُسْرِفِينَ﴾ the idolaters (al-mushrikūn) ﴿مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أَهْلَكْنَا الْقُرُونَ﴾ the nations ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ﴾ O people of Mecca ﴿لَمَّا ظَلَمُوا﴾ through shirk (associating partners with Allah) ﴿وَ﴾ [the implied meaning being] قَدْ ("while indeed") ﴿جَاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُمْ بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ﴾ which pointed to their truthfulness ﴿وَمَا كَانُوا لِيُؤْمِنُوا﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ظَلَمُوا. ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ just as We destroyed those ﴿نَجْزِي الْقَوْمَ الْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾ the disbelievers.

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَاكُمْ﴾ O people of Mecca ﴿خَلَائِفَ﴾ plural of خَلِيفَة (successor) ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ لِنَنْظُرَ كَيْفَ تَعْمَلُونَ فِيهَا﴾ and whether you will take a lesson from them and so believe Our messengers.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿وَإِذَا تُتْلَى عَلَيْهِمْ آيَاتُنَا﴾ the Quran ﴿بَيِّنَاتٍ﴾ clear; a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿قَالَ الَّذِينَ لَا يَرْجُونَ لِقَاءَنَا﴾ who do not fear the resurrection: ﴿ائْتِ بِقُرْآنٍ غَيْرِ هَذَا﴾ in which there is no faulting of our gods ﴿أَوْ بَدِّلْهُ﴾ of your own accord. ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them: ﴿مَا يَكُونُ﴾ it is not fitting ﴿لِي أَنْ أُبَدِّلَهُ مِنْ تِلْقَاءِ﴾ from the side of ﴿نَفْسِي إِنْ﴾ [meaning] not (مَا) ﴿أَتَّبِعُ إِلَّا مَا يُوحَى إِلَيَّ إِنِّي أَخَافُ إِنْ عَصَيْتُ رَبِّي﴾ by altering it ﴿عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ﴾ which is the Day of Resurrection.

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿قُلْ لَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ مَا تَلَوْتُهُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَلَا أَدْرَاكُمْ﴾ nor would He have made it known to you ﴿بِهِ﴾ — the لَا is negating, conjoined to what precedes it; and in one reading it is with a lām [i.e. وَلَأَدْرَاكُمْ], as the apodosis (jawāb) of لَوْ, i.e. He would have made it known to you on the tongue of someone other than me. ﴿فَقَدْ لَبِثْتُ﴾ I stayed ﴿فِيكُمْ عُمُرًا﴾ forty years ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِهِ﴾ telling you nothing [of it]. ﴿أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ﴾ that it is not from me?

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿فَمَنْ﴾ i.e. no one ﴿أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرَى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا﴾ by ascribing a partner to Him ﴿أَوْ كَذَّبَ بِآيَاتِهِ﴾ the Quran. ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ i.e. the matter (al-shaʾn) [the pronoun of the matter] ﴿لَا يُفْلِحُ﴾ will not attain happiness ﴿الْمُجْرِمُونَ﴾ the idolaters.

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿وَيَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. other than Him ﴿مَا لَا يَضُرُّهُمْ﴾ if they do not worship it ﴿وَلَا يَنْفَعُهُمْ﴾ if they do worship it — and that is the idols. ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ﴾ about them: ﴿هَؤُلَاءِ شُفَعَاؤُنَا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ قُلْ﴾ to them: ﴿أَتُنَبِّئُونَ اللَّهَ﴾ do you inform Him ﴿بِمَا لَا يَعْلَمُ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَلَا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ — an interrogative of disavowal (istifhām inkār), since had He a partner He would know of it, as nothing is hidden from Him. ﴿سُبْحَانَهُ﴾ as a declaration of His transcendence ﴿وَتَعَالَى عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ﴾ [with the implied object] هُ — [what they associate] with Him.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ النَّاسُ إِلَّا أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً﴾ upon one religion, which is Islam, from the time of Adam until Noah; and it is said: from the era of Abraham until ʿAmr ibn Luḥayy. ﴿فَاخْتَلَفُوا﴾ in that some held firm and some disbelieved. ﴿وَلَوْلَا كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾ to defer the recompense until the Day of Resurrection ﴿لَقُضِيَ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ i.e. between people in this world ﴿فِيمَا فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ﴾ of religion, by punishing the disbelievers.

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ﴾ i.e. the people of Mecca: ﴿لَوْلَا﴾ why not (هَلَّا) ﴿أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ﴾ upon Muhammad ﷺ ﴿آيَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ﴾ as the prophets had, such as the she-camel, the staff and the hand? ﴿فَقُلْ﴾ to them: ﴿إِنَّمَا الْغَيْبُ﴾ what is hidden from the servants, i.e. its affair, ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ and among it are the signs, so none brings them but He; my only duty is to convey. ﴿فَانْتَظِرُوا﴾ the punishment, if you do not believe; ﴿إِنِّي مَعَكُمْ مِنَ الْمُنْتَظِرِينَ﴾.

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿وَإِذَا أَذَقْنَا النَّاسَ﴾ i.e. the disbelievers of Mecca ﴿رَحْمَةً﴾ rain and fertility ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ ضَرَّاءَ﴾ misery and drought ﴿مَسَّتْهُمْ إِذَا لَهُمْ مَكْرٌ فِي آيَاتِنَا﴾ by mockery and denial. ﴿قُلِ﴾ to them: ﴿اللَّهُ أَسْرَعُ مَكْرًا﴾ in requital. ﴿إِنَّ رُسُلَنَا﴾ the guardian angels ﴿يَكْتُبُونَ مَا تَمْكُرُونَ﴾ read with tāʾ and yāʾ [تَمْكُرُونَ / يَمْكُرُونَ].

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي يُسَيِّرُكُمْ﴾ and in one reading [يَنْشُرُكُمْ] ﴿فِي الْبَرِّ وَالْبَحْرِ حَتَّى إِذَا كُنْتُمْ فِي الْفُلْكِ﴾ the ships ﴿وَجَرَيْنَ بِهِمْ﴾ — in it there is iltifāt (a shift of person) away from the second-person address — ﴿بِرِيحٍ طَيِّبَةٍ﴾ a gentle one ﴿وَفَرِحُوا بِهَا جَاءَتْهَا رِيحٌ عَاصِفٌ﴾ violently blowing, breaking everything ﴿وَجَاءَهُمُ الْمَوْجُ مِنْ كُلِّ مَكَانٍ وَظَنُّوا أَنَّهُمْ أُحِيطَ بِهِمْ﴾ i.e. they were destroyed ﴿دَعَوُا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ﴾ the supplication: ﴿لَئِنْ﴾ — the lām of the oath — ﴿أَنْجَيْتَنَا مِنْ هَذِهِ﴾ terrors ﴿لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الشَّاكِرِينَ﴾ those who affirm Your oneness.

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا أَنْجَاهُمْ إِذَا هُمْ يَبْغُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ بِغَيْرِ الْحَقِّ﴾ through shirk. ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنَّمَا بَغْيُكُمْ﴾ your wrongdoing ﴿عَلَى أَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾ because its sin falls upon them. It is ﴿مَتَاعُ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا﴾ — you enjoy yourselves in it a little — ﴿ثُمَّ إِلَيْنَا مَرْجِعُكُمْ﴾ after death ﴿فَنُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ and We shall recompense you for it. In one reading [مَتَاعَ] is in the accusative, i.e. [with the implied verb] "you enjoy" (تَتَمَتَّعُونَ).

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿إِنَّمَا مَثَلُ﴾ the description of ﴿الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا كَمَاءٍ﴾ rain ﴿أَنْزَلْنَاهُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ فَاخْتَلَطَ بِهِ﴾ because of it ﴿نَبَاتُ الْأَرْضِ﴾ and parts of it became entangled with others ﴿مِمَّا يَأْكُلُ النَّاسُ﴾ of wheat, barley and other things ﴿وَالْأَنْعَامُ﴾ of pasture, ﴿حَتَّى إِذَا أَخَذَتِ الْأَرْضُ زُخْرُفَهَا﴾ its splendour of vegetation ﴿وَازَّيَّنَتْ﴾ with blossoms — its original form is تَزَيَّنَتْ; the tāʾ was changed into a zāy and assimilated into the zāy — ﴿وَظَنَّ أَهْلُهَا أَنَّهُمْ قَادِرُونَ عَلَيْهَا﴾ able to gather its fruits, ﴿أَتَاهَا أَمْرُنَا﴾ Our decree or Our punishment ﴿لَيْلًا أَوْ نَهَارًا فَجَعَلْنَاهَا﴾ i.e. its crops ﴿حَصِيدًا﴾ like something harvested with sickles, ﴿كَأَنْ﴾ lightened (mukhaffafa), i.e. كَأَنَّهَا ("as if it") ﴿لَمْ تَغْنَ﴾ had not been ﴿بِالْأَمْسِ كَذَلِكَ نُفَصِّلُ﴾ We make clear ﴿الْآيَاتِ لِقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ﴾.

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿وَاللَّهُ يَدْعُوا إِلَى دَارِ السَّلَامِ﴾ i.e. of safety, which is Paradise, by calling to faith ﴿وَيَهْدِي مَنْ يَشَاءُ﴾ His guidance ﴿إِلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾ the religion of Islam.

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿لِلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا﴾ through faith ﴿الْحُسْنَى﴾ Paradise ﴿وَزِيَادَةٌ﴾ which is the beholding of Him, Exalted is He, as in the hadith of Muslim. ﴿وَلَا يَرْهَقُ﴾ will cover ﴿وُجُوهَهُمْ قَتَرٌ﴾ blackness ﴿وَلَا ذِلَّةٌ﴾ gloom. ﴿أُولَئِكَ أَصْحَابُ الْجَنَّةِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ﴾.

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ conjoined to الَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا, i.e. "and for those who" (وَلِلَّذِينَ) ﴿كَسَبُوا السَّيِّئَاتِ﴾ committed shirk: ﴿جَزَاءُ سَيِّئَةٍ بِمِثْلِهَا وَتَرْهَقُهُمْ ذِلَّةٌ مَا لَهُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ مِنْ﴾ redundant (zāʾida) ﴿عَاصِمٍ﴾ protector. ﴿كَأَنَّمَا أُغْشِيَتْ﴾ were clothed ﴿وُجُوهُهُمْ قِطَعًا﴾ with a fatḥa on the ṭāʾ, plural of قِطْعَة, and with it vowelless [قِطْعًا], i.e. a portion ﴿مِنَ اللَّيْلِ مُظْلِمًا أُولَئِكَ أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ﴾.

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿وَ﴾ mention ﴿يَوْمَ نَحْشُرُهُمْ﴾ i.e. creation ﴿جَمِيعًا ثُمَّ نَقُولُ لِلَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا مَكَانَكُمْ﴾ accusative through an implied "keep to" (الْزَمُوا) ﴿أَنْتُمْ﴾ a tawkīd (emphasis) of the latent (mustatir) pronoun in the implied verb, so that something may be conjoined to it ﴿وَشُرَكَاؤُكُمْ﴾ i.e. the idols. ﴿فَزَيَّلْنَا﴾ We separated ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ and the believers, as in the ayah {وَامْتَازُوا الْيَوْمَ أَيُّهَا الْمُجْرِمُونَ}. ﴿وَقَالَ﴾ to them ﴿شُرَكَاؤُهُمْ مَا كُنْتُمْ إِيَّانَا تَعْبُدُونَ﴾ — مَا is negating, and the object was put first for the sake of the verse-ending (fāṣila).

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿فَكَفَى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيدًا بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكُمْ إِنْ﴾ lightened (mukhaffafa), i.e. إِنَّا ("indeed we") ﴿كُنَّا عَنْ عِبَادَتِكُمْ لَغَافِلِينَ﴾.

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿هُنَالِكَ﴾ i.e. on that day ﴿تَبْلُو﴾ from al-balwā (testing); and in one reading with two tāʾs [تَتْلُو], from tilāwa (reciting) ﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَا أَسْلَفَتْ﴾ what it sent ahead of deeds ﴿وَرُدُّوا إِلَى اللَّهِ مَوْلَاهُمُ الْحَقِّ﴾ the established, the everlasting ﴿وَضَلَّ﴾ vanished ﴿عَنْهُمْ مَا كَانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ﴾ against Him, of partners.

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them: ﴿مَنْ يَرْزُقُكُمْ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ﴾ with rain ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ with vegetation, ﴿أَمَّنْ يَمْلِكُ السَّمْعَ﴾ in the sense of "hearings" (الْأَسْمَاع), i.e. their creation, ﴿وَالْأَبْصَارَ وَمَنْ يُخْرِجُ الْحَيَّ مِنَ الْمَيِّتِ وَيُخْرِجُ الْمَيِّتَ مِنَ الْحَيِّ وَمَنْ يُدَبِّرُ الْأَمْرَ﴾ among the creatures? ﴿فَسَيَقُولُونَ﴾ He is ﴿اللَّهُ فَقُلْ﴾ to them: ﴿أَفَلَا تَتَّقُونَ﴾ [with the implied object] هُ — will you not fear Him, and so believe?

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿فَذَلِكُمُ﴾ the doer of these things ﴿اللَّهُ رَبُّكُمُ الْحَقُّ﴾ the established. ﴿فَمَاذَا بَعْدَ الْحَقِّ إِلَّا الضَّلَالُ﴾ — an interrogative of affirmation (istifhām taqrīr), i.e. there is nothing after it other than it; so whoever misses the truth, which is the worship of Allah, falls into misguidance. ﴿فَأَنَّى﴾ how ﴿تُصْرَفُونَ﴾ from faith, while the proof stands?

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ just as these were turned away from faith ﴿حَقَّتْ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ فَسَقُوا﴾ disbelieved — and it [the word] is {لَأَمْلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ} (the ayah), or it is ﴿أَنَّهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾.

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿قُلْ هَلْ مِنْ شُرَكَائِكُمْ مَنْ يَبْدَؤُا الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ قُلِ اللَّهُ يَبْدَؤُا الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ فَأَنَّى تُؤْفَكُونَ﴾ are you turned away from His worship, while the proof stands?

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿قُلْ هَلْ مِنْ شُرَكَائِكُمْ مَنْ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْحَقِّ﴾ by setting up proofs and creating [the capacity for] being guided? ﴿قُلِ اللَّهُ يَهْدِي لِلْحَقِّ أَفَمَنْ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْحَقِّ﴾ — and He is Allah — ﴿أَحَقُّ أَنْ يُتَّبَعَ أَمْ مَنْ لَا يَهِدِّي﴾ is not guided (يَهْتَدِي) ﴿إِلَّا أَنْ يُهْدَى﴾ [is he] more worthy of being followed? — an interrogative of affirmation and rebuke (taqrīr wa-tawbīkh), i.e. the first is more worthy. ﴿فَمَا لَكُمْ كَيْفَ تَحْكُمُونَ﴾ this corrupt judgement of following what has no right to be followed?

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿وَمَا يَتَّبِعُ أَكْثَرُهُمْ﴾ in worshipping the idols ﴿إِلَّا ظَنًّا﴾ in that they blindly followed their fathers in it. ﴿إِنَّ الظَّنَّ لَا يُغْنِي مِنَ الْحَقِّ شَيْئًا﴾ in matters where what is required is knowledge. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ بِمَا يَفْعَلُونَ﴾ and He will recompense them for it.

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ هَذَا الْقُرْآنُ أَنْ يُفْتَرَى﴾ i.e. a fabrication (افْتِرَاءً) ﴿مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ other than Him; ﴿وَلَكِنْ﴾ it was sent down as ﴿تَصْدِيقَ الَّذِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ﴾ of the scriptures ﴿وَتَفْصِيلَ الْكِتَابِ﴾ a clarification of what Allah has prescribed of rulings and other things. ﴿لَا رَيْبَ﴾ no doubt ﴿فِيهِ مِنْ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ attached (mutaʿalliq) to تَصْدِيقَ, or to the omitted أَنْزَلَ. It has also been read with تَصْدِيقُ and تَفْصِيلُ in the nominative, by implying هُوَ ("it is").

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾ [meaning] "rather, do…?" (بَلْ أَ) ﴿يَقُولُونَ افْتَرَاهُ﴾ Muhammad invented it? ﴿قُلْ فَأْتُوا بِسُورَةٍ مِثْلِهِ﴾ in eloquence and rhetorical excellence, by way of fabrication, for you are eloquent Arabs like me; ﴿وَادْعُوا﴾ for help with it ﴿مَنِ اسْتَطَعْتُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. other than Him ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ in [saying] that it is a fabrication. But they were not able to do that. Allah the Exalted said:

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿بَلْ كَذَّبُوا بِمَا لَمْ يُحِيطُوا بِعِلْمِهِ﴾ i.e. the Quran, and they did not reflect on it, ﴿وَلَمَّا﴾ [meaning] not (لَمْ) ﴿يَأْتِهِمْ تَأْوِيلُهُ﴾ the outcome of the threat it contains. ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ [with] that denial ﴿كَذَّبَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ their messengers. ﴿فَانْظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ by denying the messengers, i.e. their final state of destruction; so likewise We will destroy these.

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ﴾ i.e. of the people of Mecca ﴿مَنْ يُؤْمِنُ بِهِ﴾ because Allah knows that of them ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ لَا يُؤْمِنُ بِهِ﴾ ever. ﴿وَرَبُّكَ أَعْلَمُ بِالْمُفْسِدِينَ﴾ — a threat to them.

celaleyn:41-41.t: ﴿وَإِنْ كَذَّبُوكَ فَقُلْ﴾ to them: ﴿لِي عَمَلِي وَلَكُمْ عَمَلُكُمْ﴾ i.e. to each the recompense of his deeds. ﴿أَنْتُمْ بَرِيئُونَ مِمَّا أَعْمَلُ وَأَنَا بَرِيءٌ مِمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ — and this is abrogated by the Verse of the Sword.

celaleyn:42-42.t: ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَسْتَمِعُونَ إِلَيْكَ﴾ when you recite the Quran. ﴿أَفَأَنْتَ تُسْمِعُ الصُّمَّ﴾ — He likened them to them in not benefiting from what is recited to them — ﴿وَلَوْ كَانُوا﴾ along with deafness ﴿لَا يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ do not reflect?

celaleyn:43-43.t: ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَنْظُرُ إِلَيْكَ أَفَأَنْتَ تَهْدِي الْعُمْيَ وَلَوْ كَانُوا لَا يُبْصِرُونَ﴾ — He likened them to them in not being guided; indeed [they are] worse: {فَإِنَّهَا لَا تَعْمَى الْأَبْصَارُ وَلَكِنْ تَعْمَى الْقُلُوبُ الَّتِي فِي الصُّدُورِ}.

celaleyn:44-44.t: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَظْلِمُ النَّاسَ شَيْئًا وَلَكِنَّ النَّاسَ أَنْفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:45-45.t: ﴿وَيَوْمَ يَحْشُرُهُمْ [نَحْشُرُهُمْ] كَأَنْ﴾ i.e. كَأَنَّهُمْ ("as if they") ﴿لَمْ يَلْبَثُوا﴾ in the world or in the graves ﴿إِلَّا سَاعَةً مِنَ النَّهَارِ﴾ because of the terror of what they see; and the clause of comparison is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun. ﴿يَتَعَارَفُونَ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ they recognise one another when they are resurrected, then the mutual recognition ceases because of the severity of the circumstances; and the clause is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), or what the adverb [يَوْمَ] is attached to. ﴿قَدْ خَسِرَ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِلِقَاءِ اللَّهِ﴾ the resurrection ﴿وَمَا كَانُوا مُهْتَدِينَ﴾.

celaleyn:46-46.t: ﴿وَإِمَّا﴾ — in it the nūn of the conditional إِنْ is assimilated into the added (mazīda) مَا — ﴿نُرِيَنَّكَ بَعْضَ الَّذِي نَعِدُهُمْ﴾ with, of punishment, in your lifetime — and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e. "then so be it" (فَذَاكَ) — ﴿أَوْ نَتَوَفَّيَنَّكَ﴾ before punishing them, ﴿فَإِلَيْنَا مَرْجِعُهُمْ ثُمَّ اللَّهُ شَهِيدٌ﴾ fully aware ﴿عَلَى مَا يَفْعَلُونَ﴾ of their denial and disbelief, and He will punish them with the severest punishment.

celaleyn:47-47.t: ﴿وَلِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ﴾ of the nations ﴿رَسُولٌ فَإِذَا جَاءَ رَسُولُهُمْ﴾ to them and they denied him, ﴿قُضِيَ بَيْنَهُمْ بِالْقِسْطِ﴾ with justice, so they are punished and the messenger and those who believed him are saved, ﴿وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ﴾ by being punished without a crime. So likewise shall We do with these.

celaleyn:48-48.t: ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَى هَذَا الْوَعْدُ﴾ of punishment ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ in it?

celaleyn:49-49.t: ﴿قُلْ لَا أَمْلِكُ لِنَفْسِي ضَرًّا﴾ to ward off ﴿وَلَا نَفْعًا﴾ to bring about ﴿إِلَّا مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ﴾ i.e. [what] He enables me to do; so how could I have power over bringing the punishment upon you? ﴿لِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ أَجَلٌ﴾ a known term for their destruction. ﴿إِذَا جَاءَ أَجَلُهُمْ فَلَا يَسْتَأْخِرُونَ﴾ remain behind it ﴿سَاعَةً وَلَا يَسْتَقْدِمُونَ﴾ go ahead of it.

celaleyn:50-50.t: ﴿قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ﴾ tell me: ﴿إِنْ أَتَاكُمْ عَذَابُهُ﴾ i.e. Allah's ﴿بَيَاتًا﴾ by night ﴿أَوْ نَهَارًا مَاذَا﴾ what thing ﴿يَسْتَعْجِلُ مِنْهُ﴾ i.e. of the punishment ﴿الْمُجْرِمُونَ﴾ the idolaters? — In it the overt noun is put in the place of the pronoun; and the interrogative clause is the apodosis of a condition, as when you say: "If I come to you, what will you give me?" What is intended by it is to convey the dreadfulness [of it], i.e. how terrible is what they sought to hasten!

celaleyn:51-51.t: ﴿أَثُمَّ إِذَا مَا وَقَعَ﴾ befell you ﴿آمَنْتُمْ بِهِ﴾ i.e. in Allah, or in the punishment, when it comes down? — The hamza is for disavowing the delay; so it will not be accepted from you, and it will be said to you: ﴿آلْآنَ﴾ do you believe, ﴿وَقَدْ كُنْتُمْ بِهِ تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ﴾ in mockery?

celaleyn:52-52.t: ﴿ثُمَّ قِيلَ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا ذُوقُوا عَذَابَ الْخُلْدِ﴾ i.e. in which you will abide forever. ﴿هَلْ﴾ [meaning] not (مَا) ﴿تُجْزَوْنَ إِلَّا﴾ the recompense ﴿بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَكْسِبُونَ﴾.

celaleyn:53-53.t: ﴿وَيَسْتَنْبِئُونَكَ﴾ they ask you to inform them: ﴿أَحَقٌّ هُوَ﴾ i.e. what you have promised us of punishment and resurrection? ﴿قُلْ إِي﴾ yes ﴿وَرَبِّي إِنَّهُ لَحَقٌّ وَمَا أَنْتُمْ بِمُعْجِزِينَ﴾ escaping the punishment.

celaleyn:54-54.t: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّ لِكُلِّ نَفْسٍ ظَلَمَتْ﴾ disbelieved ﴿مَا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ all of it, of wealth, ﴿لَافْتَدَتْ بِهِ﴾ from the punishment on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿وَأَسَرُّوا النَّدَامَةَ﴾ over abandoning faith ﴿لَمَّا رَأَوُا الْعَذَابَ﴾ — their leaders hid it from the weak whom they had led astray, for fear of reproach. ﴿وَقُضِيَ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ between the creatures ﴿بِالْقِسْطِ﴾ with justice ﴿وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ﴾ in anything.

celaleyn:55-55.t: ﴿أَلَا إِنَّ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ أَلَا إِنَّ وَعْدَ اللَّهِ﴾ of resurrection and recompense ﴿حَقٌّ﴾ established, ﴿وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ﴾ i.e. of people ﴿لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ that.

celaleyn:56-56.t: ﴿هُوَ يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ in the Hereafter, and He will recompense you for your deeds.

celaleyn:57-57.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ﴾ i.e. people of Mecca, ﴿قَدْ جَاءَتْكُمْ مَوْعِظَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ﴾ a Book containing what is for you and what is against you, and it is the Quran, ﴿وَشِفَاءٌ﴾ a remedy ﴿لِمَا فِي الصُّدُورِ﴾ of corrupt beliefs and doubts ﴿وَهُدًى﴾ from misguidance ﴿وَرَحْمَةٌ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ in it.

celaleyn:58-58.t: ﴿قُلْ بِفَضْلِ اللَّهِ﴾ Islam ﴿وَبِرَحْمَتِهِ﴾ the Quran ﴿فَبِذَلِكَ﴾ bounty and mercy ﴿فَلْيَفْرَحُوا هُوَ خَيْرٌ مِمَّا يَجْمَعُونَ﴾ of this world — read with yāʾ and tāʾ [يَجْمَعُونَ / تَجْمَعُونَ].

celaleyn:59-59.t: ﴿قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ﴾ tell me: ﴿مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ﴾ created ﴿لَكُمْ مِنْ رِزْقٍ فَجَعَلْتُمْ مِنْهُ حَرَامًا وَحَلَالًا﴾ such as the baḥīra, the sāʾiba and carrion. ﴿قُلْ آللَّهُ أَذِنَ لَكُمْ﴾ in that, in declaring lawful and unlawful? No. ﴿أَمْ﴾ rather (بَلْ) ﴿عَلَى اللَّهِ تَفْتَرُونَ﴾ you lie, by attributing that to Him.

celaleyn:60-60.t: ﴿وَمَا ظَنُّ الَّذِينَ يَفْتَرُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ﴾ i.e. what do they think He will do with them ﴿يَوْمَ الْقِيَمَةِ﴾ — do they reckon that He will not punish them? No. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى النَّاسِ﴾ by granting them respite and bestowing favours on them, ﴿وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَا يَشْكُرُونَ﴾.

celaleyn:61-61.t: ﴿وَمَا تَكُونُ﴾ O Muhammad ﴿فِي شَأْنٍ﴾ an affair ﴿وَمَا تَتْلُو مِنْهُ﴾ i.e. of the affair, or from Allah, ﴿مِنْ قُرْآنٍ﴾ which He sent down to you ﴿وَلَا تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ — He addresses him and his community — ﴿مِنْ عَمَلٍ إِلَّا كُنَّا عَلَيْكُمْ شُهُودًا﴾ watchers ﴿إِذْ تُفِيضُونَ﴾ you engage ﴿فِيهِ﴾ i.e. in the deed. ﴿وَمَا يَعْزُبُ﴾ is hidden ﴿عَنْ رَبِّكَ مِنْ مِثْقَالِ﴾ the weight of ﴿ذَرَّةٍ﴾ the smallest ant ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِي السَّمَاءِ وَلَا أَصْغَرَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ وَلَا أَكْبَرَ إِلَّا فِي كِتَابٍ مُبِينٍ﴾ clear, which is the Preserved Tablet.

celaleyn:62-62.t: ﴿أَلَا إِنَّ أَوْلِيَاءَ اللَّهِ لَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ﴾ in the Hereafter. They are:

celaleyn:63-63.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَكَانُوا يَتَّقُونَ﴾ Allah, by complying with His commands and prohibitions.

celaleyn:64-64.t: ﴿لَهُمُ الْبُشْرَى فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا﴾ — explained, in a hadith that al-Ḥākim declared sound, as the righteous dream which a man sees or which is seen for him — ﴿وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ﴾ Paradise and the reward. ﴿لَا تَبْدِيلَ لِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ﴾ there is no breaking of His promises. ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ what has been mentioned ﴿هُوَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ﴾.

celaleyn:65-65.t: ﴿وَلَا يَحْزُنْكَ قَوْلُهُمْ﴾ to you, "You are not sent", and other things. ﴿إِنَّ﴾ resumptive (istiʾnāf) ﴿الْعِزَّةَ﴾ might ﴿لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًا هُوَ السَّمِيعُ﴾ of speech ﴿الْعَلِيمُ﴾ of deeds, so He will recompense them and help you.

celaleyn:66-66.t: ﴿أَلَا إِنَّ لِلَّهِ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ as servants, possessions and creation. ﴿وَمَا يَتَّبِعُ الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ﴾ worship ﴿مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. other than Him — idols — ﴿شُرَكَاءَ﴾ to Him in reality? Exalted is He above that. ﴿إِنْ﴾ [meaning] not (مَا) ﴿يَتَّبِعُونَ﴾ in that ﴿إِلَّا الظَّنَّ﴾ i.e. their supposition that they are gods who will intercede for them ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ [meaning] not (مَا) ﴿هُمْ إِلَّا يَخْرُصُونَ﴾ lie in that.

celaleyn:67-67.t: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ اللَّيْلَ لِتَسْكُنُوا فِيهِ وَالنَّهَارَ مُبْصِرًا﴾ — attributing seeing to it is figurative (majāz), because one sees in it. ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ﴾ indications of His oneness, Exalted is He, ﴿لِقَوْمٍ يَسْمَعُونَ﴾ a hearing of reflection and taking admonition.

celaleyn:68-68.t: ﴿قَالُوا﴾ i.e. the Jews, the Christians and those who claimed that the angels are the daughters of Allah: ﴿اتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ وَلَدًا﴾. Allah the Exalted said to them: ﴿سُبْحَانَهُ﴾ declaring Him transcendent above [having] a child. ﴿هُوَ الْغَنِيُّ﴾ in no need of anyone; only one who needs a child seeks one. ﴿لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ as possession, creation and servants. ﴿إِنْ﴾ [meaning] not (مَا) ﴿عِنْدَكُمْ مِنْ سُلْطَانٍ﴾ proof ﴿بِهَذَا﴾ which you are saying. ﴿أَتَقُولُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ — an interrogative of rebuke (istifhām tawbīkh).

celaleyn:69-69.t: ﴿قُلْ إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَفْتَرُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ﴾ by ascribing a child to Him ﴿لَا يُفْلِحُونَ﴾ will not attain happiness. For them is

celaleyn:70-70.t: ﴿مَتَاعٌ﴾ a little ﴿فِي الدُّنْيَا﴾ which they enjoy for the span of their lives; ﴿ثُمَّ إِلَيْنَا مَرْجِعُهُمْ﴾ through death; ﴿ثُمَّ نُذِيقُهُمُ الْعَذَابَ الشَّدِيدَ﴾ after death ﴿بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْفُرُونَ﴾.

celaleyn:71-71.t: ﴿وَاتْلُ﴾ O Muhammad ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ i.e. the disbelievers of Mecca ﴿نَبَأَ﴾ the story ﴿نُوحٍ﴾ — and from it is made a badal (substitute): ﴿إِذْ قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِ يَا قَوْمِ إِنْ كَانَ كَبُرَ﴾ become burdensome ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ مَقَامِي﴾ my staying among you ﴿وَتَذْكِيرِي﴾ my admonishing you ﴿بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ فَعَلَى اللَّهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ فَأَجْمِعُوا أَمْرَكُمْ﴾ resolve upon a course you will take against me ﴿وَشُرَكَاءَكُمْ﴾ — the wāw is in the sense of "with" (مَعَ) — ﴿ثُمَّ لَا يَكُنْ أَمْرُكُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ غُمَّةً﴾ concealed; rather, make it public and confront me openly with it; ﴿ثُمَّ اقْضُوا إِلَيَّ﴾ carry out what you intend ﴿وَلَا تُنْظِرُونِ﴾ give me no respite, for I do not care about you.

celaleyn:72-72.t: ﴿فَإِنْ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ﴾ from my admonition — ﴿فَمَا سَأَلْتُكُمْ مِنْ أَجْرٍ﴾ a reward for it, that you should turn away. ﴿إِنْ﴾ [meaning] not (مَا) ﴿أَجْرِيَ﴾ my reward ﴿إِلَّا عَلَى اللَّهِ وَأُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ﴾.

celaleyn:73-73.t: ﴿فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَنَجَّيْنَاهُ وَمَنْ مَعَهُ فِي الْفُلْكِ﴾ the ship ﴿وَجَعَلْنَاهُمْ﴾ i.e. those with him ﴿خَلَائِفَ﴾ in the land ﴿وَأَغْرَقْنَا الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا﴾ by the flood. ﴿فَانْظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ الْمُنْذَرِينَ﴾ in their destruction; so likewise We do with whoever denies.

celaleyn:74-74.t: ﴿ثُمَّ بَعَثْنَا مِنْ بَعْدِهِ﴾ i.e. Noah ﴿رُسُلًا إِلَى قَوْمِهِمْ﴾ such as Abraham, Hūd and Ṣāliḥ, ﴿فَجَاءُوهُمْ بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ﴾ the miracles, ﴿فَمَا كَانُوا لِيُؤْمِنُوا بِمَا كَذَّبُوا بِهِ مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ i.e. before the messengers were sent to them. ﴿كَذَلِكَ نَطْبَعُ﴾ We seal ﴿عَلَى قُلُوبِ الْمُعْتَدِينَ﴾ so they do not accept faith, just as We sealed the hearts of those.

celaleyn:75-75.t: ﴿ثُمَّ بَعَثْنَا مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ مُوسَى وَهَارُونَ إِلَى فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَئِهِ﴾ his people ﴿بِآيَاتِنَا﴾ the nine ﴿فَاسْتَكْبَرُوا﴾ from believing in them ﴿وَكَانُوا قَوْمًا مُجْرِمِينَ﴾.

celaleyn:76-76.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا جَاءَهُمُ الْحَقُّ مِنْ عِنْدِنَا قَالُوا إِنَّ هَذَا لَسِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ clear, manifest.

celaleyn:77-77.t: ﴿قَالَ مُوسَى أَتَقُولُونَ لِلْحَقِّ لَمَّا جَاءَكُمْ﴾ that it is magic? ﴿أَسِحْرٌ هَذَا﴾ when the one who brought it has succeeded and nullified the magic of the magicians? ﴿وَلَا يُفْلِحُ السَّاحِرُونَ﴾. The interrogative in both places is for disavowal (inkār).

celaleyn:78-78.t: ﴿قَالُوا أَجِئْتَنَا لِتَلْفِتَنَا﴾ to turn us back ﴿عَمَّا وَجَدْنَا عَلَيْهِ آبَاءَنَا وَتَكُونَ لَكُمَا الْكِبْرِيَاءُ﴾ sovereignty ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ the land of Egypt? ﴿وَمَا نَحْنُ لَكُمَا بِمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ believers.

celaleyn:79-79.t: ﴿وَقَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ ائْتُونِي بِكُلِّ سَاحِرٍ عَلِيمٍ﴾ excelling in the knowledge of magic.

celaleyn:80-80.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا جَاءَ السَّحَرَةُ قَالَ لَهُمْ مُوسَى﴾ after they had said to him {إِمَّا أَنْ تُلْقِيَ وَإِمَّا أَنْ نَكُونَ نَحْنُ الْمُلْقِينَ}: ﴿أَلْقُوا مَا أَنْتُمْ مُلْقُونَ﴾.

celaleyn:81-81.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا أَلْقَوْا﴾ their ropes and staffs ﴿قَالَ مُوسَى مَا﴾ — interrogative, a mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is ﴿جِئْتُمْ بِهِ أَآلسِّحْرُ﴾ — a badal (substitute); and in one reading with a single hamza [السِّحْرُ], as a statement, so مَا is a relative noun and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَيُبْطِلُهُ﴾ i.e. will obliterate it. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُصْلِحُ عَمَلَ الْمُفْسِدِينَ﴾.

celaleyn:82-82.t: ﴿وَيُحِقُّ﴾ establishes and makes manifest ﴿اللَّهُ الْحَقَّ بِكَلِمَاتِهِ﴾ by His promises, ﴿وَلَوْ كَرِهَ الْمُجْرِمُونَ﴾.

celaleyn:83-83.t: ﴿فَمَا آمَنَ لِمُوسَى إِلَّا ذُرِّيَّةٌ﴾ a group ﴿مِنْ﴾ the children of ﴿قَوْمِهِ﴾ i.e. Pharaoh's [people], ﴿عَلَى خَوْفٍ مِنْ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَئِهِمْ أَنْ يَفْتِنَهُمْ﴾ turn them away from his religion by torturing them. ﴿وَإِنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ لَعَالٍ﴾ arrogant ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ the land of Egypt, ﴿وَإِنَّهُ لَمِنَ الْمُسْرِفِينَ﴾ those who exceed the bounds, by claiming lordship.

celaleyn:84-84.t: ﴿وَقَالَ مُوسَى يَا قَوْمِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ آمَنْتُمْ بِاللَّهِ فَعَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلُوا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُسْلِمِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:85-85.t: ﴿فَقَالُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ تَوَكَّلْنَا رَبَّنَا لَا تَجْعَلْنَا فِتْنَةً لِلْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ i.e. do not give them the upper hand over us, so that they think they are upon the truth and are thereby tempted by us.

celaleyn:86-86.t: ﴿وَنَجِّنَا بِرَحْمَتِكَ مِنَ الْقَوْمِ الْكَافِرِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:87-87.t: ﴿وَأَوْحَيْنَا إِلَى مُوسَى وَأَخِيهِ أَنْ تَبَوَّءَا﴾ take ﴿لِقَوْمِكُمَا بِمِصْرَ بُيُوتًا وَاجْعَلُوا بُيُوتَكُمْ قِبْلَةً﴾ a place of prayer in which you pray, so that you may be safe from fear — Pharaoh had prevented them from praying — ﴿وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلَوةَ﴾ perform it fully ﴿وَبَشِّرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ of victory and Paradise.

celaleyn:88-88.t: ﴿وَقَالَ مُوسَى رَبَّنَا إِنَّكَ آتَيْتَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَأَهُ زِينَةً وَأَمْوَالًا فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا رَبَّنَا﴾ You gave them that ﴿لِيُضِلُّوا﴾ as its outcome ﴿عَنْ سَبِيلِكَ﴾ Your religion. ﴿رَبَّنَا اطْمِسْ عَلَى أَمْوَالِهِمْ﴾ transform them ﴿وَاشْدُدْ عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ seal them and make them fast, ﴿فَلَا يُؤْمِنُوا حَتَّى يَرَوُا الْعَذَابَ الْأَلِيمَ﴾ the painful. He supplicated against them, and Aaron said "Āmīn" to his supplication.

celaleyn:89-89.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ the Exalted: ﴿قَدْ أُجِيبَتْ دَعْوَتُكُمَا﴾ — so their wealth was transformed into stones, and Pharaoh did not believe until drowning overtook him — ﴿فَاسْتَقِيمَا﴾ in the mission and the call, until the punishment comes to them, ﴿وَلَا تَتَّبِعَانِّ سَبِيلَ الَّذِينَ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ in seeking to hasten My decree. It is narrated that he remained forty years after it.

celaleyn:90-90.t: ﴿وَجَاوَزْنَا بِبَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ الْبَحْرَ فَأَتْبَعَهُمْ﴾ overtook them ﴿فِرْعَوْنُ وَجُنُودُهُ بَغْيًا وَعَدْوًا﴾ a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). ﴿حَتَّى إِذَا أَدْرَكَهُ الْغَرَقُ قَالَ آمَنْتُ أَنَّهُ﴾ i.e. بِأَنَّهُ ("in that it is"); and in one reading with kasra [إِنَّهُ], as a fresh start (istiʾnāf), ﴿لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا الَّذِي آمَنَتْ بِهِ بَنُو إِسْرَائِيلَ وَأَنَا مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ﴾. He repeated it so that it would be accepted from him, but it was not accepted; and Gabriel stuffed the mud of the sea into his mouth, for fear that mercy might reach him, and said to him:

celaleyn:91-91.t: ﴿آلْآنَ﴾ do you believe, ﴿وَقَدْ عَصَيْتَ قَبْلُ وَكُنْتَ مِنَ الْمُفْسِدِينَ﴾ by your going astray and leading [others] astray from faith?

celaleyn:92-92.t: ﴿فَالْيَوْمَ نُنَجِّيكَ﴾ We bring you out of the sea ﴿بِبَدَنِكَ﴾ your body, in which there is no soul, ﴿لِتَكُونَ لِمَنْ خَلْفَكَ﴾ after you ﴿آيَةً﴾ a lesson, so that they recognise your servanthood and do not venture upon the like of what you did. From Ibn ʿAbbās: some of the Children of Israel doubted his death, so he was brought out for them to see him. ﴿وَإِنَّ كَثِيرًا مِنَ النَّاسِ﴾ i.e. the people of Mecca ﴿عَنْ آيَاتِنَا لَغَافِلُونَ﴾ do not take lessons from them.

celaleyn:93-93.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ بَوَّأْنَا﴾ We settled ﴿بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ مُبَوَّأَ صِدْقٍ﴾ an honourable abode, which is Syria (al-Shām) and Egypt, ﴿وَرَزَقْنَاهُمْ مِنَ الطَّيِّبَاتِ فَمَا اخْتَلَفُوا﴾ in that some believed and some disbelieved ﴿حَتَّى جَاءَهُمُ الْعِلْمُ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَقْضِي بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ فِيمَا كَانُوا فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ﴾ of the matter of religion, by saving the believers and punishing the disbelievers.

celaleyn:94-94.t: ﴿فَإِنْ كُنْتَ﴾ O Muhammad ﴿فِي شَكٍّ مِمَّا أَنْزَلْنَا إِلَيْكَ﴾ of the stories — hypothetically — ﴿فَسْأَلِ الَّذِينَ يَقْرَءُونَ الْكِتَابَ﴾ the Torah ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِكَ﴾ for it is established with them; they will tell you of its truth. He ﷺ said: "I do not doubt, and I do not ask." ﴿لَقَدْ جَاءَكَ الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّكَ فَلَا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْمُمْتَرِينَ﴾ those who doubt it.

celaleyn:95-95.t: ﴿وَلَا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ فَتَكُونَ مِنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:96-96.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ حَقَّتْ﴾ became binding ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ﴾ of punishment ﴿لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾

celaleyn:97-97.t: ﴿وَلَوْ جَاءَتْهُمْ كُلُّ آيَةٍ حَتَّى يَرَوُا الْعَذَابَ الْأَلِيمَ﴾ and then it will not benefit them.

celaleyn:98-98.t: ﴿فَلَوْلَا﴾ so why not (فَهَلَّا) ﴿كَانَتْ قَرْيَةٌ﴾ — its people are meant — ﴿آمَنَتْ﴾ before the punishment came down on it ﴿فَنَفَعَهَا إِيمَانُهَا إِلَّا﴾ but (لَكِنَّ) ﴿قَوْمَ يُونُسَ لَمَّا آمَنُوا﴾ on seeing the sign of the punishment, and did not delay until it befell [them], ﴿كَشَفْنَا عَنْهُمْ عَذَابَ الْخِزْيِ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَمَتَّعْنَاهُمْ إِلَى حِينٍ﴾ the end of their terms.

celaleyn:99-99.t: ﴿وَلَوْ شَاءَ رَبُّكَ لَآمَنَ مَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ كُلُّهُمْ جَمِيعًا أَفَأَنْتَ تُكْرِهُ النَّاسَ﴾ to what Allah has not willed from them ﴿حَتَّى يَكُونُوا مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾? No.

celaleyn:100-100.t: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ لِنَفْسٍ أَنْ تُؤْمِنَ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ﴾ by His will; ﴿وَيَجْعَلُ الرِّجْسَ﴾ the punishment ﴿عَلَى الَّذِينَ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ do not reflect on the signs of Allah.

celaleyn:101-101.t: ﴿قُلِ﴾ to the disbelievers of Mecca: ﴿انْظُرُوا مَاذَا﴾ i.e. what (الَّذِي) ﴿فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ of signs pointing to the oneness of Allah the Exalted. ﴿وَمَا تُغْنِي الْآيَاتُ وَالنُّذُرُ﴾ plural of نَذِير, i.e. the messengers, ﴿عَنْ قَوْمٍ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ in Allah's knowledge, i.e. they do not benefit them.

celaleyn:102-102.t: ﴿فَهَلْ﴾ so [meaning] not (فَمَا) ﴿يَنْتَظِرُونَ﴾ by denying you ﴿إِلَّا مِثْلَ أَيَّامِ الَّذِينَ خَلَوْا مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ of the nations, i.e. the like of their events of punishment. ﴿قُلْ فَانْتَظِرُوا﴾ that; ﴿إِنِّي مَعَكُمْ مِنَ الْمُنْتَظِرِينَ﴾.

celaleyn:103-103.t: ﴿ثُمَّ نُنَجِّي﴾ — the imperfect is for relating a past situation (ḥikāyat al-ḥāl al-māḍiya) — ﴿رُسُلَنَا وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ from the punishment. ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ [like] that saving, ﴿حَقًّا عَلَيْنَا نُنْجِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions, when the idolaters are punished.

celaleyn:104-104.t: ﴿قُلْ يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ﴾ i.e. O people of Mecca, ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ فِي شَكٍّ مِنْ دِينِي﴾ that it is the truth, ﴿فَلَا أَعْبُدُ الَّذِينَ تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. other than Him, namely the idols, because of your doubt about it, ﴿وَلَكِنْ أَعْبُدُ اللَّهَ الَّذِي يَتَوَفَّاكُمْ﴾ takes your souls; ﴿وَأُمِرْتُ أَنْ﴾ i.e. بِأَنْ ("to") ﴿أَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾.

celaleyn:105-105.t: ﴿وَ﴾ it was said to me: ﴿أَنْ أَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفًا﴾ inclining to it, ﴿وَلَا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾.

celaleyn:106-106.t: ﴿وَلَا تَدْعُ﴾ worship ﴿مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مَا لَا يَنْفَعُكَ﴾ if you worship it ﴿وَلَا يَضُرُّكَ﴾ if you do not worship it. ﴿فَإِنْ فَعَلْتَ﴾ that — hypothetically — ﴿فَإِنَّكَ إِذًا مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾.

celaleyn:107-107.t: ﴿وَإِنْ يَمْسَسْكَ﴾ afflicts you ﴿اللَّهُ بِضُرٍّ﴾ such as poverty and illness, ﴿فَلَا كَاشِفَ﴾ remover ﴿لَهُ إِلَّا هُوَ وَإِنْ يُرِدْكَ بِخَيْرٍ فَلَا رَادَّ﴾ repeller ﴿لِفَضْلِهِ﴾ which He intended for you. ﴿يُصِيبُ بِهِ﴾ i.e. with the good ﴿مَنْ يَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ وَهُوَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ﴾.

celaleyn:108-108.t: ﴿قُلْ يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ﴾ i.e. people of Mecca, ﴿قَدْ جَاءَكُمُ الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ فَمَنِ اهْتَدَى فَإِنَّمَا يَهْتَدِي لِنَفْسِهِ﴾ because the reward of his guidance is his, ﴿وَمَنْ ضَلَّ فَإِنَّمَا يَضِلُّ عَلَيْهَا﴾ because the evil consequence of his misguidance falls on it; ﴿وَمَا أَنَا عَلَيْكُمْ بِوَكِيلٍ﴾ that I should compel you to guidance.

celaleyn:109-109.t: ﴿وَاتَّبِعْ مَا يُوحَى إِلَيْكَ﴾ from your Lord ﴿وَاصْبِرْ﴾ in the call and [upon] their harm ﴿حَتَّى يَحْكُمَ اللَّهُ﴾ concerning them by His command; ﴿وَهُوَ خَيْرُ الْحَاكِمِينَ﴾ the most just of them. And he was patient until He decreed fighting against the idolaters and the jizya for the People of the Book.

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿الر﴾ Allah knows best what He means by that. ﴿تِلْكَ﴾ i.e. these ayahs ﴿آيَاتُ الْكِتَابِ﴾ the Quran — the iḍāfa (genitive construct) is in the sense of مِنْ ("of") — ﴿الْحَكِيمِ﴾ the firmly made.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿أَكَانَ لِلنَّاسِ﴾ i.e. the people of Mecca — an interrogative of disapproving denial (istifhām inkār); the preposition and its genitive noun are a ḥāl (circumstantial) from His word ﴿عَجَبًا﴾ in the accusative, the khabar (predicate) of كَانَ, and in the nominative, its ism (subject); and the khabar — and it is its ism according to the first [Translator's note: reading] — is ﴿أَنْ أَوْحَيْنَا﴾ i.e. Our revealing [Translator's note: i.e. with عَجَبٌ in the nominative as the ism, the khabar is أَنْ أَوْحَيْنَا; with عَجَبًا in the accusative as the khabar, أَنْ أَوْحَيْنَا is the ism] ﴿إِلَى رَجُلٍ مِنْهُمْ﴾ Muḥammad ﷺ, ﴿أَنْ﴾ explicative (mufassira) ﴿أَنْذِرِ﴾ warn ﴿النَّاسَ﴾ the unbelievers, of punishment, ﴿وَبَشِّرِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنَّ﴾ i.e. that ﴿لَهُمْ قَدَمَ﴾ a precedence ﴿صِدْقٍ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ i.e. a fine reward for the deeds they sent ahead? ﴿قَالَ الْكَافِرُونَ إِنَّ هَذَا﴾ Quran containing that ﴿لَسِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ clear — and in one reading [لَسَاحِرٌ], and the one referred to is the Prophet ﷺ.

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ﴾ of this world, i.e. in their measure, since there was then neither sun nor moon; had He willed, He would have created them in a twinkling, and the turning away from that is to teach His creation deliberateness. ﴿ثُمَّ اسْتَوَى عَلَى الْعَرْشِ﴾ an establishing that befits Him, ﴿يُدَبِّرُ الْأَمْرَ﴾ among the creatures. ﴿مَا مِنْ﴾ a connective [Translator's note: i.e. redundant] (ṣila) ﴿شَفِيعٍ﴾ to intercede for anyone ﴿إِلَّا مِنْ بَعْدِ إِذْنِهِ﴾ — a rebuttal of their saying that the idols intercede for them. ﴿ذَلِكُمُ﴾ the Creator, the Disposer, is ﴿اللَّهُ رَبُّكُمْ فَاعْبُدُوهُ﴾ affirm His oneness. ﴿أَفَلَا تَذَّكَّرُونَ﴾ with assimilation (idghām) of the tāʾ of the original form into the dhāl [تَذَكَّرُونَ]?

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿إِلَيْهِ﴾ the Exalted ﴿مَرْجِعُكُمْ جَمِيعًا وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقًّا﴾ two maṣdars (verbal nouns) in the accusative by their implied (muqaddar) verb. ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ with kasra, as a new start (istiʾnāf), and with fatḥa on the implied lām [Translator's note: i.e. "because He …"], ﴿يَبْدَؤُا الْخَلْقَ﴾ i.e. originated it by bringing it into being, ﴿ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ﴾ by the resurrection, ﴿لِيَجْزِيَ﴾ reward ﴿الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ بِالْقِسْطِ وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَهُمْ شَرَابٌ مِنْ حَمِيمٍ﴾ water that has reached the utmost of heat, ﴿وَعَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾ painful, ﴿بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْفُرُونَ﴾ i.e. because of their unbelief.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ الشَّمْسَ ضِيَاءً﴾ possessing radiance, i.e. light, ﴿وَالْقَمَرَ نُورًا وَقَدَّرَهُ﴾ in respect of its course ﴿مَنَازِلَ﴾ twenty-eight stations in twenty-eight nights of every month, and it is hidden for two nights if the month is thirty days, or one night if it is twenty-nine days, ﴿لِتَعْلَمُوا﴾ by that ﴿عَدَدَ السِّنِينَ وَالْحِسَابَ مَا خَلَقَ اللَّهُ ذَلِكَ﴾ what has been mentioned ﴿إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ﴾ not in vain — exalted is He above that. ﴿يُفَصِّلُ﴾ with yāʾ and with nūn: makes clear ﴿الْآيَاتِ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ who reflect.

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿إِنَّ فِي اخْتِلَافِ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ﴾ by going and coming, increasing and decreasing, ﴿وَمَا خَلَقَ اللَّهُ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ﴾ of angels, sun, moon, stars and other things ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ in the earth, of animals, mountains, seas, rivers, trees and other things, ﴿لَآيَاتٍ﴾ indications of His power, Exalted is He, ﴿لِقَوْمٍ يَتَّقُونَ﴾ and so believe. He singled them out for mention because they are the ones who benefit from them.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ لَا يَرْجُونَ لِقَاءَنَا﴾ by the resurrection ﴿وَرَضُوا بِالْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا﴾ in place of the Hereafter, because of their denial of it, ﴿وَاطْمَأَنُّوا بِهَا﴾ rest content in it, ﴿وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ عَنْ آيَاتِنَا﴾ the proofs of Our oneness ﴿غَافِلُونَ﴾ neglecting to reflect on them,

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿أُولَئِكَ مَأْوَاهُمُ النَّارُ بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ﴾ of idolatry and acts of disobedience.

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ يَهْدِيهِمْ﴾ guides them ﴿رَبُّهُمْ بِإِيمَانِهِمْ﴾ in Him, by giving them a light by which they are guided on the Day of Resurrection; ﴿تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهِمُ الْأَنْهَارُ فِي جَنَّاتِ النَّعِيمِ﴾

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿دَعْوَاهُمْ فِيهَا﴾ their request for what they desire in Paradise is that they say: ﴿سُبْحَانَكَ اللَّهُمَّ﴾ i.e. O Allah — and lo, what they requested is before them; ﴿وَتَحِيَّتُهُمْ﴾ among themselves ﴿فِيهَا سَلَامٌ وَآخِرُ دَعْوَاهُمْ أَنِ﴾ explicative (mufassira) ﴿الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾. And there was revealed, when the idolaters sought to hasten the punishment:

daas-irab:25-26.t: ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾: the wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya), and the Name of Majesty is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive. ﴿يَدْعُوا﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the wāw because of heaviness; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the clause is the khabar (predicate). ﴿إِلى دارِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) يدعو. ﴿السَّلامِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَيَهْدِي﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb, nominative with an implied ḍamma on the yāʾ because of heaviness; the fāʿil is latent, and the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined). ﴿مَنْ﴾: a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿يَشاءُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿إِلى صِراطٍ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يدعو [Translator's note: so in the source; the attachment is evidently to يهدي]. ﴿مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾: an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾: the lām is a preposition, and the relative noun is in the position of the genitive by it; the two are attached to the fronted predicate. ﴿أَحْسَنُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿الْحُسْنى﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative with an implied ḍamma on the alif because of impossibility (al-taʿadhdhur); al-ḥusnā is Paradise. ﴿وَزِيادَةٌ﴾: maʿṭūf on الحسنى; the clause is resumptive. The "increase" (al-ziyāda) is the beholding of the Face of Allah the Magnificent. ﴿وَلا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction and lā is negating. ﴿يَرْهَقُ وُجُوهَهُمْ قَتَرٌ﴾: an imperfect verb, its fronted object and its postponed fāʿil; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَلا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction and lā is negating. ﴿ذِلَّةٌ﴾: maʿṭūf on قتر. ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾: a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ; the kāf is for address. ﴿أَصْحابُ﴾: khabar; the clause is resumptive. ﴿الْجَنَّةِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿هُمْ﴾: mubtadaʾ. ﴿فِيها﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to خالدون. ﴿خالِدُونَ﴾: khabar, nominative with the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:27-30.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the relative noun is a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿كَسَبُوا السَّيِّئاتِ﴾: a past verb; the wāw is its fāʿil (agent), and السيئات is its object, accusative (manṣūb) with the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿جَزاءُ﴾: a second mubtadaʾ. ﴿سَيِّئَةٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿بِمِثْلِها﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate); this clause is the khabar of الذين. ﴿وَتَرْهَقُهُمْ ذِلَّةٌ﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and an imperfect verb, its fronted object and its postponed fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿ما﴾: negating. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾: the Name of Majesty is in the position of the genitive by مِن; the two are attached to عاصم. ﴿مِنَ﴾: redundant (zāʾida). ﴿عاصِمٍ﴾: mubtadaʾ, genitive in form and nominative in position. ﴿كَأَنَّما﴾: the restraining particle (kāffa) and the restrained particle (makfūfa). ﴿أُغْشِيَتْ وُجُوهُهُمْ قِطَعاً﴾: a passive past verb, its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿مِنَ اللَّيْلِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an adjective of قطعا. ﴿مُظْلِماً﴾: a second adjective; the clause is resumptive. ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾: the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ; the kāf is for address. ﴿أَصْحابُ﴾: khabar. ﴿النَّارِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿هُمْ﴾: mubtadaʾ. ﴿فِيها﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to خالدون. ﴿خالِدُونَ﴾: khabar, nominative (marfūʿ) with the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَيَوْمَ﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and يوم is an adverb of time attached to an omitted verb. ﴿نَحْشُرُهُمْ﴾: an imperfect verb and its object; the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿جَمِيعاً﴾: ḥāl. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾: a conjunction. ﴿نَقُولُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined). ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun made genitive by the lām; the two are attached to نقول. ﴿أَشْرَكُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿مَكانَكُمْ﴾: a verbal noun of command (ism fiʿl amr). ﴿أَنْتُمْ﴾: tawkīd (emphasis) of the latent pronoun in مكانكم. ﴿وَشُرَكاؤُكُمْ﴾: conjoined to أنتم. ﴿فَزَيَّلْنا﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ﴾: an adverb of time attached to زيلنا [Translator's note: so in the source; بين is normally parsed as an adverb of place]; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَقالَ شُرَكاؤُهُمْ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿ما﴾: negating. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾: kāna and its noun; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿إِيَّانا﴾: a fronted mafʿūl bihi of تعبدون. ﴿تَعْبُدُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar. ﴿فَكَفى﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied fatḥa on the alif because of impossibility. ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾: the bāʾ is redundant, and the Name of Majesty is genitive in form and nominative in position as fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿شَهِيداً﴾: tamyīz (specification). ﴿بَيْنَنا﴾: an adverb of place attached to شهيد; نا is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَبَيْنَكُمْ﴾: conjoined to بيننا. ﴿إِنْ﴾: lightened from إنّ and inoperative (muhmala). ﴿كُنَّا﴾: kāna, and نا is its noun; the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿عَنْ عِبادَتِكُمْ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to غافلين. ﴿لَغافِلِينَ﴾: the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa), and the khabar, accusative with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural. ﴿هُنالِكَ﴾: a demonstrative, an adverb of place; the lām is for distance and the kāf is for address. ﴿تَبْلُوا﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative with an implied ḍamma on the wāw because of heaviness. ﴿كُلُّ﴾: fāʿil. ﴿نَفْسٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿ما﴾: a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi. ﴿أَسْلَفَتْ﴾: a past verb; the tāʾ is for the feminine and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَرُدُّوا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and a passive past verb; the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿إِلَى اللَّهِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ردوا. ﴿مَوْلاهُمُ﴾: badal (substitute) of the Name of Majesty; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿الْحَقِّ﴾: badal. ﴿وَضَلَّ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa. ﴿عَنْهُمْ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ضل. ﴿ما﴾: a relative noun, fāʿil. ﴿كانُوا﴾: kāna and its noun; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿يَفْتَرُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar.

daas-irab:31-32.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive. ﴿مَنْ﴾: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿يَرْزُقُكُمْ﴾: an imperfect verb and its object; the fāʿil is latent, and the clause is the khabar (predicate). ﴿مِنَ السَّماءِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) يرزقكم. ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾: maʿṭūf (conjoined) on السماء. ﴿أم﴾: a conjunction. ﴿مَنْ﴾: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ; the clause is conjoined. ﴿يَمْلِكُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar. ﴿السَّمْعَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَالْأَبْصارَ﴾: maʿṭūf on السمع. ﴿وَمَنْ يُخْرِجُ الْحَيَّ﴾: conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿مِنَ الْمَيِّتِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يخرج. ﴿وَيُخْرِجُ الْمَيِّتَ مِنَ الْحَيِّ﴾: conjoined to what precedes it, and its i'rab is like it. ﴿وَمَنْ﴾: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ. ﴿يُدَبِّرُ الْأَمْرَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its object; the fāʿil is latent, and the clause is the khabar; and the clause of من .. 0 is conjoined [Translator's note: "من.. 0" is reproduced as it stands in the source text]. ﴿فَسَيَقُولُونَ﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, the sīn is for the future, and an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil, and the clause is resumptive. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾: the Name of Majesty is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هو الله"; the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿فَقُلْ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَفَلا﴾: the hamza is for interrogation, the fāʾ is a conjunction, and lā is negating. ﴿تَتَّقُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil, and the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿فَذلِكُمُ﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ; the lām is for distance and the kāf is for address. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾: the Name of Majesty is the khabar; the clause is resumptive. ﴿رَبُّكُمُ﴾: badal (substitute); the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿الْحَقُّ﴾: badal, or an adjective (ṣifa) of رب. ﴿فَماذا﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, mā is negating, and dhā is redundant (zāʾida). ﴿بَعْدَ﴾: an adverb of time attached to the omitted khabar. ﴿الْحَقُّ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿الضَّلالُ﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَأَنَّى﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and أنّى is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿تُصْرَفُونَ﴾: a passive imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:33-35.t: ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾: the kāf is a preposition, and a demonstrative in the position of the genitive by the kāf; the two are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿حَقَّتْ كَلِمَةُ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the tāʾ is for the feminine. ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿عَلَى الَّذِينَ﴾: the relative noun is in the position of the genitive; the two are attached to حقت. ﴿فَسَقُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿أَنَّهُمْ﴾: anna and its noun; anna and what follows it are in the position of the genitive by an omitted preposition, i.e. "after their faith" (بعد إيمانهم) [Translator's note: so in the source]. ﴿لا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾: lā is negating, and an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) [Translator's note: so in the source; the verb is active and the wāw is its fāʿil], and the clause is the khabar (predicate). ﴿قُلْ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive. ﴿هَلْ﴾: an interrogative particle. ﴿مِنْ شُرَكائِكُمْ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar; the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مِنْ﴾ [Translator's note: so written in the source; the Quranic word is مَنْ]: a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿يَبْدَؤُا الْخَلْقَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its object; the fāʿil is latent, and the clause is the ṣila. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾: a conjunction. ﴿يُعِيدُهُ﴾: maʿṭūf (conjoined) on يبدأ; the hāʾ is its object. ﴿قُلْ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾: the Name of Majesty is a mubtadaʾ; the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿يَبْدَؤُا﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar. ﴿الْخَلْقَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ﴾: conjoined to what preceded. ﴿فَأَنَّى﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and أنّى is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿تُؤْفَكُونَ﴾: a passive imperfect verb; the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil, and the clause is resumptive. ﴿قُلْ هَلْ مِنْ شُرَكائِكُمْ مَنْ﴾: their i'rab has preceded shortly before. ﴿يَهْدِي﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the yāʾ because of heaviness; the fāʿil is latent. ﴿إِلَى الْحَقِّ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يهدي; the clause is the khabar of من, and the speech is the object of the saying. ﴿قُلْ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾: the Name of Majesty is a mubtadaʾ; the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿يَهْدِي﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative with an implied ḍamma on the yāʾ because of heaviness. ﴿لِلْحَقِّ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يهدي. ﴿أَفَمَنْ﴾: the hamza is for interrogation, the fāʾ is resumptive, and مَن is a relative noun, mubtadaʾ; the clause is resumptive. ﴿يَهْدِي﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿إِلَى الْحَقِّ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يهدي. ﴿أَحَقُّ﴾: the khabar of من. ﴿أَنْ﴾: a subjunctive-governing particle. ﴿يُتَّبَعَ﴾: a passive imperfect verb whose nāʾib fāʿil is latent; the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of the genitive by an omitted preposition. ﴿أم﴾: a conjunction. ﴿مِنْ﴾ [Translator's note: so written in the source; the Quranic word is مَنْ]: a relative noun, mubtadaʾ. ﴿لا﴾: negating. ﴿يَهْدِي﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative with an implied ḍamma on the yāʾ because of heaviness; the fāʿil is latent, and the clause is the ṣila. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿أَنْ﴾: subjunctive-governing. ﴿يَهْدِي﴾: a passive imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) with an implied fatḥa on the alif because of impossibility; the nāʾib fāʿil is latent, and the interpreted maṣdar from an and what follows it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ [Translator's note: the source analyses the word as the passive يُهْدَى, though it prints the Quranic word as ﴿يَهْدِي﴾]. ﴿فَما﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and mā is interrogative, in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ; the clause is resumptive. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar. ﴿كَيْفَ﴾: an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. ﴿تَحْكُمُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil, and the clause is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the preceding clause.

daas-irab:36-38.t: ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is resumptive and mā is negating. ﴿يَتَّبِعُ أَكْثَرُهُمْ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿ظَنًّا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿إِنَّ الظَّنَّ﴾: inna and its noun. ﴿لا﴾: negating. ﴿يُغْنِي﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the yāʾ because of heaviness; the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the clause is the khabar (predicate). ﴿مِنَ الْحَقِّ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿شَيْئاً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾: inna, and the Name of Majesty is its noun. ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾: khabar; the clause is resumptive. ﴿بِما﴾: the relative noun is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ; the two are attached to عليم. ﴿يَفْعَلُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is resumptive and mā is negating. ﴿كانَ هذَا﴾: kāna, and a demonstrative as its noun; the hāʾ [Translator's note: the source writes «الها»] is for drawing attention (tanbīh), and the clause is resumptive. ﴿الْقُرْآنُ﴾: badal (substitute). ﴿أَنْ﴾: subjunctive-governing. ﴿يُفْتَرى﴾: a passive imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an, the sign of its accusative being an implied fatḥa on the alif because of impossibility; the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent, and the clause is the khabar of kāna. ﴿مِنْ دُونِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يفترى. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾: the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَلكِنْ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction and lākin is a particle of rectification (istidrāk). ﴿تَصْدِيقَ﴾: the khabar of an omitted kāna whose noun is omitted, the implied form being "كان تصديق"; or a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined). ﴿الَّذِي﴾: the relative noun is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بَيْنَ﴾: an adverb of place attached to an omitted ṣila. ﴿يَدَيْهِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) with the yāʾ because it is a dual. ﴿وَتَفْصِيلَ﴾: maʿṭūf on تصديق. ﴿الْكِتابِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لا﴾: the lā of generic negation. ﴿رَيْبَ﴾: the noun of lā. ﴿فِيهِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar. ﴿مِنْ رَبِّ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿الْعالَمِينَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive with the yāʾ because it is treated as a sound masculine plural. ﴿أم﴾: a conjunction. ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿افْتَراهُ﴾: a past verb and its object; the fāʿil is latent, and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿قُلْ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَأْتُوا﴾: the fāʾ of eloquence (al-faṣīḥa), and an imperative verb and its fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. ﴿بِسُورَةٍ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أتوا. ﴿مِثْلِهِ﴾: an adjective of سورة; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَادْعُوا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperative verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿مَنِ﴾: a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi. ﴿اسْتَطَعْتُمْ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿مِنْ دُونِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾: the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِنْ﴾: conditional. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾: kāna and its noun; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿صادِقِينَ﴾: khabar, accusative with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

daas-irab:39-41.t: ﴿بَلْ﴾: a particle of digression (iḍrāb) and conjunction. ﴿كَذَّبُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined). ﴿بِما﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition and mā is relative; the two are attached to (mutaʿalliq) كذبوا. ﴿لَمْ﴾: jussive-governing. ﴿يُحِيطُوا﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿بِعِلْمِهِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يحيطوا. ﴿وَلَمَّا﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) and lammā is a jussive-governing particle. ﴿يَأْتِهِمْ﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive by the dropping of the weak letter; the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿تَأْوِيلُهُ﴾: fāʿil, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾: the kāf is a preposition, and the demonstrative is in the position of the genitive; the two are attached to an adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿كَذَّبَ الَّذِينَ﴾: a past verb, and a relative noun as fāʿil. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted ṣila of the relative. ﴿فَانْظُرْ﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿كَيْفَ﴾: an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as a fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿كانَ عاقِبَةُ﴾: kāna and its noun. ﴿الظَّالِمِينَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause is the mafʿūl bihi of انظر. ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ﴾: the wāw is resumptive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to a fronted khabar. ﴿مَنْ﴾: a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive. ﴿يُؤْمِنُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿بِهِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يؤمن; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ لا يُؤْمِنُ بِهِ﴾: its i'rab is like the preceding one. ﴿وَرَبُّكَ﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and a mubtadaʾ; the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَعْلَمُ﴾: khabar; the clause is resumptive. ﴿بِالْمُفْسِدِينَ﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition and المفسدين a genitive noun; the two are attached to أعلم. ﴿وَإِنْ﴾: the wāw is resumptive and in is conditional. ﴿كَذَّبُوكَ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), and it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). ﴿فَقُلْ﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis, and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿لِي﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted fronted khabar. ﴿عَمَلِي﴾: mubtadaʾ, nominative (marfūʿ) with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the letter before the yāʾ of the first person, its appearance prevented by the place being occupied with the vowel suited to it; the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi, and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَلَكُمْ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted fronted khabar. ﴿عَمَلُكُمْ﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ; the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿أَنْتُمْ﴾: mubtadaʾ. ﴿بَرِيئُونَ﴾: khabar, nominative with the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause is resumptive. ﴿مِمَّا﴾: composed of the preposition مِن and the relative mā; the two are attached to بريئون. ﴿أَعْمَلُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَأَنَا بَرِيءٌ مِمَّا﴾: conjoined to what preceded, and its i'rab is like it. ﴿تَعْمَلُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila.

daas-irab:42-44.t: ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ﴾: the wāw is resumptive; preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿مَنْ﴾: the relative noun is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive. ﴿يَسْتَمِعُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿إِلَيْكَ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يستمعون. ﴿أَفَأَنْتَ﴾: the hamza is for interrogation, the fāʾ is resumptive, and a mubtadaʾ; the clause is resumptive. ﴿تُسْمِعُ﴾: an imperfect verb, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿الصُّمَّ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the khabar. ﴿وَلَوْ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction and law is a non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿كانُوا﴾: kāna and its noun; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), and the speech is maʿṭūf (conjoined) on what preceded. ﴿لا﴾: negating. ﴿يَعْقِلُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar. ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ﴾: their i'rab has preceded shortly before. ﴿يَنْظُرُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿إِلَيْكَ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ينظر. ﴿أَفَأَنْتَ تَهْدِي الْعُمْيَ وَلَوْ كانُوا لا يُبْصِرُونَ﴾: see the i'rab of the preceding verse. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾: inna, and the Name of Majesty is its noun; the clause is resumptive. ﴿لا﴾: negating. ﴿يَظْلِمُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar. ﴿النَّاسَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿شَيْئاً﴾: a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (nāʾib mafʿūl muṭlaq, standing in for the absolute object). ﴿وَلكِنَّ النَّاسَ﴾: lākinna and its noun; the clause is conjoined. ﴿أَنْفُسَهُمْ﴾: a fronted mafʿūl bihi; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿يَظْلِمُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar of lākinna.

daas-irab:45-46.t: ﴿وَيَوْمَ﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and يوم is an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being "واذكر" ("and remember"); the clause is resumptive. ﴿يَحْشُرُهُمْ﴾: an imperfect verb and its object; the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the clause is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿كَأَنْ﴾: lightened from كأنّ; its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿لَمْ يَلْبَثُوا﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lam through the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar (predicate). ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿ساعَةً﴾: an adverb of time attached to يلبثوا. ﴿مِنَ النَّهارِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective of ساعة. ﴿يَتَعارَفُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ﴾: an adverb of place attached to يتعارفون. ﴿قَدْ﴾: a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿خَسِرَ الَّذِينَ﴾: a past verb, and the relative noun is its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿كَذَّبُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿بِلِقاءِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to كذبوا. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾: the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction and mā is negating. ﴿كانُوا﴾: kāna and its noun; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined). ﴿مُهْتَدِينَ﴾: the khabar of كانوا. ﴿وَإِمَّا﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and إمّا is composed of the conditional in and the redundant (zāʾida) mā. ﴿نُرِيَنَّكَ﴾: an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis; it is in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the clause of the protasis is initial (ibtidāʾiyya); the fāʿil is latent, and the kāf is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿بَعْضَ﴾: second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الَّذِي﴾: a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿نَعِدُهُمْ﴾: an imperfect verb and its object; the fāʿil is latent, and the clause is the ṣila. ﴿أَوْ﴾: a conjunction. ﴿نَتَوَفَّيَنَّكَ﴾: an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis; its fāʿil is latent and the kāf is its object; the clause is conjoined. ﴿فَإِلَيْنا﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis; preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted fronted khabar. ﴿مَرْجِعُهُمْ﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi, and the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿ثُمَّ﴾: a conjunction. ﴿اللَّهُ شَهِيدٌ﴾: the Name of Majesty is a mubtadaʾ and شهيد the khabar; the clause is conjoined. ﴿عَلى ما﴾: the relative noun is in the position of the genitive by على, and the two are attached to شهيد. ﴿يَفْعَلُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila.

daas-irab:47-49.t: ﴿وَلِكُلِّ﴾: the wāw is resumptive; preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿أُمَّةٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿رَسُولٌ﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَإِذا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and إذا is an adverb containing the sense of condition. ﴿جاءَ رَسُولُهُمْ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi, and the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿قُضِيَ﴾: a passive past verb whose nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ﴾: an adverb of place attached to قضي; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بِالْقِسْطِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَهُمْ﴾: the wāw is circumstantial and هم is a mubtadaʾ; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿لا﴾: negating. ﴿يُظْلَمُونَ﴾: a passive imperfect verb; the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar. ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil, and the clause is resumptive. ﴿مَتى﴾: an interrogative noun of time, attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿هذَا﴾: the hāʾ [Translator's note: the source writes «الها»] is for drawing attention (tanbīh), and ذا is a demonstrative, a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿الْوَعْدُ﴾: badal (substitute) of the demonstrative. ﴿إِنْ﴾: conditional. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾: kāna and its noun; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿صادِقِينَ﴾: the khabar of كنتم, accusative (manṣūb) with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it. ﴿قُلْ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿لا﴾: negating. ﴿أَمْلِكُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿لِنَفْسِي﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أملك; the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿ضَرًّا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَلا نَفْعاً﴾: maʿṭūf (conjoined) on ضرا. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of exception. ﴿ما﴾: a relative noun in the position of the accusative, excepted (mustathnā) by illā. ﴿شاءَ اللَّهُ﴾: a past verb, and the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿لِكُلِّ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿أُمَّةٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَجَلٌ﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَإِذا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and إذا is an adverb containing the sense of condition. ﴿جاءَ أَجَلُهُمْ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil;
