Abū Jaʿfar said: Aḥmad ibn Shuʿayb read to me [Translator's note: the source has «قرأ عليّ أحمد بن شعيب بن علي بن الحسين بن حريث», which merges two links of the chain; elsewhere the chain runs Aḥmad ibn Shuʿayb ← ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Ḥurayth]: he said: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn informed us, from his father, from Yazīd, that ʿIkrima narrated to him from Ibn ʿAbbās: «الر» and «حم» and «ن» are "al-Raḥmān" separated. [Yazīd said:] I narrated it to al-Aʿmash, and he said: "You have things like this and you do not tell me?" Abū Jaʿfar said: We mentioned in Sūrat al-Baqara that Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah's mercy be upon him, said: the meaning of «الر» is "I am Allah; I see" (anā llāhu arā). I saw Abū Isḥāq inclining towards this view, because Sībawayh reported the like of it from the Arabs, and recited: [al-Rajaz] 195-
بالخير خيرات وإن شرّا فا ... ولا أريد الشّرّ إلّا أن تا
("With good, good things; and if evil, then [evil]; and I do not want evil unless you [will].")
Sībawayh said: He means "if evil, then evil; and I do not want evil unless you will (tashāʾ)". Al-Ḥasan and ʿIkrima said: «الر» is an oath. Saʿīd related from Qatāda: «الر» is the name of the sūra; he said: and so is every spelled-out letter group in the Qur'an. Mujāhid said: They are the openings of the sūras. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: It is a call to attention, and so are the letters of the alphabet [at the openings]. (تِلْكَ آياتُ الْكِتابِ الْحَكِيمِ): mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), i.e. those that have been mentioned are the verses of the wise Book; if you wish, the implied form is "these — those are the verses of the wise Book". Abū ʿUbayda said: «الحكيم» means "made firm" (al-muḥkam).
(أَكانَ لِلنَّاسِ عَجَباً أَنْ أَوْحَيْنا إِلى رَجُلٍ مِنْهُمْ أَنْ أَنْذِرِ النَّاسَ وَبَشِّرِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنَّ لَهُمْ قَدَمَ صِدْقٍ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ قالَ الْكافِرُونَ إِنَّ هذا لَساحِرٌ مُبِينٌ) (2). (أَكانَ لِلنَّاسِ عَجَباً): the khabar of kāna, and its ism is (أَنْ أَوْحَيْنا). In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd]: «أكان للناس عجب», as the ism of kāna, the khabar being (أَنْ أَوْحَيْنا). (أَنْ أَنْذِرِ النَّاسَ): in the position of the accusative, i.e. «بأن أنذر الناس» ("that you warn mankind"), and likewise (أَنَّ لَهُمْ قَدَمَ صِدْقٍ). «إنّ لهم قدم صدق» [with kasra] is also permissible, meaning "say: …".

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: (دَعْواهُمْ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. their supplication. (فِيها سُبْحانَكَ): a maṣdar (verbal noun). (وَتَحِيَّتُهُمْ فِيها سَلامٌ): mubtadaʾ and khabar (predicate), and likewise (وَآخِرُ دَعْواهُمْ أَنِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ). Abū ʿUbayd reported only the lightened «أن» with the nominative after it. He said: We think they chose this and distinguished it from His words, Majestic and Mighty, (أَنَّ لَعْنَتَ اللَّهِ) and (أَنَّ غَضَبَ اللَّهِ) [al-Nūr: 7, 9] [Translator's note: the source gives only «[النور: 9]»], because they intended to quote what is said: «الحمد لله». Abū Jaʿfar said: The position of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh is that this «أن» is lightened from the heavy one, and the meaning is «أنه الحمد لله» ("that [the fact is]: praise be to Allah"). Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: «أن الحمد لله» [with the accusative, al-ḥamda] is also permissible, making it govern when light as it governs when heavy; but the nominative is more in line with analogy, because it resembles the verb only in form, not in meaning, so when it falls short of the verb it does not govern as the verb does; whoever uses the accusative likens it to the verb when something is dropped from it. Abū Jaʿfar said: Abū Ḥātim reported that Bilāl ibn Abī Burda read (وَآخِرُ دَعْواهُمْ أَنِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ) [Translator's note: i.e. anna l-ḥamda, with the heavy anna and the accusative; the source prints the standard vowelling].

nahhas-irab:11-11.t:
(وَلَوْ يُعَجِّلُ اللَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ الشَّرَّ اسْتِعْجالَهُمْ بِالْخَيْرِ لَقُضِيَ إِلَيْهِمْ أَجَلُهُمْ): it is said that its meaning is: if Allah hastened punishment for people as they seek to hasten reward and good, and punished them, they would die, because they were created in this world with a weak constitution; and they will not be so on the Day of Resurrection, because on the Day of Resurrection they will be created for permanence. Abū Jaʿfar said: We have mentioned a view other than this. «استعجالهم», according to the view of al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ, means «كاستعجالهم» ("like their seeking to hasten"); then the kāf was dropped and it was put in the accusative. Al-Farrāʾ said: As you say «ضربت زيدا ضربك», i.e. "like your striking". As for the position of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh — and it is the right one — the implied form in it is "if Allah hastened evil for people with a hastening like their seeking to hasten good"; then «تعجيلا» was omitted and its qualifier was put in its place, then its qualifier was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi was put in its place, like (وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ). Sībawayh reported «زيد شرب الإبل» ("Zayd drinks the drinking of camels"). If what al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ said were permissible, «زيد الأسد» would be permissible in the sense of "like the lion"; this is very clear.
Abū Isḥāq said: It is also read (لَقُضِيَ إِلَيْهِمْ أَجَلُهُمْ) [Translator's note: i.e. la-qaḍā ilayhim ajalahum, active; the source prints the standard vowelling], which is the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir al-Shāmī; it is a good reading because it is connected with His words, Majestic and Mighty, (وَلَوْ يُعَجِّلُ اللَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ الشَّرَّ). Al-Akhfash said: (فَنَذَرُ الَّذِينَ لا يَرْجُونَ لِقاءَنا) is a new beginning. He said: (يَعْمَهُونَ) means they wander in confusion.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t:
(وَإِذا مَسَّ الْإِنْسانَ الضُّرُّ دَعانا لِجَنْبِهِ): in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (أَوْ قاعِداً): conjoined to the position; the implied form is "he calls on Us lying down, or sitting, or standing". (كَأَنْ لَمْ يَدْعُنا): al-Akhfash said: It is the heavy «أنّ», lightened, as [the poet] said: [al-Khafīf] 197-
وي كأن من يكن له نشب يحبب ... ومن يفتقر يعش عيش ضرّ
("Ah! It seems that whoever has wealth is loved, and whoever becomes poor lives a life of hardship.")

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: (ثُمَّ جَعَلْناكُمْ خَلائِفَ): two objects. (لِنَنْظُرَ): accusative by the lām of kay (purpose).

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: (وَإِذا تُتْلى عَلَيْهِمْ آياتُنا): the noun of a verb whose agent is not named [i.e. nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)]. Abū Isḥāq said: (بَيِّناتٍ) is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: (قُلْ لَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ ما تَلَوْتُهُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَلا أَدْراكُمْ بِهِ): i.e. had Allah willed, He would not have sent me to you so that I recited the Qur'an to you, nor would He have made you know it, i.e. the Qur'an. Abū Ḥātim said: I heard al-Aṣmaʿī say: I asked Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ about al-Ḥasan's reading «ولا أدرأتكم به» — does it have a valid construction? He said: No. Abū ʿUbayd said: Al-Ḥasan's reading «ولا أدرأتكم به» has no valid construction except as a mistake. The meaning of Abū ʿUbayd's saying "as a mistake", if Allah wills, is that one says darītu, i.e. I knew, and adraytu someone else [I made him know]; and one says daraʾtu, i.e. I repelled; so a confusion occurs between darītu, adraytu and daraʾtu. Abū Ḥātim said: Al-Ḥasan means — so I reckon — «ولا أدريتكم به», and he replaced the yāʾ with an alif according to the dialect of Banū al-Ḥārith ibn Kaʿb, because they replace yāʾ with alif when what precedes it has fatḥa, as in (إِنْ هذانِ لَساحِرانِ) [Ṭāhā: 63]. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a mistake, because the transmission from al-Ḥasan is «ولا أدرأتكم به» with hamza, while Abū Ḥātim spoke of it as being without hamza. It may be from daraʾtu, when I repelled, i.e. "nor would I have commanded you to repel and abandon disbelief in the Qur'an". (فَقَدْ لَبِثْتُ فِيكُمْ عُمُراً مِنْ قَبْلِهِ): there is an omission in the sentence; the implied form is "I have stayed among you a lifetime before it, while you knew me for truthfulness and trustworthiness, not reading or writing; then I came to you with the miracles". (أَفَلا تَعْقِلُونَ) that this could only be from Allah, Majestic and Mighty?

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: (وَما كانَ النَّاسُ إِلَّا أُمَّةً واحِدَةً): the ism of «كان» and its khabar (predicate). (وَلَوْلا كَلِمَةٌ): nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). (سَبَقَتْ مِنْ رَبِّكَ): in the position of the naʿt (adjective).

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: (فَانْتَظِرُوا إِنِّي مَعَكُمْ مِنَ الْمُنْتَظِرِينَ): the original is «أنني» [i.e. innanī]; the nūn was dropped. The meaning is: "a waiter among those who wait".

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: (وَإِذا أَذَقْنَا النَّاسَ رَحْمَةً): the answer of «إذا», according to the view of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, is (إِذا لَهُمْ مَكْرٌ فِي آياتِنا), the implied sense being "they plotted". Mujāhid said: «إذا لهم مكر في آياتنا» means mockery and denial. (قُلِ اللَّهُ أَسْرَعُ): mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). (مَكْراً): by way of clarification (bayān) [i.e. tamyīz (specification)].

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: (هُوَ الَّذِي يُسَيِّرُكُمْ): mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). «يسيّركم» carries the sense of intensity/frequency, while «يسيركم» [yusīrukum] is for little and much. Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ read «هو الذي ينشركم» ("it is He who spreads you"), and it is the known reading of al-Ḥasan. «يسيّركم» fits better with His words, Majestic and Mighty, (وَجَرَيْنَ بِهِمْ بِرِيحٍ طَيِّبَةٍ). (والْفُلْكِ) is masculine and feminine, and it is singular and also the plural of «فلك», as one says «وثن» and «وثن» [wathan and wuthn]. (جاءَتْها): the hāʾ refers back to the ships, and it may also refer back to the good wind. (رِيحٌ عاصِفٌ).

nahhas-irab:23-23.t: (إِنَّما بَغْيُكُمْ): nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is (مَتاعَ الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا) [Translator's note: i.e. matāʿu in the nominative; the source prints the accusative vowelling of Ḥafṣ]. Its khabar may also be (عَلى أَنْفُسِكُمْ), and you imply a mubtadaʾ, i.e. "that is the enjoyment of the life of this world" or "it is the enjoyment of the life of this world". There is a subtle difference between the two meanings. If you put «متاع» in the nominative as the khabar of «بغيكم», the meaning is "the transgression of some of you against others is only …", like (فَسَلِّمُوا عَلى أَنْفُسِكُمْ) [al-Nūr: 61], and likewise (لَقَدْ جاءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ مِنْ أَنْفُسِكُمْ) [al-Tawba: 128]. If the khabar is «على أنفسكم», the meaning is "your corruption only comes back upon you", like (وَإِنْ أَسَأْتُمْ فَلَها) [al-Isrāʾ: 7]. Ibn Abī Isḥāq read (مَتاعَ الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا) in the accusative, as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "you enjoy the enjoyment of the life of this world".

nahhas-irab:24-24.t: (إِنَّما مَثَلُ الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا): a mubtadaʾ (subject). (كَماءٍ): its khabar (predicate), and the kāf is in the position of the nominative. (أَنْزَلْناهُ مِنَ السَّماءِ): a naʿt (adjective) for «ماء». (فَاخْتَلَطَ بِهِ نَباتُ الْأَرْضِ): conjoined. (حَتَّى إِذا أَخَذَتِ الْأَرْضُ زُخْرُفَها وَازَّيَّنَتْ): the original is «تزيّنت»; the tāʾ was assimilated into the zāy and the connecting alif (alif al-waṣl) was brought, because the assimilated letter stands for two letters, the first of which is quiescent. Al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿraj and Abū al-ʿĀliya read (وَازَّيَّنَتْ) [Translator's note: i.e. wa-azyanat; the source prints the standard vowelling], i.e. it brought forth adornment; the verb is given in its original form — had it been made weak, it would be «أزانت». ʿAwf al-Aʿrābī said: Our elders read «وازيانّت», whose pattern is like «واسوادّت». In the transmission of al-Muqaddamī: «وازّاينت», whose original is «تزاينت», on the pattern tafāʿalat, then assimilated. (وَظَنَّ أَهْلُها أَنَّهُمْ قادِرُونَ عَلَيْها): Abū Isḥāq said: The meaning is "able to benefit from it". (أَتاها أَمْرُنا لَيْلًا أَوْ نَهاراً): two adverbials (ẓarf). (فَجَعَلْناها حَصِيداً): two objects.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: (لِلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا الْحُسْنى): in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). (وَزِيادَةٌ): conjoined to it. Abū Jaʿfar said: We have mentioned the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ that the "increase" is looking upon Allah the Exalted. It is also said: the increase is that a good deed is multiplied tenfold and more than that. Al-Ḥasan read (وَلا يَرْهَقُ وُجُوهَهُمْ قَتَرٌ وَلا ذِلَّةٌ) [Translator's note: i.e. qatrun, with sukūn; the source prints the standard vowelling]. «القتر», «القتر» and «القترة» [qatar, qatr and qatara] have one meaning.

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: (قِطَعاً): plural of «قطعة». (مِنَ اللَّيْلِ مُظْلِماً): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الليل»; it is unlikely to be a naʿt (adjective) for «قطع», because He did not say «مظلمة». Al-Kisāʾī read (قِطَعاً) with sukūn on the ṭāʾ [qiṭʿan]; on this reading «مظلما» is a naʿt, and it may also be a ḥāl from «الليل».

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: Al-Farrāʾ said: Some read (فزايلنا بينهم) [Translator's note: i.e. fa-zāyalnā, instead of fa-zayyalnā]. One says «لا أزايل فلانا», i.e. "I do not part from so-and-so"; but if you say «لا أزاوله», it has another meaning: "I do not try to deceive him".

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: (شَهِيداً): accusative as a tamyīz (specification). Abū Isḥāq said: It may also be accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: (ما مِنْ شَفِيعٍ): in the position of the nominative; the meaning is "there is no intercessor (إِلَّا مِنْ بَعْدِ إِذْنِهِ)".

nahhas-irab:30-30.t:
(هُنالِكَ): in the position of the accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf), i.e. at that time. (تَبْلُوا كُلُّ نَفْسٍ). The lām [in «هنالك»] is additional, given kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and the kāf is for address and has no grammatical position. Zuhayr said: [al-Ṭawīl] 198-
هنالك إن يستخبلوا المال يخبلوا ... وإن يسألوا يعطوا وإن ييسروا يغلوا
("There, if they are asked to lend property, they lend it; if they are asked, they give; and if they play at the gaming-arrows, they choose the costly [camels].")
(وَرُدُّوا إِلَى اللَّهِ مَوْلاهُمُ الْحَقِّ): in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective), and likewise «الحقّ». «الحق» may be in the accusative in three ways: the implied form may be "they were returned truly", and then the alif and lām were brought; the implied form may be "their master truly, not what they worship besides Him"; and the third way is that it be praise, i.e. "I mean the True". It is also permissible to put «الحقّ» in the nominative, the meaning being "their master is the True, not what they associate besides Him". (وَضَلَّ عَنْهُمْ ما كانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ): in the position of the nominative, and it has the sense of a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. their fabrication.

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: (فَذلِكُمُ اللَّهُ رَبُّكُمُ الْحَقُّ): the accusative of «الحق» is also permissible, as explained above.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: (كَذلِكَ حَقَّتْ كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ فَسَقُوا أَنَّهُمْ): the meaning is «بأنّهم» and «لأنهم» ("in that they" / "because they"), so «أنّ» is in the position of the accusative. Abū Isḥāq said: It may also be in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) from «كلمات» [Translator's note: so in the source; the reading being discussed here is «كلمة»]. Al-Farrāʾ said: (أَنَّهُمْ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ) is permissible with kasra of «إنّ», as a new sentence.

nahhas-irab:35-35.t:
(أَمَّنْ): al-Akhfash said: If someone asks, "How can «أم» come in upon «من»?", it is said: because «أم» and the alif are the basis of interrogation; do you not see that «أم» indicates «هل»?
Abū Jaʿfar said: There are five readings of (أَمَّنْ لا يَهِدِّي). Abū ʿAmr, Ibn Kathīr and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir read «أم من لا يهدّي» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and the hāʾ and doubling of the dāl [yahaddī]; and so Warsh related from Nāfiʿ. Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿArafa narrated to me: he said: Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq narrated to me: he said: Qālūn narrated to me from Nāfiʿ that he read «أم من لا يهدّي» with fatḥa on the yāʾ, sukūn on the hāʾ and doubling of the dāl [yahddī]. Abū ʿUbayd said: ʿĀṣim read (أَمَّنْ لا يَهِدِّي) with fatḥa on the yāʾ, kasra on the hāʾ and doubling of the dāl [yahiddī]. Al-Kisāʾī said: ʿĀṣim read «أم من لا يهدي» with kasra on the yāʾ and the hāʾ and doubling of the dāl [yihiddī]. These are four readings. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read «أم من لا يهدي» with fatḥa on the yāʾ, sukūn on the hāʾ and a light dāl [yahdī].
Abū Jaʿfar said: The first reading is clear in Arabic: its original is «يهتدي»; the tāʾ was assimilated into the dāl and its vowel was transferred to the hāʾ. The third reading is the one known from ʿĀṣim, al-Ḥasan and Abū Rajāʾ: the yāʾ [Translator's note: so in the source; the tāʾ is meant] was assimilated into the dāl, and the hāʾ was given kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. The second reading, which Qālūn related from Nāfiʿ, represents a combination of two quiescent letters; this is not permissible, and no one is able to pronounce it. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: Whoever attempts the like of this must make a slight movement towards kasra; Sībawayh calls this "snatching the vowel" (ikhtilās al-ḥaraka). As for the kasra of the yāʾ together with the hāʾ, which al-Kisāʾī related from ʿĀṣim, it is not permissible according to Sībawayh. Sībawayh permits «تهدي», «نهدي» and «إهدي» [tihiddī, nihiddī, ihiddī — Translator's note: the source prints «تهدي ويهدي وأهدي»] and does not permit «يهدي» [yihiddī], because kasra on the yāʾ is heavy. As for the fifth reading, «أم من لا يهدي», it has two constructions in Arabic, though it is far-fetched. One of the two is that al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ said: «يهدي» means «يهتدي» ("is guided"). Abū al-ʿAbbās said: This is not known; rather, the implied form is "or one who does not guide another" — the sentence is complete; then He said (إِلَّا أَنْ يُهْدى), an exception not of the same kind as the first, i.e. "but he himself needs to be guided", as you say «فلان لا يشبع غيره إلّا أن يشبع» ("so-and-so does not satisfy anyone else's hunger, except that he be fed"), i.e. but he himself needs to be fed. Abū Isḥāq said: (فَما لَكُمْ) — the sentence is complete, and the meaning is "what do you have in worshipping idols?" (كَيْفَ تَحْكُمُونَ): he said: (كَيْفَ) is in the position of the accusative, and the meaning is "in what state?".

nahhas-irab:37-37.t:
(وَما كانَ هذَا الْقُرْآنُ أَنْ يُفْتَرى مِنْ دُونِ): al-Kisāʾī said: The meaning is "this Qur'an is not a fabrication", as you say «فلان يحبّ أن يركب» and «يحبّ الركوب» ("he likes to ride" / "he likes riding"). Someone else said: The implied form is «لأن يفترى» ("to be fabricated"). Al-Farrāʾ said: The meaning is "it is not fitting for this Qur'an to be fabricated". Someone else said: The meaning is "no one could produce the like of this Qur'an from other than Allah and then attribute it to Allah", because of its inimitability in its arrangement, its meanings and its composition.
(وَلكِنْ تَصْدِيقَ الَّذِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ): al-Kisāʾī, al-Farrāʾ and Muḥammad ibn Saʿdān said: The implied form is "but it was a confirmation of what was before it". According to them the nominative is also permissible, meaning "but it is a confirmation"; and likewise (وَتَفْصِيلَ الْكِتابِ لا رَيْبَ فِيهِ مِنْ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ).

nahhas-irab:38-38.t: (أَمْ يَقُولُونَ افْتَراهُ): «أم» in the sense of «بل» ("rather"), and it carries the sense of making them acknowledge (taqrīr), so as to establish the argument against them.

nahhas-irab:39-39.t: (بَلْ كَذَّبُوا بِما لَمْ يُحِيطُوا بِعِلْمِهِ): i.e. they denied it while ignorant of its meanings and interpretation, whereas they were obliged to learn that by asking. (وَلَمَّا يَأْتِهِمْ): i.e. they denied it without knowing its interpretation; it is also said: and there has not yet come to them what its matter will lead to. (كَذلِكَ كَذَّبَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ): i.e. such was their way; the kāf is in the position of the accusative. (فَانْظُرْ كَيْفَ كانَ عاقِبَةُ الظَّالِمِينَ): «كيف» is in the position of the accusative as the khabar (predicate) of kāna.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: (إِلَيْهِ مَرْجِعُكُمْ): nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). (جَمِيعاً): as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَعْدَ اللَّهِ): a maṣdar (verbal noun), because the meaning of "your return" is "He has promised you". (حَقًّا): a maṣdar, accusative. Al-Farrāʾ permitted «وعد الله» in the nominative, meaning "your return to Him is the promise of Allah". Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā Thaʿlab said: he makes it the khabar (predicate) of «مرجعكم». Al-Farrāʾ also permitted «وعد الله حقّ». Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ read (إِنَّهُ يَبْدَؤُا الْخَلْقَ) [Translator's note: i.e. annahu, with fatḥa; the source prints the standard vowelling], with «أنّ» in the position of the accusative, i.e. "He promised you that He originates creation"; the implied form may also be "because He originates creation", as one says «لبّيك أن الحمد والنّعمة لك» ("at Your service — for praise and grace are Yours"). The kasra is better. Al-Farrāʾ permitted «أنّ» to be in the position of the nominative. Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā said: the implied form is then "truly, the originating of creation".

nahhas-irab:40-40.t: (وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يُؤْمِنُ بِهِ): i.e. in the future; «من» is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and likewise (وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ لا يُؤْمِنُ بِهِ). The meaning is: and among them is one who persists in his disbelief. So Allah, Majestic and Mighty, made known that He delayed the punishment from them only because among them are some who will believe. (وَرَبُّكَ أَعْلَمُ بِالْمُفْسِدِينَ): i.e. of those who persist in disbelief.

nahhas-irab:41-41.t: (وَإِنْ كَذَّبُوكَ فَقُلْ لِي عَمَلِي): nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); the meaning is "mine is the recompense of my deeds"; and likewise (وَلَكُمْ عَمَلُكُمْ). (أَنْتُمْ بَرِيئُونَ مِمَّا أَعْمَلُ وَأَنَا بَرِيءٌ مِمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ): the same.

nahhas-irab:42-42.t: (وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَسْتَمِعُونَ إِلَيْكَ): [the plural is] according to the meaning [of «من»].

nahhas-irab:43-43.t: (وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَنْظُرُ إِلَيْكَ): [the singular is] according to the wording [of «من»].

nahhas-irab:44-44.t:
(وَلكِنَّ النَّاسَ أَنْفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ): a group of grammarians, among them al-Farrāʾ, claimed that when the Arabs say «ولكنّ» with the wāw they prefer the doubled form, and when they drop the wāw they prefer the light form. Al-Farrāʾ gave a reason for this; he said: Because without the wāw it resembles «بل», so they lightened it so that what follows it would be like what follows «بل»; and when they brought the wāw it differed from «بل», so they doubled it and put [the following noun] in the accusative by it, because it is «إنّ» with a lām and a kāf added to it, made into a single particle. He recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 199-
ولكنّني من حبّها لكميد
("But I, from love of her, am surely grief-stricken.")
He brought the lām because it is «إنّ».

nahhas-irab:45-45.t:
(كَأَنْ لَمْ يَلْبَثُوا): in the sense of «كأنّهم لم يلبثوا» ("as if they had not tarried"). (يَتَعارَفُونَ): in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(قَدْ خَسِرَ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِلِقاءِ اللَّهِ): this may be a statement from Allah, Majestic and Mighty, after He has pointed to the resurrection and the raising; and the meaning may be that they recognise one another, saying this among themselves.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t:
(هُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ الشَّمْسَ ضِياءً): two objects. (وَالْقَمَرَ نُوراً): conjoined. (وَقَدَّرَهُ مَنازِلَ): in the sense of "and He determined for it", like (وَإِذا كالُوهُمْ) [al-Muṭaffifīn: 3]; it is also possible that the meaning is "He made it possessed of stations", like (وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ) [Yūsuf: 82]. He said «وقدّره» and did not say «وقدّرهما», though the sun and the moon both have stations; there are two answers to this. One is that He singled out the moon because ordinary people know the months by it. The other answer is that [the pronoun] is omitted from the first because the second indicates it; Sībawayh and al-Farrāʾ recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 196-
رماني بأمر كنت منه ووالدي ... بريئا ومن جول الطّويّ رماني
("He accused me of a thing of which I and my father were innocent; and from the side of the well he cast it at me.")
(لِتَعْلَمُوا عَدَدَ السِّنِينَ وَالْحِسابَ): on the basis that it is the nūn of the [sound masculine] plural. Some Arabs say «عدد السّنين والحساب» [Translator's note: presumably al-sinīni, declining on the nūn; the vowelling is not shown in the source]. Some Arabs say «سنوات» and some say «سنهات», and the diminutive is «سنيهة» and «سنيّة». It is permissible to pluralise them with wāw and nūn as compensation for what was dropped from them, and the first letter is given kasra as an indication of what has been attached to it that properly belongs to others. (ما خَلَقَ اللَّهُ ذلِكَ إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ): i.e. Allah, Majestic and Mighty, intended nothing by creating that except wisdom and rightness.

nahhas-irab:7-8.t: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ لا يَرْجُونَ لِقاءَنا): the ism of inna, and the khabar (predicate) is (أُولئِكَ مَأْواهُمُ النَّارُ).

nahhas-irab:46-46.t: وَإِمَّا نُرِيَنَّكَ: a condition (sharṭ). أَوْ نَتَوَفَّيَنَّكَ: conjoined to it. فَإِلَيْنا مَرْجِعُهُمْ: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ثُمَّ اللَّهُ شَهِيدٌ: a clause conjoined to a clause. al-Farrāʾ said: and if it were said «ثمّ الله شهيد» in the sense of "there" (هناك), it would be permissible. «[Translator's note: i.e. read as «ثَمَّ» ("there"), the adverb, rather than the conjunction «ثُمَّ».]»

nahhas-irab:47-47.t: وَلِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ رَسُولٌ فَإِذا جاءَ رَسُولُهُمْ قُضِيَ بَيْنَهُمْ: the meaning may be: every nation has a messenger who is a witness against them, and when their messenger comes on the Day of Resurrection, judgement is passed between them, like فَكَيْفَ إِذا جِئْنا مِنْ كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ بِشَهِيدٍ [al-Nisāʾ: 41]. And the meaning may be that they are not punished until We send [a messenger] to them, like وَما كُنَّا مُعَذِّبِينَ حَتَّى نَبْعَثَ رَسُولًا [al-Isrāʾ: 15].

nahhas-irab:50-50.t: قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ أَتاكُمْ عَذابُهُ بَياتاً أَوْ نَهاراً: two adverbs (ẓarf, mafʿūl fīhi). ماذا يَسْتَعْجِلُ مِنْهُ الْمُجْرِمُونَ: if you make the hāʾ in «منه» refer back to the punishment, there are two possible analyses: «ما» is in the position of the nominative (rafʿ) as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «ذا» has the meaning of «الذي» ("which") and is the khabar (predicate) of «ما»; the other analysis is that «ماذا» is a single unit in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is in the clause. And if you make the hāʾ in «منه» refer back to the name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and make «ماذا» a single unit, «ما» is in the position of the accusative (naṣb) governed by «يستعجل». The meaning is: what thing do the criminals seek to hasten from Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He?

nahhas-irab:51-51.t: أَثُمَّ إِذا ما وَقَعَ آمَنْتُمْ بِهِ: there is an ellipsis in the speech, and the implied form is: «أتأمنون أن ينزل بكم العذاب ثم يقال بكم إذا حلّ بكم الآن آمنتم به» ("Do you feel secure that the punishment will descend upon you, and then it will be said to you, when it has befallen you: Now you believe in it?"). «[Translator's note: the source has «يقال بكم»; «يقال لكم» ("it will be said to you") would be expected.]» Concerning the fatḥa of «الآن» there are three views. Two of them belong to al-Farrāʾ. The first is that its origin is «أوان» ("time"): the hamza was dropped from it and the wāw changed into alif, then the alif and lām were brought in, so it was made indeclinable (mabnī) with them and remained on its accusative ending. The second view is that its origin is from (آن), i.e. "it has become time" (حان); then the alif and lām entered it and it remained on its fatḥa, like «قيل وقال» ("it was said" and "he said"). Abū Isḥāq claimed that if this were so, it would not be permissible for it to be [as it is] with the alif and lām, just as one says: «نهى عن القيلِ والقالِ» ("he forbade gossip and hearsay"). «[Translator's note: the point appears to be that such verbs, once given the article, are treated as declinable nouns, as in «القيلِ والقالِ» with the genitive.]» The third view is the doctrine of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh: the proper function of the alif and lām is to enter for something already known (maʿhūd), and (الآن) is not something already known; its meaning is only "we are at this time doing such-and-such". Since it contained the meaning of "this", it had to be indeclinable, and it was given fatḥa because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.

nahhas-irab:53-53.t:
وَيَسْتَنْبِئُونَكَ: i.e. about the punishment's coming about. أَحَقٌّ: a mubtadaʾ (subject). هُوَ: a fāʿil (agent) that stands in place of the khabar (predicate).
This is the view of Sībawayh; and «هو» may also be a mubtadaʾ with «حقّ» as its khabar. قُلْ إِي وَرَبِّي: an oath, and its response (jawāb) is إِنَّهُ لَحَقٌّ.

nahhas-irab:55-55.t: أَلا إِنَّ وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقٌّ: i.e. His is the dominion of the heavens and the earth, so there is no preventer to prevent Him from carrying out what He has promised.

nahhas-irab:56-56.t: هُوَ يُحْيِ: assimilation (idghām) is not permissible here according to Sībawayh, lest two quiescent letters come together.

nahhas-irab:58-58.t: فَبِذلِكَ فَلْيَفْرَحُوا: a reference to the bounty and the mercy; the Arabs use «ذلك» for the singular, the dual and the plural. It is narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he read «فبذلك فلتفرحوا» ("in that let you rejoice"), and this is the reading of Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ. Hārūn said: in the codex (ḥarf) of Ubayy it is «فافرحوا» ("so rejoice"). Abū Jaʿfar said: the proper way of the imperative is to have the lām, so that there is a jussive particle with it, just as with the prohibition there is a particle; except that they omit it from the imperative addressed to the second person, dispensing with it because the person is addressed directly; and sometimes they bring it in its original form, and of this is «فبذلك فلتفرحوا».

nahhas-irab:59-59.t: «ما» is in the position of the accusative (naṣb), governed by «رأيتم»; and Abū Isḥāq said: it is in the position of the accusative, governed by «أنزل». «[Translator's note: the reference is to «قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ ما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ مِنْ رِزْقٍ».]»

nahhas-irab:61-61.t: وَما تَكُونُ فِي شَأْنٍ وَما تَتْلُوا مِنْهُ مِنْ قُرْآنٍ: al-Farrāʾ said: the hāʾ in «منه» refers back to the affair (الشأن), and this is a statement that needs explanation. The meaning would be: and you do not recite [anything] from the affair, i.e. on account of the affair; i.e. an affair occurs and the Qur'an is recited on account of it so that its ruling may be known, or Qur'an is revealed concerning it and is recited. يَعْزُبُ عَنْ رَبِّكَ مِنْ مِثْقالِ ذَرَّةٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلا فِي السَّماءِ وَلا أَصْغَرَ مِنْ ذلِكَ وَلا أَكْبَرَ إِلَّا: conjoined to «مثقال», or if you wish to «ذرة»; the nominative (rafʿ) is by conjunction to the position, because «من» is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis; and the nominative is also permissible as a mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) being إِلَّا فِي كِتابٍ مُبِينٍ. «[Translator's note: «إِلَّا» stands in the source after the quoted words, before "conjoined"; it appears to belong to the following phrase إِلَّا فِي كِتابٍ مُبِينٍ.]» Some of the grammarians claimed that in the one in «Sabaʾ» only the nominative is permissible, because «من» is not with it; that is a mistake, and we will mention it in its place, if Allah wills.

nahhas-irab:62-62.t: أَلا إِنَّ أَوْلِياءَ اللَّهِ: the noun (ism) of «إنّ». لا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ: in the position of the khabar (predicate); i.e. whoever Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, takes as His ally, and takes charge of guarding and protecting him, and is pleased with him, will not fear on the Day of Resurrection nor grieve. Similar to it is لا يَحْزُنُهُمُ الْفَزَعُ الْأَكْبَرُ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 103].

nahhas-irab:63-63.t:
الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا: in the position of the accusative (naṣb) as a badal (substitute) from the ism of «إنّ», or if you wish by [an implied] «أعني» ("I mean"); and the nominative (rafʿ) by implying a mubtadaʾ, and as a badal from the position [of the ism of «إنّ»], and as a mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) being هُمُ الْبُشْرى فِي الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ. «[Translator's note: the source quotes «هُمُ الْبُشْرى»; the text of the ayah (64) is «لَهُمُ الْبُشْرى».]»
There is a fourth view on it: al-Kisāʾī said: the naʿt (adjective) follows the pronoun latent in the verb. al-Farrāʾ said: this is a mistake, because a pronoun is not qualified by an overt noun. Abū Jaʿfar said: as for his statement that a pronoun is not qualified by an overt noun, that is correct; but it may be that al-Kisāʾī meant that this, which is a naʿt following the pronoun, is what the Basrans call badal, because the Kufans do not use this term, I mean badal. Abū Jaʿfar said: we have already mentioned the meaning of هُمُ الْبُشْرى فِي الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ.
It has been said: in the life of this world at death, and in the Hereafter when they come out of their graves. And it was said «[Translator's note: the source prints «وقبل», evidently for «وقيل» ("and it was said")]»: it is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: يُبَشِّرُهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ بِرَحْمَةٍ مِنْهُ وَرِضْوانٍ [al-Tawba: 21], the verse; and what indicates this is تَبْدِيلَ لِكَلِماتِ اللَّهِ. «[Translator's note: the ayah reads «لا تَبْدِيلَ لِكَلِماتِ اللَّهِ»; «لا» is missing in the source.]»

nahhas-irab:65-65.t: وَلا يَحْزُنْكَ قَوْلُهُمْ: the statement is complete here; then He said إِنَّ الْعِزَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعاً: [«جميعا» is] accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:70-70.t: al-Kisāʾī said: مَتاعٌ فِي الدُّنْيا, i.e. «ذلك متاع» ("that is an enjoyment") or «هو متاع في الدنيا» ("it is an enjoyment in this world"). Abū Isḥāq said: the accusative is permissible outside the Qur'an. ثُمَّ نُذِيقُهُمُ الْعَذابَ الشَّدِيدَ بِما كانُوا يَكْفُرُونَ: i.e. because of their disbelief.

nahhas-irab:71-71.t:
وَاتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ: the wāw was dropped because it is an imperative. إِذْ: in the position of the accusative (naṣb). فَأَجْمِعُوا أَمْرَكُمْ وَشُرَكاءَكُمْ: with the connective alif made disjunctive (qaṭʿ) and the accusative of «الشركاء»; this is the reading of most of the imams. ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read فَأَجْمِعُوا أَمْرَكُمْ, from «جمع يجمع», with وَشُرَكاءَكُمْ accusative «[Translator's note: the words are printed identically to the first reading; from «جمع يجمع» the reading meant is «فاجْمَعوا» with a connective alif]»; and al-Ḥasan, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, ʿĪsā and Yaʿqūb read «فأجمعوا أمركم وشركاؤكم» with the alif disjunctive and the nominative (rafʿ) of «الشركاء». The first reading is from «أجمع على الشيء يُجمع» ("to resolve upon a thing"), when one has determined upon it. Concerning the accusative of «الشركاء» on this reading there are three views. al-Farrāʾ said: «أجمع الشيء» means «عدّه» (he made it ready). al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ said: it has the meaning of «وادعوا شركاءكم» ("and call your partners"), so for both of them it is accusative by an implied verb of this kind. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: it is conjoined according to the sense, as [the poet] said: [majzūʾ al-kāmil] 200-
يا ليت زوجك قد غدا ... متقلّدا سيفا ورمحا
(Would that your husband had gone out in the morning, girt with a sword and a spear.)
And a spear is not girded on, but it is carried like the sword. Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning is "with your partners", as one says: «التقى الماء والخشبة» ("the water met the plank"). The second reading is by conjunction to «أمركم», or if you wish with the meaning of "with". Abū Jaʿfar said: and I heard Abū Isḥāq permit «قام زيد وعمرا» ("Zayd stood up together with ʿAmr"). The third reading is by conjoining «الشركاء» to the nominative pronoun; conjunction to the nominative pronoun is acceptable [here] because the speech has become long. This reading is far-fetched, because if it were nominative it would have had to be written with wāw; and moreover, your partners are the idols, and the idols do nothing. ثُمَّ لا يَكُنْ أَمْرُكُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ غُمَّةً: the ism of «يكون» and its khabar. ثُمَّ اقْضُوا إِلَيَّ: a connective alif, from «قضى يقضي». al-Akhfash and al-Kisāʾī said: it is like وَقَضَيْنا إِلَيْهِ ذلِكَ الْأَمْرَ [al-Ḥijr: 66], i.e. We conveyed it to him and made it reach him. It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning ثُمَّ اقْضُوا إِلَيَّ وَلا تُنْظِرُونِ that he said: "Proceed against me and do not delay." Abū Jaʿfar said:
this is a sound statement linguistically, and from it is «قضى الميّت», i.e. he passed on. And by this he informed them that they would not reach him, and this is one of the proofs of prophethood. al-Farrāʾ claimed [it could be] «ثمّ أفضوا», with a disjunctive alif and fāʾ, [meaning] «توجّهوا إليّ حتى تصلوا» ("turn towards me until you reach [me]"); and from it is «أفضت الخلافة إلى فلان» ("the caliphate passed to so-and-so").

nahhas-irab:72-72.t: فَإِنْ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ: i.e. if you turn away from what I have brought you, that is not because I asked you for a wage.

nahhas-irab:74-74.t: فَما كانُوا لِيُؤْمِنُوا بِما كَذَّبُوا بِهِ مِنْ قَبْلُ: it was said that the implied form is «بما كذّب به قوم نوح من قبل» ("in what the people of Noah denied before"). Among the best of what has been said about this is that it concerns a particular people, like أَأَنْذَرْتَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تُنْذِرْهُمْ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ [al-Baqara: 6].

nahhas-irab:77-77.t:
al-Akhfash said: أَسِحْرٌ هذا is a quotation of their words, because they had said «أسحر هذا» ("Is this magic?"), so it was said to them:
"Do you say of the truth when it has come to you: Is this magic?"

nahhas-irab:78-78.t: It is narrated from al-Ḥasan: «ويكون لكما الكبرياء» with yāʾ, because it is a non-real feminine and there is separation between them. Sībawayh reported: «حضر القاضيَ اليومَ امرأتان» ("two women came before the judge today").

nahhas-irab:80-80.t: أَنْتُمْ: nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) being مُلْقُونَ; the clause is in the ṣila (relative clause), and the pronoun returning to «الذي» is omitted, i.e. «ملقوه» ("[which you are] casting").

nahhas-irab:81-81.t:
فَلَمَّا أَلْقَوْا قالَ مُوسى ما جِئْتُمْ بِهِ السِّحْرُ: there are five readings of it, and most of the readers follow this reading. ما جِئْتُمْ بِهِ السِّحْرُ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). Abū Jaʿfar Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ and Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ read ما جِئْتُمْ بِهِ السِّحْرُ «[Translator's note: printed identically to the first reading; the reading of these two is the interrogative «آلسِّحْرُ»]»: «ما» is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is «جئتم به». The implied meaning is: "What thing is it that you have brought?" — by way of rebuke and belittlement of what they brought.
السِّحْرُ is [then nominative] by an implied mubtadaʾ, the implied form being «هو السحر» ("it is magic"). Hārūn the reader said: in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is «ما جئتم به سحر», and this too is mubtadaʾ and khabar. The entry of the alif and lām in this is more usual in the speech of the Arabs, because they had said to Moses ﷺ: «هذا سحر» ("this is magic"), so he said to them: rather, what you have brought is the magic (السحر). In the same way one says at the beginning of books and letters: «سلام على من اتّبع الهدى» ("peace be upon whoever follows the guidance"), and at their end:
«والسلام» ("and the peace"). If someone said to you, "I found a dirham," and you then asked him, the preferred choice would be to say «فأين الدرهم؟» ("so where is the dirham?"), and you would not say «أين درهم؟» ("where is a dirham?"), lest it be imagined that you were asking him about another one. Hārūn said: in the codex (ḥarf) of Ubayy it is «ما آتيتم به سحر», and this is like the one before it. al-Farrāʾ permitted «ما جئتم به السّحرَ إنّ الله سيبطله» with the accusative of «السحر», making «ما» conditional and «جئتم» in the position of the jussive (jazm) by «ما», with the fāʾ omitted, the implied form being «فإنّ الله سيبطله», as [the poet] said: [al-basīṭ] 201-
من يفعل الحسنات الله يشكرها ... والشّر بالشرّ عند الله مثلان
(Whoever does good deeds, Allah will thank him for them; and evil for evil — with Allah the two are equal.)
And «السحر», according to him, is accusative by «جئتم», but he did not explain it in a way that makes clear the true nature of the accusative. Abū Jaʿfar said: «السحر» would be accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. «ما جئتم به سحرا», and then the alif and lām were brought in; except that omitting the fāʾ in the conditional (mujāzāt) is not permitted by many of the grammarians except under poetic necessity; indeed some of them have even rejected that it could be permissible by intention [of the fāʾ]. «[Translator's note: the final phrase «أن يجوز النيّة» is elliptical in the source and is rendered according to its apparent sense.]» And I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd told me: al-Māzinī told me: I heard al-Aṣmaʿī say: the grammarians altered this verse; the [correct] transmission is only:
من يفعل الخير فالرحمن يشكره (Whoever does good, the All-Merciful will thank him.) And I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: omitting the fāʾ in the conditional is permissible. He said: the proof of that is the reading «وما أصابكم من مصيبة بما كسبت أيديكم» [al-Shūrā: 1] and وَما أَصابَكُمْ مِنْ مُصِيبَةٍ فَبِما كَسَبَتْ أَيْدِيكُمْ [al-Shūrā 2] — two well-known, recognised readings. «[Translator's note: both refer to al-Shūrā 42:30; the bracketed numbers are as printed in the source.]»

nahhas-irab:82-82.t: وَيُحِقُّ اللَّهُ الْحَقَّ بِكَلِماتِهِ: i.e. He makes the truth clear by His speech, His arguments and His proofs.

nahhas-irab:83-83.t:
فَما آمَنَ لِمُوسى إِلَّا ذُرِّيَّةٌ مِنْ قَوْمِهِ: [«ذريّة» is] nominative by its verb; it may not be accusative as an exception, because the speech before it is not complete. عَلى خَوْفٍ مِنْ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَائِهِمْ: He did not say «وملائه» ("and his chiefs"), and there are six answers concerning this. One of them is that since Pharaoh was a tyrant, he was spoken of with the [pronoun] form used for a plural. Another is that when Pharaoh was mentioned it was known that others were with him, so the pronoun refers back to him and to them; this is one of al-Farrāʾ's two answers. Another is that the group was called "Pharaoh", like Thamūd. al-Farrāʾ's other answer is that the implied form is «على خوف من آل فرعون» ("in fear of the family of Pharaoh"), like وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ. This answer is wrong according to the doctrine of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh: for both of them «قامت هند» ("Hind stood up") is not permissible when you mean her servant boy. The fifth answer is the doctrine of al-Akhfash Saʿīd: that the pronoun refers back to the progeny, i.e. "and the chiefs of the progeny". The sixth answer, which seems to be the clearest of them, is that the pronoun refers back to «قومه» ("his people"). أَنْ يَفْتِنَهُمْ: in the position of the genitive (khafḍ) as a badal al-ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion), and it may be in the position of the accusative (naṣb), governed by «خوف». «فرعون» is a diptote because it is a foreign name and definite.
لَعالٍ: in the position of the nominative (rafʿ) as the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ»; we have already mentioned its like.

nahhas-irab:85-85.t: فَقالُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ تَوَكَّلْنا: i.e. we have surrendered our affairs to Him, are content with His decree and predestination, and have come to rest in His command.

nahhas-irab:87-88.t:
وَأَوْحَيْنا إِلى مُوسى وَأَخِيهِ أَنْ تَبَوَّءا لِقَوْمِكُما بِمِصْرَ بُيُوتاً وَاجْعَلُوا بُيُوتَكُمْ قِبْلَةً وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ وَبَشِّرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ (87) وَقالَ مُوسى رَبَّنا إِنَّكَ آتَيْتَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَأَهُ زِينَةً وَأَمْوالاً فِي الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا رَبَّنا لِيُضِلُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِكَ رَبَّنَا اطْمِسْ عَلى أَمْوالِهِمْ وَاشْدُدْ عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ فَلا يُؤْمِنُوا حَتَّى يَرَوُا الْعَذابَ الْأَلِيمَ (88) وَاجْعَلُوا بُيُوتَكُمْ قِبْلَةً: two objects (mafʿūl bihi, direct object); and likewise آتَيْتَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَأَهُ زِينَةً وَأَمْوالًا. فِي الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا رَبَّنا لِيُضِلُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِكَ: the lām of kay (purpose). The soundest of what has been said about it, and it is the doctrine of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, is that since their affair ended in this, it was as though [it had been given] for this; and it is called the lām of consequence (lām al-ʿāqiba), i.e. since the outcome of their affair had come to this, it was in the position of that for whose sake the first thing was done. Some people claimed that the meaning is: "Our Lord, You have given Pharaoh and his chiefs adornment and wealth in the life of this world so that they would not lead astray from Your way", with «لا» omitted, as He said يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ أَنْ تَضِلُّوا [al-Nisāʾ: 176], the meaning being «أن لا تضلّوا» ("lest you go astray"). Abū Jaʿfar said:
the outward form of this answer is good, except that the Arabs do not omit «لا» together with «أن»; so the author of this answer gave a misleading semblance [of proof] with His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: «أن تضلّوا». رَبَّنَا اطْمِسْ عَلى أَمْوالِهِمْ وَاشْدُدْ عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ فَلا يُؤْمِنُوا: this too is among the difficult points. It is asked: how could he pray against them, when the way of the messengers, Allah bless them and grant them peace, is to call their people to faith? The answer is that the meaning of «اطمس على أموالهم» is: punish them for their disbelief by destroying their wealth. Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning of the effacing (taṭmīs) of a thing is removing it from its form. وَاشْدُدْ عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ: it was said that its meaning is "grieve them as a punishment for them", and it was said that its meaning is "make them endure what has befallen them, [so that] they do not go out to a fertile place", because the meaning of «شددت الشيء» and «ربطته» in the language is "I constricted it". فَلا يُؤْمِنُوا is not a supplication according to the view of Muḥammad ibn Yazīd; he said: it is conjoined to His saying «ليضلّوا». al-Kisāʾī and Abū ʿUbayda said: it is a supplication, so for both of them it is in the position of the jussive (jazm). al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ permitted it to be a response (jawāb), and al-Farrāʾ recited: [al-rajaz] 202-
يا ناق سيري عنقا فسيحا ... إلى سليمان فنستريحا
(O she-camel, travel at a broad, swift pace to Sulaymān, so that we may rest.)
On this [view], the nūn was dropped because it is accusative (manṣūb).

nahhas-meani:1-1.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿الۤر تِلْكَ آيَاتُ ٱلْكِتَابِ ٱلْحَكِيمِ﴾.
ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib narrated from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr concerning the saying of Allah the Exalted ﴿الۤر﴾: he said: [It means] "I am Allah; I see."
Abū Jaʿfar said: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to us; he said: al-Zaʿfarānī narrated to us; he said: ʿAlī ibn al-Jaʿd narrated to us; he said: Sharīk narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Abū al-Ḍuḥā, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿الۤر﴾ — he said: I am Allah; I see.
And in the narration of ʿIkrima from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿الر﴾, ﴿حم﴾ and ﴿ن﴾ are the letters of «الرحمن» (al-Raḥmān), separated.
Abū Jaʿfar said: We have explained this at the beginning of Sūrat al-Baqara.
The meaning of ﴿ٱلْحَكِيمِ﴾ according to the people of language is «المُحْكَم» (made firm), just as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿هَذَا مَا لَدَيَّ عَتِيدٌ﴾, that is, «مُعَدٌّ» (prepared) [Translator's note: a faʿīl pattern in the sense of a passive participle].

nahhas-meani:2-2.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَكَانَ لِلنَّاسِ عَجَباً أَنْ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ رَجُلٍ مِّنْهُمْ أَنْ أَنذِرِ ٱلنَّاسَ﴾.
It is narrated that by "the people" here is meant the people of Mecca, because they said: How strange! Did Allah find no messenger other than Abū Ṭālib's orphan? So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed ﴿أَكَانَ لِلنَّاسِ عَجَباً أَنْ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ رَجُلٍ مِّنْهُمْ أَنْ أَنذِرِ ٱلنَّاسَ﴾.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَبَشِّرِ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ أَنَّ لَهُمْ قَدَمَ صِدْقٍ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: That is, an abode of truth.
And it was said: «القَدَم» is righteous deeds.
And it was said: precedence (al-sābiqa).
And it is narrated from al-Ḥasan or Qatāda that he said: «القَدَم» is Muḥammad ﷺ, who intercedes for them.
Abū Zayd said: «رجلٌ قَدَمٌ», that is, a brave man.
Qatāda said: That is, a forerunner of truth.
Mujāhid said: That is, [a forerunner] of good.
And in the narration of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa from him [Ibn ʿAbbās], he said: Happiness was decreed for them beforehand in the first record.
These views are close to one another, and the meaning is: a lofty rank.

nahhas-meani:3-3.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَا مِن شَفِيعٍ إِلاَّ مِن بَعْدِ إِذْنِهِ﴾.
There had been no mention of an intercessor [before this], because the meaning was already known, since they used to say: "These are our intercessors with Allah." Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿مَا مِن شَفِيعٍ إِلاَّ مِن بَعْدِ إِذْنِهِ﴾, that is, no intercessor intercedes except for one whom He has approved.

nahhas-meani:4-4.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَعْدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقّاً إِنَّهُ يَبْدَأُ ٱلْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar "Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ" read: ﴿أَنَّهُ يَبْدَأُ ٱلْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ﴾ [with fatḥa on the hamza].
Abū Jaʿfar [al-Naḥḥās] said: Reading it with fatḥa admits two meanings:
One of them: "because He…".
The other: "the promise of Allah that He…".
And «القسط» is justice.

nahhas-meani:5-5.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هُوَ ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ ٱلشَّمْسَ ضِيَآءً وَٱلْقَمَرَ نُوراً وَقَدَّرَهُ مَنَازِلَ﴾.
He did not say «وقدَّرهما» (and He measured them both), because what is measured out for the number of years and the reckoning is the moon.
And it [has] twenty-eight stations.
Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: It is possible that the meaning is «وقدَّرهما», and then [one of them] was omitted, as [the poet] said:
نَحْنُ بِمَا عِنْدَنَا وَأَنْتَ بِمَا * عِنْدَكَ رَاضٍ، والرَّأْيُ مُخْتَلِفُ
(We are content with what we have, and you with what you have — and opinion differs.) [i.e. "content" is stated once for both.]

nahhas-meani:9-9.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ يَهْدِيهِمْ رَبُّهُمْ بِإِيمَانِهِمْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, He makes for them a light by which they walk.
And there is narrated from the Prophet ﷺ what strengthens this, that he said: "The believer is met by his deed in the most beautiful form, and it keeps him company and guides him; and the disbeliever is met by his deed in the ugliest form, and it frightens him and leads him astray." This is the sense of the ḥadīth.

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿دَعْوَاهُمْ فِيهَا سُبْحَانَكَ ٱللَّهُمَّ﴾.
That is: their supplication is declaring Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, free of imperfection. ﴿وَتَحِيَّتُهُمْ فِيهَا سَلاَمٌ﴾: that is, they greet one another with [wishes of] safety.
And it is possible that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, greets them with peace, as an honour to them.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَآخِرُ دَعْوَاهُمْ أَنِ ٱلْحَمْدُ للَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ﴾.
So He informed that the opening of their supplication is declaring Allah free of imperfection, and its end is thanking Him.

nahhas-meani:11-11.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَوْ يُعَجِّلُ ٱللَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ ٱلشَّرَّ ٱسْتِعْجَالَهُمْ بِٱلْخَيْرِ لَقُضِيَ إِلَيْهِمْ أَجَلُهُمْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: It is a man's supplicating, when angry, against his family and his children; if that were hastened for them, they would die.
And it was said: It is their saying ﴿اللَّهُمَّ إنْ كَانَ هَذَا هُوَ الحَقَّ مِنْ عِنْدَكَ فَأَمْطِرْ عَلَيْنَا حِجَارَةً مِنَ السَّمَاءِ﴾.
If this were hastened for them, they would perish.

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا مَسَّ ٱلإِنسَانَ ٱلضُّرُّ دَعَانَا لِجَنبِهِ أَوْ قَاعِداً أَوْ قَآئِماً﴾.
It is possible that the meaning is: and when harm touches man while lying down, or sitting, or standing, he calls upon Us.
And it is possible that the implied construction (taqdīr) is: he calls upon Us in one of these states.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَلَمَّا كَشَفْنَا عَنْهُ ضُرَّهُ مَرَّ كَأَن لَّمْ يَدْعُنَآ إِلَىٰ ضُرٍّ مَّسَّهُ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayd narrated from Abū ʿUbayda that «مرَّ» is in the sense of «استمرَّ» (he continued).
Al-Farrāʾ said: That is, he continued in what he had been upon before the harm touched him.

nahhas-meani:13-13.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أَهْلَكْنَا ٱلْقُرُونَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ لَمَّا ظَلَمُواْ وَجَآءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُم بِٱلْبَيِّنَاتِ وَمَا كَانُواْ لِيُؤْمِنُواْ﴾.
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَمَا كَانُواْ لِيُؤْمِنُواْ﴾ — there are two views on it:
One of them: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, informed of what He knew of them had He let them remain.
The other: that He requited them for their disbelief by sealing their hearts.
And what indicates this is that He said: ﴿كَذٰلِكَ نَجْزِي ٱلْقَوْمَ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ آيَاتُنَا بَيِّنَاتٍ قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يَرْجُونَ لِقَآءَنَا ٱئْتِ بِقُرْآنٍ غَيْرِ هَـٰذَآ أَوْ بَدِّلْهُ﴾.
Qatāda said: Those who said this were the idolaters of the people of Mecca.
Someone else said: That is, bring a Qurʾān in which there is no mention of the resurrection and the raising, nor insulting of our gods. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿قُلْ مَا يَكُونُ لِيۤ أَنْ أُبَدِّلَهُ مِن تِلْقَآءِ نَفْسِيۤ﴾.

nahhas-meani:16-16.t:
Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿قُل لَّوْ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مَا تَلَوْتُهُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَلاَ أَدْرَاكُمْ بِهِ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: That is, nor would He have made you aware of it, nor informed you of it.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَقَدْ لَبِثْتُ فِيكُمْ عُمُراً مِّن قَبْلِهِ﴾.
Qatāda said: He remained among them forty years, and he spent two years seeing the visions of the prophets; and he ﷺ died at the age of sixty-two.

nahhas-meani:18-18.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لاَ يَضُرُّهُمْ وَلاَ يَنفَعُهُمْ﴾ [verse 18].
That is: what does not harm them if they do not worship it, nor benefit them if they worship it.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿هَـٰؤُلاۤءِ شُفَعَاؤُنَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ قُلْ أَتُنَبِّئُونَ ٱللَّهَ بِمَا لاَ يَعْلَمُ فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَلاَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
That is: Do you worship what does not intercede, nor help, nor discern, and say: It intercedes for us with Allah — and so you lie? And is it possible for you to inform Him of what He does not know?

nahhas-meani:19-19.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ ٱلنَّاسُ إِلاَّ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً فَٱخْتَلَفُواْ﴾.
There are three views on it:
The clearest of them is the view of Mujāhid: that in the time of Adam ﷺ they were upon a single religion, then they differed.
The second view: that this is general [in wording] with a specific meaning, and that "the people" here means the Arabs specifically.
The third view: that it is like his saying ﷺ: "Every child is born upon the natural disposition (al-fiṭra)", that is, then they differ after that.

nahhas-meani:21-21.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَآ أَذَقْنَا ٱلنَّاسَ رَحْمَةً مِّن بَعْدِ ضَرَّآءَ مَسَّتْهُمْ﴾.
By "the people" here the disbelievers are meant, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿إنَّ الإِنْسَانَ لِرَبِّهِ لَكَنُودٌ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: That is the hypocrite.
The mercy here is relief, and ﴿مِّن بَعْدِ ضَرَّآءَ﴾ means: after distress.
﴿إِذَا لَهُمْ مَّكْرٌ فِيۤ آيَاتِنَا﴾: that is, they use stratagems so as to attribute the cause of the mercy to something other than its [true] source.
Mujāhid said: ﴿إِذَا لَهُمْ مَّكْرٌ فِيۤ آيَاتِنَا﴾: mockery and denial.

nahhas-meani:22-22.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا كُنتُمْ فِي ٱلْفُلْكِ وَجَرَيْنَ بِهِم بِرِيحٍ طَيِّبَةٍ﴾.
It was said: The meaning is "until, when you are in the ships"; then the address was turned to the Prophet ﷺ, so the meaning became: "and they sailed with them, O Muḥammad."
And it was said: The Arabs put the absent in the place of the present and address him as such, then return him to the absent [person] (iltifāt).
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَظَنُّوۤاْ أَنَّهُمْ أُحِيطَ بِهِمْ﴾.
It is said of one who has fallen into a calamity: «قد أُحيط به» (he has been surrounded), as though the calamity has encompassed him. The origin of this is that when the enemy surrounds a place, its people have perished.

nahhas-meani:23-23.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِذَا هُمْ يَبْغُونَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ بِغَيْرِ ٱلْحَقِّ﴾.
«البغي» is tending towards corruption. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: It is said: «بغى الجرحُ يبغِي بغياً» when a wound tends towards festering.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّمَا بَغْيُكُمْ عَلَىٰ أَنفُسِكُمْ﴾.
That is: your working of injustice comes back upon you.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿مَّتَاعَ ٱلْحَيَاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾.
That is: whatever you obtain through transgression and corruption is only something you take pleasure in during this world. This is the view of the people of language.
It is narrated from Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna that he said: "He meant that transgression is an enjoyment of the life of this world, that is, its punishment is hastened for the one who does it in this world."
As it is said: "Transgression is a place of downfall." And He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿ثُمَّ بُغِيَ عَلَيْهِ لَيَنْصُرَنَّهُ اللهُ﴾.

nahhas-meani:24-24.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَا مَثَلُ ٱلْحَيَاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا كَمَآءٍ أَنزَلْنَاهُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَٱخْتَلَطَ بِهِ نَبَاتُ ٱلأَرْضِ مِمَّا يَأْكُلُ ٱلنَّاسُ وَٱلأَنْعَامُ﴾. «[Translator's note: the quotation in the source begins «مَا مَثَلُ» for «إِنَّمَا مَثَلُ».]»
The vegetation mingled with the rain, and the rain with the vegetation.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَآ أَخَذَتِ ٱلأَرْضُ زُخْرُفَهَا﴾.
«الزخرف» in the language is perfection of beauty; and from it gold was called «زُخْرُف».
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿كَأَن لَّمْ تَغْنَ بِٱلأَمْسِ﴾.
That is: as though it had not flourished.
And the meaning according to the people of language is: as though it had not been inhabited.
And «المعاني» are the dwellings that people inhabit; and «غَنيتُ بالمنزلِ» means: I resided in the dwelling and inhabited it. «[Translator's note: «المعاني» here is evidently a misprint for «المغاني» (dwellings), from the same root as تَغْنَ.]» «[Translator's note: «كأنْ تَنْعم» in the source presumably stands for «كأنْ لم تَنْعم»; translated in that sense.]»

nahhas-meani:25-25.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ يَدْعُوۤاْ إِلَىٰ دَارِ ٱلسَّلاَمِ﴾.
Qatāda said: «دار السلام» is Paradise, and «السلام» is Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning on this [view] is: and Allah invites to His abode.
And repeating the noun [instead of a pronoun], when it is not ambiguous, is more majestic.
Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: And it is possible that the meaning is — and Allah knows best — He invites to the abode in which one is safe from afflictions.

nahhas-meani:26-26.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِّلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُواْ ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ وَزِيَادَةٌ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: What the people of ḥadīth hold is that «الحُسنى» is Paradise and the "increase" is looking upon Allah, exalted be His name. Al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUmar narrated to us; he said: Hannād narrated to us; he said: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Abū Bakr al-Hudhalī, from Abū Tamīma al-Hujaymī, from Abū Mūsā, concerning the saying of Allah the Exalted ﴿لِّلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُواْ ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ﴾: he said: Paradise; ﴿وَزِيَادَةٌ﴾: he said: looking upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
Al-Ḥusayn narrated to us; he said: Hannād narrated to us; he said: Qabīṣa narrated to us; he said: Ḥammād ibn Salama narrated to us; — and it was read to Ibn Bint Manīʿ, from Hudba ibn Khālid; he said: Ḥammād ibn Salama narrated to us — from Thābit al-Bunānī, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, from Ṣuhayb; he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited ﴿لِّلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُواْ ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ وَزِيَادَةٌ﴾ and said: "When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of the Fire enter the Fire, a caller will call out: O people of Paradise, you have an appointment with Allah which He wishes to fulfil for you. They will say: And what is it? Has Allah not made our scales heavy, whitened our faces, admitted us to Paradise and saved us from the Fire? Then the veil will be lifted and He will manifest Himself, and they will look at Him, Mighty and Majestic is He." He said: By Allah, Allah has not given them anything more beloved to them than looking at Him, and that is the "increase".
Abū Jaʿfar said: In the ḥadīth of Ibn Bint Manīʿ [it has] "and let us pass (wa-yujiznā)", and in his ḥadīth [it has] "and they will look at Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He".
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَلاَ يَرْهَقُ وُجُوهَهُمْ قَتَرٌ وَلاَ ذِلَّةٌ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: «القَتَر» is blackness of the faces.
Someone else said: «القَتَر» is the plural of «قَتَرة», which is dust.
The meaning of ﴿يَرْهَقُ﴾ is: covers; and «الذلّة» is abasement.
In the ḥadīth of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā: ﴿وَلاَ يَرْهَقُ وُجُوهَهُمْ قَتَرٌ وَلاَ ذِلَّةٌ﴾ — he said: after their looking at their Lord.
And «العاصم» is the one who protects.

nahhas-meani:27-27.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَأَنَّمَا أُغْشِيَتْ وُجُوهُهُمْ قِطَعاً مِّنَ ٱلْلَّيْلِ مُظْلِماً﴾.
«القِطَع» is the plural of «قِطْعة»; and whoever read ﴿قِطْعاً﴾, it is the name of what is cut off. It is said: «قَطَعَهُ قَطْعاً», and the name of what you have cut off is «قِطْعٌ». «[Translator's note: the source prints the last word as «قِطَعٌ»; the argument requires «قِطْعٌ».]»

nahhas-meani:28-28.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ نَقُولُ لِلَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُواْ مَكَانَكُمْ﴾.
That is: wait in your place — a threat.
﴿فَزَيَّلْنَا بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ is from your saying «زِلتُ الشيءَ من الشيءِ», that is, I removed it; and «زَيَّلْتُ» is for intensification.

nahhas-meani:29-29.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ شَهِيداً بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكُمْ﴾.
Because they said: Who bears witness for you that you are the Messenger of Allah?

nahhas-meani:30-30.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هُنَالِكَ تَبْلُواْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَّآ أَسْلَفَتْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, it tests.
And its meaning is: it finds it and comes to know it.
And concerning ﴿تَبْلُواْ﴾ there are two views: «[Translator's note: the two views that follow concern the variant reading «تَتْلُو»; the source prints «تَبْلُوا» here.]»
Al-Akhfash said: That is, it reads, as He said: ﴿وكُلَّ إنْسَانٍ ألْزَمْنَاه طَائِرهُ في عُنُقِهِ ونُخْرِجُ لَهُ يَوْمَ القِيَامَةِ كِتَاباً يَلْقَاهُ مَنْشُوراً. اقرَأْ كِتَابَكَ﴾.
The other view: that the meaning of ﴿تَبْلُواْ﴾ is "it follows", as [the poet] said:
* قَدْ جَعَلْتَ دَلْوِي تَسْتَتْلِيني *
(My bucket has begun to make me follow it.)

nahhas-meani:33-33.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَذَلِكَ حَقَّتْ كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ فَسَقُوۤاْ﴾.
Then He explained "the word" and said: ﴿أَنَّهُمْ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾. So the meaning is: it has become due against them that they will not believe [Translator's note: the anna-clause being a badal (substitute) for "the word"].
And it is possible that the meaning is: because they do not believe, and "the word" would be the punishment.

nahhas-meani:37-37.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْآنُ أَن يُفْتَرَىٰ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Its meaning is: «لأنْ يُفترى» (to be forged), that is, to be fabricated.
And it is possible that the meaning of ﴿وَمَا كَانَ هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْآنُ أَن يُفْتَرَىٰ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ﴾ is as you say: "This Qurʾān was not a lie" [Translator's note: the interpreted maṣdar being the khabar of kāna].
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَلَـٰكِن تَصْدِيقَ ٱلَّذِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ﴾.
It is possible that the meaning is: but the confirmation of the thing before which the Qurʾān is [i.e. that preceded it], that is, it confirms the scriptures and the reports of the nations that preceded it.
And it is possible that the meaning is: that it confirms what has not yet come of the matter of the Hour.

nahhas-meani:38-38.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَمْ يَقُولُونَ ٱفْتَرَاهُ قُلْ فَأْتُواْ بِسُورَةٍ مِّثْلِهِ﴾.
The meaning is: a sūra like its sūras, as in ﴿وَاسْأَلِ القَرْيَةَ﴾ [Translator's note: with a muḍāf omitted], the genus being meant.
And it was said: The meaning is: then bring a Qurʾān like this Qurʾān; and a sūra is Qurʾān, so He referred to it with the masculine [pronoun] according to the meaning; had it been according to the wording it would have been said «مثلِها».
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَٱدْعُواْ مَنِ ٱسْتَطَعْتُمْ مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ إِن كُنتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾.
That is: call whoever will help you, of those who follow your way, ﴿إِن كُنتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ that it is forged.

nahhas-meani:39-39.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿بَلْ كَذَّبُواْ بِمَا لَمْ يُحِيطُواْ بِعِلْمِهِ﴾.
It was said: By this is meant — and Allah knows best — whoever denies while in doubt.
And it was said: ﴿بِمَا لَمْ يُحِيطُواْ بِعِلْمِهِ﴾, that is, the threat it contains for their disbelief.
﴿وَلَمَّا يَأْتِهِمْ تَأْوِيلُهُ﴾: that is, what that threat leads to.
And it was said: ﴿وَلَمَّا يَأْتِهِمْ تَأْوِيلُهُ﴾, that is, they have not understood it; and this indicates that it is obligatory to look into interpretation.
And it is possible that the meaning is: and there has not yet come to them the punishment to which their affair leads.

nahhas-meani:40-40.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ وَمِنهُمْ مَّن يُؤْمِنُ بِهِ وَمِنْهُمْ مَّن لاَّ يُؤْمِنُ بِهِ وَرَبُّكَ أَعْلَمُ بِٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ﴾.
That is: among them is he who knows that it is true but displays disbelief out of obstinacy and to preserve his leadership, ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَّن لاَّ يُؤْمِنُ بِهِ﴾ in secret or in public.

nahhas-meani:42-42.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَّن يَسْتَمِعُونَ إِلَيْكَ أَفَأَنتَ تُسْمِعُ ٱلصُّمَّ..؟﴾.
That is: their outward appearance is the appearance of people who listen, but because of the intensity of their enmity and their turning away from the Prophet ﷺ they are in the position of the deaf.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَلَوْ كَانُواْ لاَ يَعْقِلُونَ﴾.
That is: even if, along with this, they are ignorant?!

nahhas-meani:43-43.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿ وَمِنهُمْ مَّن يَنظُرُ إِلَيْكَ أَفَأَنْتَ تَهْدِي ٱلْعُمْيَ وَلَوْ كَانُواْ لاَ يُبْصِرُونَ﴾.
﴿وَمِنهُمْ مَّن يَنظُرُ إِلَيْكَ﴾: that is, he keeps looking at you, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿يَنْظُرُونَ إلَيْكَ تَدُورُ أعْيُنُهُمْ كَالَّذِي يُغْشَى عَلَيْهِ مِنَ المَوْتِ﴾.

nahhas-meani:45-45.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَوْمَ يَحْشُرُهُمْ كَأَن لَّمْ يَلْبَثُوۤاْ إِلاَّ سَاعَةً مِّنَ ٱلنَّهَارِ﴾.
That is: what lies between their death and their resurrection is short. Then He said: ﴿يَتَعَارَفُونَ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾, that is, they recognise one another; and that is more severe for their rebuke, when they recognise one another [as partners] in misleading and corruption.

nahhas-meani:46-46.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِمَّا نُرِيَنَّكَ بَعْضَ ٱلَّذِي نَعِدُهُمْ أَوْ نَتَوَفَّيَنَّكَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, whether We show you the punishment in your lifetime ﴿أَوْ نَتَوَفَّيَنَّكَ﴾ before that, ﴿فَإِلَيْنَا مَرْجِعُهُمْ﴾.
[Someone else said: By His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He,] ﴿وَإِمَّا نُرِيَنَّكَ بَعْضَ ٱلَّذِي نَعِدُهُمْ﴾ He means the battle of Badr. And Allah knows best.

nahhas-meani:47-47.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ رَّسُولٌ فَإِذَا جَآءَ رَسُولُهُمْ قُضِيَ بَيْنَهُمْ بِٱلْقِسْطِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means the Day of Resurrection.
The meaning on this [view] is: when their messenger comes bearing witness against them as to belief and disbelief, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿فَكَيْفَ إذَا جِئنَا مِنْ كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ بِشَهِيدٍ﴾?
And He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَقَالَ الر‍َّسُولُ يَا رَبِّ إنَّ قَوْمِي اتَّخَذُوا هَذَا القُرْآنَ مَهْجُوراً﴾.
Someone other than Mujāhid said: It is possible [that the meaning is] that He does not punish anyone until the removal of excuse and the warning have come to him, and only the messengers bring this.

nahhas-meani:50-50.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ أَتَاكُمْ عَذَابُهُ بَيَاتاً أَوْ نَهَاراً مَّاذَا يَسْتَعْجِلُ مِنْهُ ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ﴾.
It is possible that the meaning is: what do they hasten of Allah [Translator's note: i.e. the pronoun refers to Allah].
And it is possible [that it is]: what of the punishment do the criminals hasten.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is closer to the meaning, because of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿أَثُمَّ إذَا مَا وَقَعَ آمَنْتُمْ بِهِ﴾?

nahhas-meani:51-51.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿الآنَ وَقَدْ كُنتُم بِهِ تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ﴾.
In the speech there is an omission, and the meaning is: Now you believe in it?

nahhas-meani:53-53.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَسْتَنْبِئُونَكَ أَحَقٌّ هُوَ﴾.
The meaning is: and they ask you for information, saying: Is it true?
﴿قُلْ إِي وَرَبِّيۤ إِنَّهُ لَحَقٌّ﴾: that is, the meaning [of إِي] is "yes".
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَآ أَنتُمْ بِمُعْجِزِينَ﴾.
That is: you are not among those who can escape being requited for their disbelief.

nahhas-meani:54-54.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَسَرُّواْ ٱلنَّدَامَةَ لَمَّا رَأَوُاْ ٱلْعَذَابَ﴾.
There are two views on its meaning:
One of them: that the chiefs who called to disbelief concealed their regret when they saw the punishment.
The other: that ﴿أَسَرُّواْ﴾ means "they showed".
Abū al-ʿAbbās said: If this is correct, then its meaning is: regret appeared in the lines (asirra) of their faces; its singular is «سِرار», and they are the lines in the forehead.

nahhas-meani:57-57.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ قَدْ جَآءَتْكُمْ مَّوْعِظَةٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ﴾.
He means the Qurʾān.

nahhas-meani:58-58.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ بِفَضْلِ ٱللَّهِ وَبِرَحْمَتِهِ فَبِذَلِكَ فَلْيَفْرَحُواْ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: His bounty is Islam, and His mercy is the Qurʾān.
Abū al-Tayyāḥ said: ﴿بِفَضْلِ ٱللَّهِ﴾ means Islam, ﴿وَبِرَحْمَتِهِ﴾ means the Qurʾān, ﴿فَبِذَلِكَ فَلْيَفْرَحُواْ﴾ O Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ, ﴿هُوَ خَيْرٌ مِّمَّا يَجْمَعُونَ﴾ — he said: meaning the disbelievers.
ʿIkrima narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿بِفَضْلِ ٱللَّهِ﴾ is the Qurʾān, ﴿وَبِرَحْمَتِهِ﴾ is that He made us among its people.

nahhas-meani:59-59.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ مَّآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ مِّن رِّزْقٍ فَجَعَلْتُمْ مِّنْهُ حَرَاماً وَحَلاَلاً﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means the baḥīras and the sāʾibas [animals the pagans dedicated and forbade].
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: He means [what is in] His saying ﴿وَجَعَلُوا للهِ مِمَّا ذَرَأَ مِنَ الحَرْثِ وَالأَنْعَامِ نَصِيباً﴾.

nahhas-meani:61-61.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا تَكُونُ فِي شَأْنٍ وَمَا تَتْلُواْ مِنْهُ مِن قُرْآنٍ وَلاَ تَعْمَلُونَ مِنْ عَمَلٍ إِلاَّ كُنَّا عَلَيْكُمْ شُهُوداً إِذْ تُفِيضُونَ فِيهِ﴾.
The meaning of ﴿وَمَا تَكُونُ فِي شَأْنٍ﴾ is: whatever time you are engaged in an affair, of worship or otherwise. ﴿وَمَا تَتْلُواْ مِنْهُ مِن قُرْآنٍ﴾: Abū Isḥāq said: The meaning is: from the affair [Translator's note: i.e. the pronoun in مِنْهُ refers to «الشأن»].
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِذْ تُفِيضُونَ فِيهِ﴾.
That is: you engage in it; and from it is «أَفَاضَ في الحديث» (he launched into the talk).
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا يَعْزُبُ عَن رَّبِّكَ مِن مِّثْقَالِ ذَرَّةٍ﴾.
That is: nothing is far or absent [from Him].
«مثقال الشيء» is its weight, and «الذرّة» is the small ant.

nahhas-meani:62-62.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَلاۤ إِنَّ أَوْلِيَآءَ ٱللَّهِ لاَ خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلاَ هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ﴾.
It is narrated that a man said to the Prophet ﷺ: Who are the friends (awliyāʾ) of Allah? He said: "Those who, when they are seen, Allah is remembered."
"Abū Jaʿfar narrated to us; he said: al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUmar al-Kūfī narrated to us in Baghdad; he said: al-ʿAlāʾ ibn ʿAmr narrated to us; he said: Yaḥyā ibn al-Yamān narrated to us, from Ashʿath ibn Isḥāq al-Qummī, from Jaʿfar ibn Abī al-Mughīra, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ: ﴿أَلاۤ إِنَّ أَوْلِيَآءَ ٱللَّهِ لاَ خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلاَ هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ﴾ — he said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is remembered at the sight of them."

nahhas-meani:64-64.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَهُمُ ٱلْبُشْرَىٰ فِي ٱلْحَياةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَفِي ٱلآخِرَةِ﴾.
ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿لَهُمُ ٱلْبُشْرَىٰ فِي ٱلْحَياةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَفِي ٱلآخِرَةِ﴾, and he said: "It is the righteous dream which the Muslim sees, or which is seen for him; and in the Hereafter: Paradise."
There is another view on it, which Shuʿba narrated from Ibn ʿImrān al-Jawnī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ṣāmit, from Abū Dharr: I said to the Prophet ﷺ: "A man does a good deed for himself, and people love him for it. He said: That is the believers' glad tidings hastened in this world." «[Translator's note: the narrator is usually named Abū ʿImrān al-Jawnī; the source has «ابن عمران».]»
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لاَ تَبْدِيلَ لِكَلِمَاتِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
That is: there is no breaking of His promise.
And it was said: The meaning of ﴿لاَ تَبْدِيلَ لِكَلِمَاتِ ٱللَّهِ﴾ is: there is no changing His reports, that is, nothing abrogates them, and they will only be as He said.

nahhas-meani:65-65.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ يَحْزُنكَ قَوْلُهُمْ﴾.
That is: let not their threats, their denial and their arrogance towards you grieve you.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلْعِزَّةَ للَّهِ جَمِيعاً﴾.
That is: dominance belongs to Allah.

nahhas-meani:66-66.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا يَتَّبِعُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ شُرَكَآءَ إِن يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلاَّ ٱلظَّنَّ وَإِنْ هُمْ إِلاَّ يَخْرُصُونَ﴾.
That is: they guess and conjecture.

nahhas-meani:67-67.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هُوَ ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلْلَّيْلَ لِتَسْكُنُواْ فِيهِ وَٱلنَّهَارَ مُبْصِراً﴾.
That is: [a day] in which one sees, by way of attribution (ʿalā al-nasab), as He said: ﴿فِي عِيشَةٍ رَاضِيَةٍ﴾, that is, possessing contentment, that is, one is content with it.

nahhas-meani:68-68.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنْ عِندَكُمْ مِّن سُلْطَانٍ بِهَـٰذَآ﴾.
That is: you have no proof for this.

nahhas-meani:69-69.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿قُلْ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَفْتَرُونَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ ٱلْكَذِبَ لاَ يُفْلِحُونَ﴾.
The statement is complete [here].
Then He said: ﴿مَتَاعٌ فِي الدُّنْيَا﴾, that is: that is an enjoyment in this world [Translator's note: مَتَاعٌ being the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ].

nahhas-meani:71-71.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَجْمِعُوۤاْ أَمْرَكُمْ وَشُرَكَآءَكُمْ﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ said: Its meaning is: and call your partners. He said: «الإجماع» is preparing and resolving upon a matter.
Abū al-ʿAbbās [al-Mubarrad] said: It is construed according to the meaning, because the meaning of «أَجْمِعُوا» and «اجْمَعُوا» is one.
Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: The meaning is: together with your partners [Translator's note: i.e. a wāw of accompaniment, شركاءكم being mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment)]. He said: Al-Farrāʾ's view has no sense, because if he holds that the meaning is "and call your partners to help you", then its meaning is the meaning of «مع» (with); and if he holds it is calling only, then there is no sense in calling them for nothing.
Al-Jaḥdarī read — and it is also narrated from al-Aʿraj — ﴿فَاجْمَعُوا أمْرَكُمْ﴾ with a connecting alif and fatḥa on the mīm.
Al-Ḥasan read: ﴿فَأَجْمِعُوۤاْ أَمْرَكُمْ وَشُرَكَاؤُكُمْ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This indicates that they are two dialectal forms with one meaning.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ لاَ يَكُنْ أَمْرُكُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ غُمَّةً﴾.
There are two views on it:
One of them: that the meaning of «غُمَّة» is like the meaning of «غَمّ» (grief).
The other — and it is sounder linguistically — is that the meaning is: let your affair be manifest. It is said: «القومُ في غُمَّة» when their affair is obscure to them and confused; and from this is «غُمَّ الهلالُ على الناس», that is, something covered it and concealed it.
And «الغَمّ» (grief) from this is only the distress that covers the heart and constricts it; and the origin of this is derived from «الغَمامة» (the cloud).
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ ٱقْضُوۤاْ إِلَيَّ وَلاَ تُنظِرُونَ﴾.
That is: then do whatever seems good to you.
Al-Kisāʾī said: And it is read ﴿وأفْضُوا إلَيَّ﴾ with a disjunctive alif (hamzat qaṭʿ) and with fāʾ.

nahhas-meani:78-78.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالُوۤاْ أَجِئْتَنَا لِتَلْفِتَنَا عَمَّا وَجَدْنَا عَلَيْهِ آبَاءَنَا﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, to twist us away.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is well known in the language. It is said: «لَفَتَهُ يَلْفِتُه» when he turned him aside. And from this is «التفت» (he turned round): it is only turning aside from the direction in front of him.
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَتَكُونَ لَكُمَا ٱلْكِبْرِيَآءُ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, sovereignty; and that is well known in the language. Sovereignty was called «كبرياء» (grandeur) only because it is the greatest thing attained in this world.

nahhas-meani:81-81.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلَمَّآ أَلْقُواْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ مَا جِئْتُمْ بِهِ ٱلسِّحْرُ﴾.
Whoever read ﴿آلسِّحْرُ﴾, its meaning for him is rebuke, that is: What is it that you have brought — is it magic?

nahhas-meani:83-83.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَمَآ آمَنَ لِمُوسَىٰ إِلاَّ ذُرِّيَّةٌ مِّن قَوْمِهِ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: That is, a few.
Mujāhid said: He means that none of them [the elders] believed in him; only their children believed.
Some of the people of language said: They were called "offspring" only because their fathers were Copts and their mothers were from the Children of Israel, just as those [of Persian descent] who ended up in Yemen from Persia were called "al-Abnāʾ" (the sons); he takes them to be men who are [specifically] referred to [by this name].
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿عَلَىٰ خَوْفٍ مِّن فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَئِهِمْ أَن يَفْتِنَهُمْ﴾.
He said «ومَلَئِهِمْ» (and their chiefs) [with a plural pronoun] because it is known that with him were those who obeyed his orders and referred to his word.
And it was said: The meaning is: in fear of the family of Pharaoh.

nahhas-meani:86-86.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿رَبَّنَا لاَ تَجْعَلْنَا فِتْنَةً لِّلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّالِمِينَ. وَنَجِّنَا بِرَحْمَتِكَ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلْكَافِرِينَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, do not destroy us at the hands of our enemies, nor punish us with a punishment from You, so that our enemies would say: Had they been in the right, we would not have been given power over them and they would not have been punished — that is, so that they would be tempted [further] by that.
Abū Mijlaz said: [That is,] let them not prevail and so think that they are better than us.

nahhas-meani:87-87.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱجْعَلُواْ بُيُوتَكُمْ قِبْلَةً﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: That is, places of prayer.
Mujāhid said: That is, facing the Kaʿba.
Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī said: They were in fear, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, informed, so they were commanded to pray in their houses so that no harm would reach them.

nahhas-meani:88-88.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ رَبَّنَآ إِنَّكَ آتَيْتَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلأَهُ زِينَةً وَأَمْوَالاً فِي ٱلْحَيَاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا رَبَّنَا لِيُضِلُّواْ عَن سَبِيلِكَ﴾. «وَلِيُضِلُّوا».
