The interpreted maṣdar (أن يؤمنوا) is conjoined to a maṣdar extracted from the preceding supplication, i.e. "let there be from You a hardening upon their hearts, and so a lack of faith from them".
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يروا..) is in the position of genitive by (حتّى), attached to (اشدد).
The clause «قال موسى ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause أوحينا إلى موسى ...
The clause «the vocative and its response» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl (object of speech) «1».
The clause «إنّك آتيت ...» has no grammatical position; response to the vocative.
The clause «آتيت فرعون ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of inna.
The clause «the second vocative» has no grammatical position; parenthetical.
The clause «يضلّوا» has no grammatical position; ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «ربّنا.. the third» has no grammatical position; resumptive within the scope of the speech «2».
The clause «اطمس ...» has no grammatical position; response to the third vocative.
The clause «اشدد ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause اطمس.
The clause «يؤمنوا ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila of the second implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «يروا ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila of the third implied particle relative (أن).

safi-cedvel:89-89.t:
* I'rab:
(قال) a past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "he", i.e. Allah. (قد) a particle of realization (taḥqīq). (أجيبت) a passive past verb. And (التاء) for the feminine. (دعوة) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ), and (كما) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (الفاء) conjunction, for linking the effect to the cause. (استقيما) an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn.. and (الألف) an attached pronoun in the position of nominative as fāʿil. (الواو) conjunction. (لا) prohibitive, making jussive. (تتّبعانّ) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and the sign of the jussive is the dropping of the nūn, as it is one of the five verbs.. and (الألف) is fāʿil, and (النون) is the heavy nūn of emphasis [Note: The verb attributed to the alif of the dual, the wāw of the plural or the yāʾ of the feminine addressee, when the nūn of emphasis enters it, is declinable (muʿrab), and the nūn is doubled with kasra when with the alif of the dual. Also, (لا) may be negative, the verb then being nominative by the retention of the nūn, which has been dropped because of the succession of like letters.. and the clause is resumptive.], (سبيل) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb). (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. (لا) negative. (يعلمون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is an attached pronoun in the position of nominative as fāʿil.
The clause «قال ...» has no position [Translator's note: the source has «لا محلّ» without «لها»]; an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «أجيبت دعوتكما» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «استقيما» has no grammatical position; conjoined to an implied resumptive clause, i.e. "take heed, and so stand firm"...
The clause «لا تتّبعانّ ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause استقيما.
The clause «لا يعلمون» has no grammatical position; ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).

* Morphology:
(دعوة), an aural (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb دعا يدعو, in the sense of الدعاء (supplication); its pattern is فعلة, with fatḥa then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
Variation in address (al-tanwīʿ fī al-khiṭāb): the Glorified One varied in addressing them: first He used the dual, then the plural, then finally the singular. The secret in that is that Mūsā and Hārūn were addressed to settle houses for their people and to choose them for worship; then the address was made general, to them both and to their people, to take places of prostration for praying in them, because that is obligatory on the generality; then finally Mūsā was singled out for the glad tidings, which are the loftiest aim, out of exaltation of them and of the one who gives them.

* Benefits:
- Emphasizing the verb with the nūn:
In this verse there occurs His saying, Exalted is He, وَلا تَتَّبِعانِّ سَبِيلَ الَّذِينَ لا يَعْلَمُونَ. The verb (وَلا تَتَّبِعانِّ) has had the heavy nūn of emphasis enter upon its end. This nūn enters the imperfect and the imperative, and does not enter the past. There is a precise rule in emphasizing the verb, which we will explain in what follows:
1- If the imperfect is attributed to an overt noun or to the pronoun of the singular, what precedes the nūn takes fatḥa, whether the verb is sound or defective, so we say: لينصرنّ علي and ليدعونّ, and ليرمينّ, and ليسعينّ.
2- If it is attributed to the alif of the dual, the nūn of emphasis takes kasra after the alif, so we say:
لينصرنّ, and ليدعوانّ, and ليرميانّ, and ليسعيانّ. [Translator's note: the first example is printed «لينصرنّ»; the dual form would be «لينصرانّ».]
3- If it is attributed to the wāw of the plural, what precedes the nūn takes ḍamma, and the last letter of the defective verb is dropped absolutely, and the wāw of the plural is also dropped, except in the verb weak with alif, where it remains, vowelled with a vowel congruent with it, so we say:
لينصرنّ, and ليدعنّ, and ليرمنّ, and ليسعونّ.
4- If it is attributed to the yāʾ of the feminine addressee, what precedes the nūn takes kasra, and the last letter of the defective verb is dropped absolutely, and the yāʾ of the feminine addressee is also dropped, except in the verb weak with alif, where it remains with a vowel congruent with it, so you say: لتنصرنّ, and لتدعنّ, and لترمنّ, and لتسعينّ.
5- If it is attributed to the nūn of the feminine plural, an alif is added between the two nūns and the nūn of emphasis takes kasra, so you say: لينصرنانّ, ليدعونانّ, ليرمينانّ, ليسعينانّ. And the imperative is like the imperfect in that, so you say: انصرنّ, ادعونّ, ارمينّ, اسعينّ, and so on.

safi-cedvel:51-51.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for the interrogative; (ثمّ) conjunction; (إذا) adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (آمنتم); (ما) redundant (zāʾida); (وقع) past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is «هو», i.e. the punishment; (آمنتم) past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, with its fāʿil; (الباء) preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (آمنتم), and the pronoun refers to Allah; (الهمزة) for the interrogative; (الآن) adverb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being «تؤمنون» (you believe); (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (قد) particle of verification (taḥqīq); (كنتم) defective past verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — indeclinable on the sukūn.. and (تم) is a pronoun, the noun of kāna; (به) like the first one, attached to (تستعجلون) by its being made to include the meaning of «تكذبون» (you deny); (تستعجلون) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).. and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The clause «the condition, its verb and its apodosis ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «أرأيتم» [Note: in the previous verse (50).].
The clause «وقع ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «آمنتم به ...» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «الآن (تؤمنون) ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «كنتم به تستعجلون» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of «تؤمنون».
The clause «تستعجلون» is in the position of the accusative as the khabar (predicate) of «كنتم».

* Morphology:
(الآن): the interrogative hamza was merged with the connective hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) of the definite article (ال) into a single alif with a madda over it, and such is the case with every connective hamza of the definite article (ال) when it is preceded by a hamza. It is said that this merging is obligatory, and it is said that it is permissible, by dropping the connective hamza entirely and keeping the interrogative hamza. Six places of this kind occur in the Qur'an in which the two alifs were merged.. two in al-Anʿām, namely (الذكرين) [Note: in verses (143) and (144).] twice, and three in this sura, namely (الآن) here [Note: and in verse (91).], and the word (الله) [Note: in verse (60) of this sura.], and the word (الله) in Surat al-Naml [Note: in verse (59).].

safi-cedvel:52-52.t:
* I'rab:
(ثمّ) conjunction; (قيل) past verb, passive (mabnī lil-majhūl); (اللام) preposition; (الذين) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (قيل); (ظلموا) past verb with its fāʿil (agent); (ذوقوا) imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil; (عذاب) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (الخلد) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (هل) interrogative particle in the sense of negation; (تجزون) imperfect verb, passive, nominative (marfūʿ).. and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (إلّا) particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (الباء) preposition of causation; (ما) maṣdar-forming particle; (كنتم) like the preceding one «1»; (تكسبون) like «تستعجلون» «2». [Translator's note: «1» and «2» are cross-reference markers left in the source; they refer to the parsing of (كنتم) and (تستعجلون) in the previous verse (51).]
The interpreted maṣdar (ما كنتم) is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, attached to the verb «تجزون» [Note: it is permissible for (ما) to be a relative noun, the clause being its ṣila (relative clause), with the referring pronoun omitted.].
The clause «قيل ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the resumptive clause «الآن (تؤمنون)» [Note: in the previous verse (51).. or it is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to that same clause if it is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl) of an omitted verb of saying.].
The clause «ظلموا» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «ذوقوا ...» is in the position of the nominative as the nāʾib fāʿil.
The clause «تجزون ...» has no grammatical position, having the status of a causal explanation (taʿlīl).
The clause «كنتم تكسبون» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative (ما).
The clause «تكسبون» is in the position of the accusative as the khabar (predicate) of «كنتم».

* Rhetoric:
Implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «ذُوقُوا عَذابَ الْخُلْدِ», i.e. the painful one, perpetually.

safi-cedvel:53-53.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (يستنبئون) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and (الكاف) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (الهمزة) for the interrogative; (حقّ) fronted khabar (predicate), nominative [Note: or a mubtadaʾ (subject) relying on an interrogative, with (هو) as the fāʿil of the maṣdar, standing in place of the khabar.]; (هو) detached pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative as a postponed mubtadaʾ; (قل) imperative verb, and the fāʿil is «أنت»; (إي) particle of answer; (الواو) the wāw of oath; (ربّ) genitive (majrūr) by the wāw, the sign of the genitive being the kasra implied (muqaddar) on its end, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied verb «أقسم» (I swear), and (الياء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (إنّ) particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — and (الهاء) is a pronoun in the position of the accusative as the noun of inna; (اللام) the lām of oath [Note: it is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) in contexts other than an oath.]; (حقّ) khabar of inna, nominative; (الواو) conjunctive; (ما) negative, functioning like laysa; (أنتم) detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as the noun of «ما»; (الباء) redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (معجزين) genitive in form, accusative in position, as the khabar of «ما», the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «يستنبئونك ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «حقّ هو» is in the position of the accusative as the second mafʿūl bihi of the verb «يستنبئون», which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «(أقسم) بربّي ..» is in the position of the accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «إنّه لحقّ» has no grammatical position, being the answer to the oath.
The clause «ما أنتم بمعجزين» has no grammatical position, being conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the answer to the oath.

* Benefits:
- «إي» with kasra and sukūn:
In this verse there occurs the saying of Allah the Exalted قُلْ إِي وَرَبِّي إِنَّهُ لَحَقٌّ, where (إي) is a particle of answer. We will set out what Ibn Hishām related about it:
It is a particle of answer meaning «نعم» (yes), so it serves to confirm the one who informs, to inform the one who asks, and to promise the one who requests; so it occurs after: «قام زيد» (Zayd stood), «هل قام زيد» (did Zayd stand?), «اضرب زيدا» (strike Zayd) and the like, just as «نعم» occurs after them. Ibn al-Ḥājib claimed that it occurs after the interrogative, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted وَيَسْتَنْبِئُونَكَ أَحَقٌّ هُوَ قُلْ إِي وَرَبِّي إِنَّهُ لَحَقٌّ, and according to all of them it occurs only before an oath, as in the verse «إِي وَرَبِّي». [Translator's note: in Ibn Hishām's Mughnī, Ibn al-Ḥājib's claim is that it occurs only after the interrogative; the source here does not include the word «إنما» (only).]

safi-cedvel:54-54.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (لو) non-jussive conditional particle; (أنّ) particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh); (لكلّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, fronted khabar (predicate); (نفس) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (ظلمت) past verb.. and (التاء) is for the feminine, and the fāʿil (agent) is «هي», i.e. every soul; (ما) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative as the postponed noun of anna; (في الأرض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted [word], the ṣila (relative clause) of «ما».
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ لكلّ ... ما في الأرض) is in the position of the nominative as the fāʿil of an omitted verb, its implied form being «ثبت» (it were established), i.e. the existence [of ...] were established..
(اللام) occurring in the apodosis of «لو»; (افتدت) like «ظلمت»; (الباء) preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (افتدت); (الواو) conjunctive; (أسرّوا) past verb with its fāʿil; (الندامة) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (لمّا) adverb meaning «حين» (when), containing the meaning of condition, in the position of the accusative, attached to the implied apodosis; (رأوا) past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.. and the wāw is the fāʿil; (العذاب) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الواو) conjunctive; (قضي ... لا يظلمون) its i'rab has already passed [Note: in verse (47) of this sura.].
The clause «(ثبت) امتلاك ما في الأرض» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «ظلمت ...» is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of «نفس».
The clause «افتدت» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «أسرّوا ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the resumptive clause [Note: or resumptive, if the concealing takes place in the Hereafter.].
The clause «رأوا ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.. and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.
The clause «قضي بينهم ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «هم لا يظلمون» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
The clause «لا يظلمون» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (هم).

safi-cedvel:55-55.t:
* I'rab:
(ألا) particle of alerting (tanbīh); (إنّ) particle resembling the verb; (لله) a preposition and its genitive noun, fronted khabar (predicate); (ما) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative as the noun of inna; (في السموات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted [word], the ṣila (relative clause) of «ما»; (الواو) conjunctive; (الأرض) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «السموات», genitive (majrūr); (ألا إنّ) like the first; (وعد) noun of inna, accusative (manṣūb); (الله) the Divine Name, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive; (حقّ) khabar of inna, nominative (marfūʿ); (الواو) conjunctive; (لكنّ) like «إنّ»; (أكثر) noun of lākinna, accusative, and (هم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (لا) negative; (يعلمون) imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent).
The clause «إنّ لله ما في السموات» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «إنّ وعد الله حقّ» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «لكنّ أكثرهم ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «إنّ وعد الله حقّ».
The clause «لا يعلمون» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of lākinna.

safi-cedvel:56-56.t:
* I'rab:
(هو) detached pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (يحيي) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, and the fāʿil (agent) is «هو»; (الواو) conjunctive; (يميت) like «يحيي»; (الواو) conjunctive; (إلى) preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ترجعون), which is an imperfect verb, passive, nominative, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The clause «هو يحيي ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يحيي ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ «هو».
The clause «يميت ...» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the khabar clause.
The clause «ترجعون» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.

safi-cedvel:57-57.t:
* I'rab:
(يا) vocative particle; (أيّ) the one addressed (munādā), a specified indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative, and (ها) is a particle of alerting (tanbīh); (الناس) badal (substitute) of «أيّ», following it in the nominative in form — or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition); (قد) particle of verification (taḥqīq); (جاءت) past verb.. and (التاء) is for the feminine, and (كم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (موعظة) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); (من ربّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «موعظة» [Note: or attached to (جاءتكم) if (من) is for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya).. and the construction is figurative.], and (كم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الواو) conjunctive; (شفاء) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «موعظة», nominative; (اللام) preposition; (ما) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, attached to a naʿt of «شفاء» [Note: this is if (شفاء) is a noun meaning «دواء» (remedy).. and if it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), then (اللام) is redundant (zāʾida), for strengthening, and (ما) is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi of «شفاء».]; (في الصدور) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted [word], the ṣila (relative clause) of «ما»; (الواو) conjunctive in both places; (هدى، رحمة) two nouns conjoined by the two conjunctions to «موعظة», nominative, the sign of the nominative in (هدى) being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif; (للمؤمنين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «رحمة», the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «the vocative يأيّها ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «جاءتكم موعظة ...» has no grammatical position, being the response to the vocative.

* Morphology:
(شفاء): a transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb «شفى يشفي», of the pattern-class «ضرب»; it was then made into a descriptive for intensiveness, or it is a noun for that which heals, like «الدواء» (medicine). Its pattern is «فعال» with kasra on the fāʾ. It contains iʿlāl or ibdāl (substitution) by changing the weak letter into a hamza; its original form is «شفاي», and when the yāʾ came at the end after a quiescent alif it was changed into a hamza.

* Benefits:
In this verse there occurs the saying of Allah the Exalted قَدْ جاءَتْكُمْ مَوْعِظَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ وَشِفاءٌ لِما فِي الصُّدُورِ وَهُدىً وَرَحْمَةٌ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ. Here we are concerned with the noun (هدى): it is conjoined to «موعظة» and nominative like it, by the ḍamma implied on the alif, which is dropped in pronunciation because of the tanwīn but kept in writing. Someone might imagine that the tanwīn on the alif is a case vowel, but it is not so; rather, it is an indication of the dropped alif. To clarify this point we say: when the maqṣūr noun (the noun ending in alif) is devoid of definition by «أل» and devoid of annexation (iḍāfa), it takes tanwīn in all cases of i'rab, and the vowels are implied on its alif, which is dropped because of the tanwīn. It is known that this alif is dropped in pronunciation and kept in writing, but in i'rab we consider it dropped. If, however, the maqṣūr noun does not take tanwīn — that being when it comes annexed (muḍāf) or defined by «أل» — then we parse it with vowels implied on the alif, whose appearance is prevented by impossibility (taʿadhdhur).

safi-cedvel:90-92.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (جاوزنا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn..
and (نا) a pronoun in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent). (ببني) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (جاوزنا) [Note: The bāʾ here is for transitivity (taʿdiya), i.e.: We made the Children of Israel cross the sea.], and the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ, as it is assimilated to the sound masculine plural. (إسرائيل) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), and the sign of the genitive is the fatḥa. (البحر) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb). (الفاء) conjunction. (أتبع) a past verb, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (فرعون) fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ), and it is barred from nunation because of being a proper name and foreign. (جنود) conjoined to فرعون by the wāw, nominative, and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi. (بغيا) mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), accusative [Note: Or it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "transgressing".], (عدوا) conjoined to (بغيا) by the wāw, accusative. (حتى) a particle of inception (ibtidāʾ). (إذا) an adverb of future time containing the sense of condition, in the position of accusative, attached to (قال), (أدرك) a past verb, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (الغرق) fāʿil, nominative. (قال) like أدرك, and the fāʿil is "he". (آمنت) a past verb and its fāʿil. (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb, abrogating (nāsikh) — for emphasis — and (الهاء) the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), in the position of accusative as the noun of anna. (لا) the lā of generic negation. (إله) the noun of lā, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative, and the khabar (predicate) of lā is omitted, its implied form being "existent" or "worshipped in truth". (إلّا) a particle of exception. (الذي) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as badal (substitute) from the pronoun latent in the khabar [Note: It is parsed as badal because the clause before the particle of exception is negated.. And the relative may be in the position of accusative as excepted.] (آمنت) a past verb.. and (التاء) for the feminine. (الباء) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (آمنت), (بنو) fāʿil, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the wāw, as it is assimilated to the sound masculine plural. (إسرائيل) like the first.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّه لا إله ...) is in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, attached to (آمنت), i.e.: "I believed in that there is no god except ...".
(الواو) conjunction. (أنا) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). (من المسلمين) a preposition and its genitive noun, khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ.
The clause «جاوزنا ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «أتبعهم فرعون ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause جاوزنا.
The clause «أدركه الغرق» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position; apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «آمنت ...» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «لا إله إلّا ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of anna.
The clause «آمنت به بنو ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذي).
The clause «أنا من المسلمين» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the maqūl al-qawl clause.
(الهمزة) for reproachful interrogation. (الآن) an adverb of time, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being تؤمن ("do you believe"). (الواو) the wāw of ḥāl. (قد) a particle of realization (taḥqīq). (عصيت) like آمنت. (قبل) an adverb, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of accusative, attached to (عصيت), (الواو) conjunction. (كنت) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb.. and (التاء) a pronoun, the noun of kāna, in the position of nominative. (من المفسدين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar of kāna, and the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ.
The clause «(تؤمن) الآن ...» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl of an implied saying, which is an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «قد عصيت» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl from the fāʿil in (تؤمن).
The clause «كنت من المفسدين» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the ḥāl clause.
(الفاء) conjunction. (اليوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (ننجيك), which is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi.. and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "We", for majesty. (ببدن) a preposition and its genitive noun, ḥāl from the pronoun of address, and (الكاف) muḍāf ilayhi. (اللام) for cause (taʿlīl). (تكون) an incomplete imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām of cause, and its noun is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you". (اللام) a preposition. (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to a ḥāl from آية — a naʿt (adjective) placed before the noun it qualifies — (آية) khabar of takūn, accusative. And (خلف) an adverb, accusative, attached to an omitted ṣila of من, and (الكاف) like the last.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تكون) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (ننجيك).
(الواو) parenthetical. (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb — abrogating — (كثيرا) the noun of inna, accusative. (من الناس) a preposition and its genitive noun, naʿt of (كثيرا), (عن آيات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (غافلون), and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (اللام) it is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), conveying emphasis. (غافلون) khabar of inna, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the wāw.
The clause «ننجيك ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the maqūl al-qawl clause.
The clause «تكون ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila of the implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «إنّ كثيرا من الناس ...» has no grammatical position; a parenthetical tail-clause (iʿtirāḍ tadhyīlī) to confirm the reported speech.

* Morphology:
(الغرق), an aural (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb غرق يغرق, of the class of فرح; its pattern is فعل, with two fatḥas.

* Rhetoric:
Double entendre (al-tawriya): in His saying, Exalted is He, «فَالْيَوْمَ نُنَجِّيكَ بِبَدَنِكَ», if بدن is interpreted as the coat of mail. But if it is interpreted as the body, the meaning is: We shall save you in the state in which there is no spirit in you, and you are only a body. As for interpreting بدن as the coat of mail, the saying of ʿAmr ibn Maʿdī Karib indicates it:
أعاذل شكّتي بدني وسيفي ... وكلّ مقلّص سلس القياد
(O you who reproach me, my weapons are my coat of mail and my sword, and every lean, tightly-girthed horse, easy to lead.)
Pharaoh had a coat of mail of gold by which he was known, and so tawriya is valid in البدن: in its near, apparent sense, البدن means the body, and in its far, hidden sense it means the coat of mail, and the hidden sense is the one intended; for Pharaoh's being saved — i.e. his coming out of the sea after drowning — with his coat of mail is a more wondrous sign than his coming out bare. Tawriya, briefly, is: that the speaker mentions a single word that has two meanings: a near, apparent one that is not intended, and a far, hidden one that is the intended one.

safi-cedvel:93-93.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (اللام) the lām of oath, for an implied oath. (قد) a particle of realization (taḥqīq). (بوأنا) like جاوزنا «1», (بني) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ. (إسرائيل) like the previous one «2», (مبوّأ) mafʿūl bihi, accusative [Note: By making (بوّأ) contain the sense of أنزل ("to lodge").. And it may be a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), on the basis that it is a mīmī maṣdar..
Or it is an adverb attached to (بوّأنا), on the basis that it is a noun of place.], (صدق) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr). (الواو) conjunction. (رزقنا) like جاوزنا «4», and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (من الطيّبات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (رزقنا). (الفاء) conjunction. (ما) negative. (اختلفوا) a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). (حتى) a particle of limit (ghāya) and a preposition. (جاء) a past verb, and (هم) like the last. (العلم) fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ). (إنّ ربّ) like إنّ كثيرا [Note: In verse (92) of this sura.], and (الكاف) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (يقضي) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, and the fāʿil is "he". (بين) an adverb, accusative, attached to (يقضي), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (يقضي), (القيامة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (في) a preposition. (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive, attached to (يقضي), (كانوا) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb — abrogating (nāsikh) — and the wāw is the noun of kāna. (في) like the first, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (يختلفون), which is an imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is fāʿil. The interpreted maṣdar (أن جاءهم) is in the position of genitive, attached to (اختلفوا).
The clause «بوّأنا ...» has no grammatical position; response to an implied oath.
The clause «رزقناهم..» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause of the response to the oath.
The clause «ما اختلفوا ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause رزقناهم.
The clause «جاءهم العلم» has no grammatical position; ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «إنّ ربك يقضي ...» has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumptive clause.
The clause «يقضي ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of inna.
The clause «كانوا فيه يختلفون» has no grammatical position; ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «يختلفون» is in the position of accusative as khabar of kānū.

* Morphology:
(مبوّأ), a mīmī maṣdar (verbal noun) — or a noun of place — and it is valid to take both considerations in the verse.. Its pattern is مفعّل, with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:94-94.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive. (إن) a conditional particle that makes jussive. (كنت) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).. and (التاء) is the noun of kāna. (في شكّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, khabar (predicate) of kunta. (من) a preposition. (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of شكّ. (أنزلنا) like جاوزنا [Note: In verse (90) of this sura.
(2, 3) in the previous verse (93).], (إلى) a preposition and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أنزلنا), (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (اسأل) an imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "you". (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (يقرءون) like يختلفون «2», (الكتاب) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb). (من قبل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يقرءون), and (الكاف) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (لقد جاء) like بوّأنا, indeclinable on the fatḥa «3», and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (الحقّ) fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ). (من ربّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (جاء). (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition. (لا) prohibitive, making jussive. (تكوننّ) an incomplete imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of jussive ... and (النون) is the nūn of emphasis, and its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "you". (من الممترين) a preposition and its genitive noun, khabar of takūnanna, and the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ.
The clause «كنت في شكّ....» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «أنزلنا» has no grammatical position; ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).
The clause «اسأل ...» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «يقرءون ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila of the relative (الذين).
The clause «جاءك الحقّ ...» has no grammatical position; response to an implied oath.
The clause «لا تكوننّ من الممترين» has no grammatical position; apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you have grasped it, then do not be ...".

* Benefits:
Does the Messenger of Allah ﷺ doubt what was sent down to him? Regarding this verse a question and an objection have been raised. It is to say: did the Prophet ﷺ doubt what was sent down to him concerning his prophethood, so that he should ask?
And if he were doubtful of his own prophethood, others would be more worthy of doubt than him. The answer to this question is what al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said in his book al-Shifāʾ: "Beware — may Allah make your heart firm — lest there occur to your mind what some exegetes have mentioned from Ibn ʿAbbās or others, of affirming this doubt of the Prophet ﷺ — regarding what was revealed to him — on the ground that he is a human being; for the like of this is not possible for him ﷺ at all. Rather, Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Prophet ﷺ did not doubt, and did not ask. And similar is reported from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī.
And it is related from Qatāda that he said: It has reached us that the Prophet ﷺ [Translator's note: the source has «صلّى عليه وآله وسلم», with the word «الله» missing] said, when this verse was revealed: I do not doubt and I do not ask. And the generality of the exegetes hold this." The speech of al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, ends here. Then they differed regarding the meaning of the verse and who is addressed, holding two views. One of them is that the address is to the Prophet ﷺ outwardly, while someone else is meant by it; so it is like His saying (لَئِنْ أَشْرَكْتَ لَيَحْبَطَنَّ عَمَلُكَ), and it is known that the Prophet ﷺ did not associate partners, so it is established that someone else is meant by it.
And among the proverbs of the Arabs is «إياك أعني واسمعي يا جارة» ("It is you I mean, but listen, O neighbour-woman"). What indicates the soundness of this interpretation is His saying, Exalted is He, at the end of this sura: قُلْ يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ فِي شَكٍّ مِنْ دِينِي. And it has been said: Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, knew that the Prophet ﷺ never doubted at all, so what is meant by this is stirring him up (al-tahyīj); for when he ﷺ heard this speech he would say: I do not doubt, O Lord, and I do not ask. And al-Zajjāj said that Allah addressed the Messenger ﷺ in His saying (فإن كنت في شك), while it encompasses all of creation; so it is like His saying يا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ إِذا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّساءَ. This is a good approach. But there is remoteness in it, because the Prophet ﷺ is included in this address and the objection remains standing. The other view is that this address is not to the Prophet ﷺ at all. The rationale of this view is that people in his time were three groups: one believing him, one belying him, and one doubting; so the Exalted addressed the third group with this speech, and Allah knows best.
And they differed regarding those to be asked in His saying, Exalted is He, in this verse, فَسْئَلِ الَّذِينَ يَقْرَؤُنَ الْكِتابَ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ. The meticulous scholars among the people of exegesis said: they are those of the People of the Book who believed, such as ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām and his companions, because they are the ones whose reports are trusted.

safi-cedvel:95-95.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction. (لا تكونن) like the previous one «1», (من) a preposition. (الذين) a relative in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of takūnanna. (كذّبوا) a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). (بآيات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (كذّبوا), (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr). (الفاء) the fāʾ of causation (fāʾ al-sababiyya). (تكون) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb — abrogating (nāsikh) — accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the fāʾ, and its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "you". (من الخاسرين) like من الممترين «2».
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تكون) is conjoined to a maṣdar extracted from the preceding النبي [Translator's note: so in the source; «النهي» (the prohibition) is evidently meant], i.e. "let there not be from you a belying of the signs of Allah, and so loss".
The clause «لا تكوننّ ...» is conjoined to the clause لا تكوننّ من الممترين «3». [Translator's note: the source does not state the clause's position here.]
The clause «كذّبوا ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «تكون ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila of the implied particle relative (أن).

safi-cedvel:96-98.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّ) a particle resembling the verb. (الذين) a relative in the position of accusative as the noun of inna. (حقّت) a past verb.. and (التاء) for the feminine. (على) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (حقّت), (كلمة) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ). (ربّ) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), and (الكاف) in the position of genitive by annexation. (لا) negative. (يؤمنون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is fāʿil.
The clause «إنّ الذين حقّت ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «حقّت.. كلمة....» has no grammatical position; ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «لا يؤمنون» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of inna.
(الواو) the wāw of ḥāl. (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle. (جاءت) like حقّت, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (كلّ) fāʿil, nominative. (آية) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (حتى) a particle of limit (ghāya) and a preposition. (يروا) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), and the sign of the accusative is the dropping of the nūn..
and the wāw is fāʿil. (العذاب) mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (الأليم) naʿt (adjective) of العذاب, accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يروا) is in the position of genitive by (حتّى), attached to (لا يؤمنون).
The clause «جاءتهم كلّ آية ...» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of يؤمنون..
And the apodosis (jawāb) of law is omitted, what precedes it indicating it.
The clause «يروا ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila of the implied particle relative (أن).
(الفاء) conjunction. (لولا) a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ) in the sense of هلّا, containing the sense of reproach. (كانت) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb [Note: Or complete (tāmm), its fāʿil being (قرية), and the clause آمنت a naʿt of قرية.. And the word قرية is a majāz mursal (metonymic trope) by which its inhabitants are meant.] and (التاء) for the feminine. (قرية) the noun of kānat, nominative. (آمنت) like حقّت [Note: In verse (96) of this sura.], (الفاء) conjunction. (نفع) a past verb, and (ها) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (إيمان) fāʿil, nominative, and (ها) muḍāf ilayhi. (إلّا) a particle of exception. (قوم) excepted, accusative [Note: It has been said: the exception is disjoined (munqaṭiʿ), because the people are not of the genus of the town.. And it has been said: rather it is joined (muttaṣil), because by the town its inhabitants are meant.] (يونس) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and the sign of the genitive is the fatḥa. (لما) an adverb in the sense of "when", containing the sense of condition, attached to (كشفنا), (آمنوا) a past verb and its fāʿil. (كشفنا) a past verb and its fāʿil. (عن) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (كشفنا), (عذاب) mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (الخزي) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (في الحياة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to عذاب [Note: Or to a ḥāl from it.], (الدنيا) naʿt of الحياة, genitive, and the sign of the genitive is the kasra implied (muqaddar) on the alif. (الواو) conjunction. (متّعنا) like كشفنا, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (إلى حين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (متّعناهم).
The clause «لولا كانت قرية ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the preceding resumptive clause.
The clause «آمنت ...» is in the position of accusative as khabar of kānat [Note: Or it is a naʿt of قرية, and the clause نفعها إيمانها is the khabar of kānat, with the fāʾ being redundant in the khabar.].
The clause «نفعها إيمانها» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause آمنت.
The clause «آمنوا ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «كشفنا ...» has no grammatical position; apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «متّعناهم ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the apodosis clause.

* Morphology:
(يونس), a foreign name. In Lisān al-ʿArab it comes: «يونس — with ḍamma, fatḥa and kasra on the nūn — three dialectal forms — the name of a man, and the hamza has also been reported in it.» End of quote.

* Benefits:
- The inimitability of the Qur'an:
In these two verses there is one of the aspects of the inimitability (iʿjāz) of the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, for He affirms in them:
that those against whom the word of disbelief has come due will never believe, and will not acknowledge the truth of Islam until they see the painful punishment on the Day of Resurrection. The aspect of inimitability is that we see with our own eyes a group of people who persist in disbelief and go deep in it, and who never believe, however much proof, evidence and persuasion you make clear to them; and they remain insistent on disbelief, such that even if you showed them Allah openly they would say: this is sorcery and falsehood. This group is not particular to one time rather than another; rather it has existed from the time of Adam and his offspring until the coming of the Hour. So if you see a person persisting in disbelief and never being convinced of Islam, which is the truth, this is a proof of the truthfulness of the Noble Qur'an, and that it is from Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, who created man and knows what he is upon.
- Mention of the story of the people of Yūnus:
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Wahb and others mentioned it. They said: The people of Yūnus were in the town of Nineveh, in the land of Mosul, and they were people of disbelief and polytheism. So Allah, Glorified is He, sent to them Yūnus, upon him be blessing and peace, calling them to belief in Allah, but they refused him. So it was said to him: Tell them that the punishment will come upon them in the morning within three days. He told them that, and they said: We have never found him to lie, so watch: if he spends the night among you tonight, then it is nothing; but if he does not spend the night, then know that the punishment will come upon you in the morning. When it was the middle of the night, Yūnus went out from among them, and when they woke in the morning the punishment covered them, and it was above their heads. Ibn ʿAbbās said: The punishment had been sent down upon the people of Yūnus until there was between them and it only the measure of two-thirds of a mile; then when they supplicated, Allah removed that from them. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: The punishment covered the people of Yūnus as the garment covers the grave. And Wahb said: When the punishment covered them, they went out with their children, their livestock and their women to the open desert, put on sackcloth, and proclaimed Islam and repentance, and they were sincere; so their Lord had mercy on them, answered their supplication, and removed from them what had descended upon them. This is of Allah's great mercy to His servants, and that He accepts repentance and pardons evil deeds, and does not pour out the whip of His punishment except upon a people whose belief is not hoped for.
- In this verse occurs His saying, Exalted is He, فَلَوْلا كانَتْ قَرْيَةٌ آمَنَتْ فَنَفَعَها إِيمانُها إِلَّا قَوْمَ يُونُسَ. Views have been put forward about (لولا) in this verse, and Ibn Hishām spoke on this topic, saying: "Al-Harawī mentioned that لولا can be negative, in the status of لم, and he counted among such the (لولا) occurring in this verse. But what is apparent is that the meaning is one of reproach, i.e. 'why was there not a single town among the destroyed towns that turned back [Translator's note: the source has «ثابت», evidently for «تابت» (repented)] from disbelief before the coming of the punishment, so that that benefited it?' This is the interpretation of al-Akhfash, al-Kisāʾī, al-Farrāʾ, ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā and al-Naḥḥās, and it is supported by the reading of Ubayy and ʿAbd Allāh (فهلّا كانت). Negation follows necessarily from this meaning, because reproach entails non-occurrence. It may be imagined that al-Zamakhsharī holds that it is for negation, because of his saying: 'The exception is disjoined (munqaṭiʿ), in the sense of لكن ("but"), and it may be joined (muttaṣil), the clause being in the sense of negation, as though it were said: "no [town] believed"'; but perhaps he only meant what we have mentioned, and for this reason he said: 'and the clause is in the sense of negation', and did not say: 'and لولا is for negation'. The Seven (i.e. the readers) agreed on the accusative in (إلا قوم), which indicates that the speech is affirmative (mūjab), but there is in it a scent of non-affirmation, like the saying of al-Akhṭal:
وبالصريمة منزل منزل خلق ... عاف تغيّر إلا النؤي والوتد
(And at al-Ṣarīma there is a worn-out dwelling, effaced, changed, all but the trench and the tent-peg.) [Translator's note: the source repeats «منزل»; the verse is usually cited as «وبالصريمة منهم منزل خلق».]
عاف: effaced (ruined). النؤي: a trench around the tent that keeps water from it. In this verse there is a scent of negation, because تغيّر means 'did not remain as it was'."

safi-cedvel:99-100.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (لو شاء) like لو جاء [Note: In verse (97) of this sura.], (ربّ) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), and (الكاف) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (اللام) linking the apodosis (jawāb) of law. (آمن) a past verb. (من) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as fāʿil. (في الأرض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of من. (كلّ) semantic tawkīd (emphasis) of the relative noun, following it in the nominative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (جميعا) an emphasizing ḥāl (circumstantial) from the relative noun, accusative (manṣūb). (الهمزة) for interrogation. (الفاء) conjunction. (أنت) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) [Note: Or the fāʿil of an omitted verb explained by the one mentioned, in the manner of ishtighāl, i.e.: "will you (أنت) compel the people ...". That is because the interrogative hamza is more closely attached to the verb than to the noun.], (تكره) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is "you". (الناس) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative. (حتّى) a particle of limit (ghāya) and a preposition. (يكونوا) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after حتّى.. and the wāw is a pronoun, the noun of kāna. (مؤمنين) khabar (predicate), accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يكونوا..) is in the position of genitive by (حتّى), attached to (تكره).
The clause «لو شاء ربّك ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «آمن من في الأرض» has no grammatical position; apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «أنت تكره ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «تكره الناس ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ أنت.
The clause «يكونوا ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila of the implied particle relative (أن).
(الواو) conjunction. (ما) negative. (كان) an incomplete past verb — abrogating (nāsikh) — [Note: It may be complete (tāmm), in the sense of "to be right" or "to be fitting", the fāʿil being the interpreted maṣdar.], (لنفس) a preposition and its genitive noun, fronted khabar [Note: Or attached to the complete verb كان.], (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle that makes accusative. (تؤمن) an imperfect verb, accusative, and the fāʿil is "she".
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تؤمن) is in the position of nominative as the postponed noun of kāna.
(إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). (بإذن) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl from the fāʿil of تؤمن, i.e. "except accompanied by the permission of Allah". (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr).
(الواو) conjunction. (يجعل) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is "he". (الرجس) mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (على) a preposition. (الذين) a relative in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi of the verb يجعل. (لا) negative. (يعقلون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is fāʿil.
The clause «ما كان لنفس ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause شاء ربّك.
The clause «تؤمن ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «يجعل ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to an implied clause, i.e. "so He permits some to believe, and makes ..." etc.
The clause «لا يعقلون» has no grammatical position; ṣila of the relative (الذين).

safi-cedvel:101-101.t:
* I'rab:
(قل) an imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "you". (انظروا) an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is fāʿil. (ماذا) an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) [Note: Or (ما) is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ, and (ذا) a relative noun, khabar (predicate), and (في السموات) the ṣila (relative clause).], (في السموات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. (الواو) conjunction. (الأرض) conjoined to السموات, genitive (majrūr). (الواو) parenthetical. (ما) negative [Note: Or an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, i.e.: "what avail"], (تغني) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the sign of the nominative is the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, (الآيات) fāʿil, nominative. (الواو) conjunction. (النذر) conjoined to الآيات, nominative. (عن قوم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تغني), (لا يؤمنون) like لا يعقلون [Note: In the previous verse (100).].
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «انظروا ...» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «ماذا في السموات ...» is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb of looking, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative.
The clause «تغني الآيات» has no grammatical position; a parenthetical tail-clause (iʿtirāḍ tadhyīlī) to the preceding clause.
The clause «لا يؤمنون» is in the position of genitive as naʿt (adjective) of قوم.

safi-cedvel:102-102.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive. (ينتظرون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).. and the wāw is fāʿil (agent). And (هل) interrogative in the sense of negation. (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). (مثل) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb). (أيّام) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr). (الذين) a relative in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. (خلوا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif that is dropped because of the meeting of two quiescents.. and the wāw is fāʿil. (من قبل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (خلوا), and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. (قل) like the earlier one «1», (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition. (انتظروا) like انظروا «2», (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, and (الياء) a pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of inna. (مع) an adverb, accusative, attached to المنتظرين, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (من المنتظرين) a preposition and its genitive noun, khabar (predicate) of inna.
The clause «هل ينتظرون ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive [Note: It may be in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied jussive condition, i.e.: "if the warnings do not avail them, then do they await anything but the like of the days of those who passed away (خلو) [Translator's note: so in the source, for «خلوا»]....?"].
The clause «خلوا ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «انتظروا ...» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e. "if you are awaiting that, then wait ...", and the clause of the condition and apodosis is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «إنّي معكم من المنتظرين» has no grammatical position; it has the status of a causal (taʿlīliyya) clause.

safi-cedvel:103-103.t:
* I'rab:
(ثمّ) a conjunction. (ننجي) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the sign of the nominative is the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, and the fāʿil (agent) is "We", for majesty. (رسل) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (الواو) conjunction. (الذين) a relative in the position of accusative, conjoined to رسل. (آمنوا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is fāʿil. (الكاف) a preposition. (ذلك) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) whose governor is ننجي.. and (اللام) for distance, and (الكاف) for address. (حقّا) a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, i.e. حقّ ذلك حقّا ("that is truly due") [Note: It may be a badal (substitute) from the maṣdar to which (كذلك) is attached.], (على) a preposition and (نا) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (حقّا), (ننجي) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the ḍamma implied on the yāʾ; the yāʾ has been dropped in the script of the Muṣḥaf because it fell away in pronunciation due to the meeting of two quiescents, and the fāʿil is "We", for majesty. (المؤمنين) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ.
The clause «ننجي ...» is conjoined to implied speech, i.e.: "We destroy the nations, then We save Our messengers".
The clause «آمنوا» has no grammatical position; ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «(حقّ) حقا..» has no grammatical position; parenthetical.
The clause «ننجي (the second)» has no grammatical position; resumptive.

* Rhetoric:
Representational simile (al-tashbīh al-tamthīlī): in His saying, Exalted is He, «كَذلِكَ حَقًّا عَلَيْنا نُنْجِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ», i.e. "like that saving, We save the believers among you and destroy the polytheists". He likened the salvation of those believers who remain to the salvation of those who passed, and the point of resemblance is that each of them deserves salvation.

safi-cedvel:104-106.t:
* I'rab:
(قل) an imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "you". (يا) a vocative particle. (أيّ) the one addressed, an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of accusative, and (ها) a particle of alerting (tanbīh). (الناس) badal (substitute) from أيّ — or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) — following it in the nominative in form. (أن) [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has «إن»] a conditional particle that makes jussive. (كنتم) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb — abrogating (nāsikh) — indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).. and the wāw is the noun of kāna. (في شكّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, khabar (predicate) of kuntum. (من ديني) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) شك, and the sign of the genitive is the kasra implied (muqaddar) on what precedes the yāʾ.. and (الياء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (لا) negative. (أعبد) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil is "I". (الذين) a relative in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (تعبدون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is fāʿil. (من دون) a preposition and its genitive noun, ḥāl (circumstantial) from the omitted referential pronoun, i.e. "you worship it, being other than Allah". (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr). (الواو) conjunction. (لكن) a particle of rectification (istidrāk) with no governing effect. (أعبد الله) like أعبد الذين. (الذي) a relative in the position of accusative as naʿt (adjective) of the Name of Majesty. (يتوفّى) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the implied ḍamma, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is "he". (الواو) conjunction. (أمرت) a passive past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn.. and (التاء) is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle that makes accusative. (أكون) an incomplete imperfect verb — abrogating — and its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "I". (من المؤمنين) a preposition and its genitive noun, khabar of akūna, and the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن أكون) is in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, attached to (أمرت), i.e. "to be" (بأن أكون) [Note: The interpreted maṣdar may be a mafʿūl bihi of the verb أمرت.].
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «the vocative ...» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «إن كنتم في شك» has no grammatical position; response to the vocative.
The clause «لا أعبد ...» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «تعبدون ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «أعبد الله» is in the position of jussive, conjoined to the clause لا أعبد.
The clause «يتوفّاكم» has no grammatical position; ṣila of the relative (الذي).
The clause «أمرت ...» is in the position of jussive, conjoined to the clause لا أعبد.
The clause «أكون ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
(الواو) conjunction. (أن) an explicative particle [Note: Or a maṣdar-forming particle, the interpreted maṣdar being the nāʾib fāʿil of the verb أوحي إليّ ("it was revealed to me"), or قيل لي ("it was said to me").] with an implied verb, i.e. "it was revealed to me that ...". (أقم) an imperative verb, and the fāʿil is "you". (وجه) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb), and (الكاف) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (للدين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أقم), (حنيفا) ḥāl, accusative, from the pronoun of the fāʿil in أقم, or from الدين. (الواو) conjunction. (لا) prohibitive, making jussive. (تكوننّ) an incomplete imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of jussive.. and (النون) is the nūn of emphasis, and its noun is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you". (من المشركين) a preposition and its genitive noun, khabar of takūnanna, and the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ.
The clause «أقم ...» has no grammatical position; explicative.. and the implied clause "it was revealed to me".. is in the position of jussive, conjoined to the clause لا أعبد ...
The clause «لا تكوننّ ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the explicative clause.
(الواو) conjunction. (لا) prohibitive, making jussive. (تدع) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and the sign of the jussive is the dropping of the weak letter, and the fāʿil is "you". (من دون) a preposition and its genitive noun, ḥāl from the relative ما. (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi. (لا) negative. (ينفع) an imperfect verb, nominative, and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is "you" [Translator's note: so in the source; the fāʿil of ينفعك is a latent pronoun "it" referring to ما]. (الواو) conjunction. (لا يضرّك) like لا ينفعك, (الفاء) resumptive. (إن) a conditional particle that makes jussive. (فعلت) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of jussive as the protasis.. and (التاء) is fāʿil. (الفاء) linking the apodosis. (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of inna. (إذا) a particle of response with no governing effect. (من الظالمين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the khabar of inna, and the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ.
The clause «لا تدع ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause أقم [Note: Or it is conjoined to the clause قل يأيّها الناس.. And it may be resumptive.].
The clause «لا ينفعك ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «لا يضرّك» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «إن فعلت ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «إنّك.. من الظالمين» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of the jussive condition.

* Morphology:
(تدع), in it there is iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by dropping, owing to the jussive; its origin is تدعو, and its pattern is تفع.

* Benefits:
In this verse occurs His saying, Exalted is He, وَلكِنْ أَعْبُدُ اللَّهَ الَّذِي يَتَوَفَّاكُمْ. Allah, Majestic and Exalted is He, has brought the attribute of "taking in death" (al-tawaffī) in this verse, and we will present the wisdom of that as the exegetes stated it: What is meant is that the One who deserves worship, so that I and you should worship Him, is the One who created you first when you were nothing, then causes you to die second, then gives you life after death. So He sufficed with mentioning death as an alert to the rest, and that the One who gives life and causes death is more worthy of worship than any other. And it has been said: since death is the hardest of things on the soul, it was mentioned in this place so as to be stronger in restraint and deterrence. And it has been said: when they were hasty in demanding the punishment, He answered them with His saying: "but I worship Allah, who is able to destroy you and to grant me victory over you". This is of the inimitability of the speech of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and that there is no word but it has been placed in its proper place.

semin-durr:3-3.t: The words of the Exalted: {يُدَبِّرُ الأمر} — there are three views on it. First: it is in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as a second khabar (predicate) of «إنَّ». Second: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial). Third: it is resumptive (mustaʾnaf), a clause with no grammatical position.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
The words of the Exalted: {وَعْدَ الله}: accusative (manṣūb) as the emphasizing maṣdar (verbal noun) [i.e. mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of emphasis], because the meaning of «إليه مَرْجِعُكُمْ» is: He has promised you that.
And His words: {حَقّاً} are another maṣdar, emphasizing the meaning of this promise, and what governs it in the accusative is concealed, i.e. «أَحُقُّ ذلك حقاً» (I affirm that as a truth). It was also said: «حقاً» is accusative through «وَعْدَ» with «في» implied, i.e. «وَعْدَ الله في حق» (Allah's promise in truth), meaning by likening it to an adverb (ẓarf). Al-Akhfash the Younger said: "The implied form is: «وقتَ حق» (at a time of truth)," and he recited:
2566 - أحقاً عبادَ الله أنْ لَسْتُ ذاهباً ... ولا والِجاً إلا عليَّ رقيبُ
(Is it truly so, O servants of Allah, that I do not go out nor come in without a watcher over me?)
His words: {إِنَّهُ يَبْدَأُ}: the majority read the hamza with kasra (إِنَّه), as a resumptive clause. ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd], Ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ, al-Aʿmash and Sahl ibn Shuʿayb read it with fatḥa (أَنَّه). There are several interpretations of this reading. First: it is the fāʿil (agent) of the verb that governs «حقاً» in the accusative, i.e. «حَقَّ حَقَّاً بَدْءُ الخلق ثم إعادتُه» (truly true is the origination of creation and then its repetition), as in the poet's words:
2567 - أحقاً عبادَ الله أَنْ لستُ جائِياً ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Is it truly so, O servants of Allah, that I do not come…)
— the verse [as above]. This is the position of al-Farrāʾ, for he said: "The implied form is: «يحقُّ أنه يبدأ الخلق» (it is true that He originates creation)." Second: it is accusative through the verb that governed «وعد الله» in the accusative, i.e. Allah the Exalted promised the origination of creation and then its repetition, the meaning being the repetition of creation after its origination. Third: it is with the lām of the genitive omitted, i.e. «لأنه» (because He…). Al-Zamakhsharī and others mentioned these three views. Fourth: it is a badal (substitute) from «وَعْدَ الله»; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. Fifth: it is nominative through «حقاً» itself, i.e. through the nunated maṣdar; this only works if «حقاً» is made non-emphasizing, because the emphasizing maṣdar has no governing power unless it stands in for its verb — and there is some discussion of this. Sixth: «حقاً» is likened to an adverb, serving as a fronted khabar, and «أنَّه» is in the position of nominative as a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), as in their saying «أحقاً أنك ذاهب» (Is it true that you are going?), of which they said: its implied form is «أفي حقٍ ذهابك» (Is your going in truth?).
Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «حَقٌّ أنه» with «حق» in the nominative and «أنَّ» with fatḥa, as mubtadaʾ and khabar. Al-Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "That «حق» is the khabar of a mubtadaʾ and «أنه» is the mubtadaʾ is the [correct] way of parsing it, just as you say «صحيحٌ أنك تخرج» (it is correct that you are going out), because the noun of «أنَّ» is definite, while what precedes it in this example is indefinite." I say: the apparent sense of this phrasing suggests that the reverse is permissible, and this has indeed occurred in the chapter of «إنَّ», as in the poet's words:
2568 - وإن حراماً أن أَسُبَّ مُجاشعاً ... بآبائيَ الشُّمِّ الكرامِ الخَضَارمِ
(And it is indeed forbidden that I should revile Mujāshiʿ by my lofty, noble, generous forefathers.)
And his words:
2569 - وإن شفاءً عَبْرَةٌ أَنْ سَفَحْتُها وهل عند رسمٍ دارسٍ مِنْ مُعَوَّل ...
(And indeed a cure is a tear, that I should shed it — yet is there any recourse at an effaced trace of a dwelling?)
— taking «أنْ سفحتُها» as a badal from «عبرة». And with «كان», an indefinite has been made the subject of which a definite is predicated, as in the poet's words:
2570 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ولا يكُ موقفٌ منكِ الوَدَاعا
(…and let not a halting with you be the farewell.)
And his words:
2571 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... يكون مزاجَها عَسَلٌ وماءُ
(…its mixture being honey and water.)
Makkī said: "Al-Farrāʾ allowed the nominative of «وعد», making it the khabar of «مرجعكم». And he allowed the nominative of «وعد» and «حق» as mubtadaʾ and khabar, and that is good, but no one read it so." I say: yes, no one read both «وعد» and «حق» in the nominative together; as for the nominative of «حق» alone, it has been stated above that Ibn Abī ʿAbla read it so, and its justification has been given. It is not permissible for «وعدَ الله» to govern «أنه», because it has been qualified by His words «حقاً»; Abū al-Fatḥ [Ibn Jinnī] said this.
And it was read «وَعَدَ اللَّهُ» in the form of the past verb with the Name of Majesty in the nominative as its fāʿil; on this reading «أنه يَبْدَأ» is governed by it, if this reader reads «أنه» with fatḥa.
The majority read «يَبْدأُ» with fatḥa on the yāʾ, from «بدأ»; Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa read «يُبْدِىء» from «أَبْدأ»; «بَدَأ» and «أبدأ» have the same meaning.
His words: {لِيَجْزِيَ} are attached to His words «ثم يُعيده», and «بالقسطِ» is attached to «يَجْزي». It may also be a ḥāl, either from the fāʿil or from the object, i.e. He recompenses them while being in conjunction with justice, or while they are in conjunction with it. «القِسْط» means justice.
His words: {والذين كَفَرُواْ} admit two views. First: it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and the clause after it is its khabar. Second: it is accusative, conjoined to the relative noun before it, and the clause after it explains their recompense. «شراب» may be a fāʿil, or a mubtadaʾ; the first is preferable.
His words: {بِمَا كَانُواْ}: the apparent view is that it is attached to the [notion of] settled being (istiqrār) concealed in the preposition-phrase that serves as the khabar, the implied form being: «استقر لهم شراب من جهنم وعذاب أليم بما كانوا» (there is settled for them a drink from Hell and a painful punishment because of what they used to…). Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed two views for it and mentioned no others. First: it is another naʿt (adjective) of «عذاب». Second: it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ — and this has no meaning, and there is no need to depart from the first view.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
The words of the Exalted: {ضِيَآءً}: either a second object, taking «الجَعْل» in the sense of transforming (taṣyīr), or a ḥāl (circumstantial), taking it in the sense of bringing into being (inshāʾ). The majority read «ضياء» with an explicit yāʾ before the alif, its origin being wāw because it is from «الضوء». Qunbul, from Ibn Kathīr, read here, in al-Anbiyāʾ and in al-Qaṣaṣ «ضِئاءً», changing the yāʾ into a hamza, so that there is an alif between two hamzas. This was interpreted as a case of metathesis (maqlūb): its lām [third radical] was moved forward and its ʿayn [second radical] moved back, so the yāʾ fell at the end after a superfluous alif and was changed into a hamza, as in «رداء». Or, if you wish, you may say: when the word was metathesized it became «ضياواً» with wāw, the ʿayn reverting to its original wāw because the cause of its change into yāʾ — the kasra preceding it — no longer existed; then the wāw was replaced by a hamza, as in «كساء». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It was changed into an alif and then the alif was changed into a hamza so that two alifs would not come together."
This reading was considered unlikely on the grounds that the language is built on lightening the hamza, so how could they contrive to change a light letter into something heavier than it? I say: there is nothing strange in that, for they have changed the weak letters — alif, wāw and yāʾ — into hamza in places that can hardly be counted; except that here it is heavy because two hamzas come together. Abū Shāma said: "This is a weak reading, for the analogy of the language is to flee from the meeting of two hamzas towards lightening one of them; so how could one contrive a fronting and delaying that leads to the meeting of two hamzas that were not there originally? This is contrary to the rule of the language."
Abū Bakr Ibn Mujāhid — who was one of those who read under Qunbul — said: "Ibn Kathīr alone [read] «ضِئاء» with two hamzas throughout the Quran: the first hamza before the alif and the second after it. That is how I read it under Qunbul, and it is a mistake. The companions of al-Bazzī and Ibn Fulayḥ used to reject this and read «ضياء» like everyone else." I say: Abū Bakr often presumes against his teacher and declares him mistaken — you will come across several places of that kind — and this ought not to be, for Qunbul is of a standing that prevents anyone from speaking against him.
And His saying «ضياء» with respect to the sun is because «الضوء» (radiance) is stronger than «النور» (light); this was discussed at the beginning of al-Baqara. «ضياء ونوراً» may both be maṣdars (verbal nouns), made to be the two heavenly bodies themselves for hyperbole, or [they may be] on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. «ذات ضياء وذا نور» (possessing radiance and possessing light). «ضياء» may also be the plural of «ضوء», like «سَوْط / سِياط» and «حَوْض / حياض».
«منازل» is accusative as an adverb of place. Al-Zamakhsharī took it to be on the omission of a muḍāf, either from the first [element], i.e. «قَدَّر مَسيره» (He determined its course [in stations]), or from the second, i.e. «قدَّره ذا منازل» (He determined it as possessing stations). On the first implied form «منازل» is an adverb as already stated; on the second it is a second object, with «قَدَّر» being made to include the meaning «صَيَّره ذا منازل بالتقدير» (He made it, by determination, possess stations). Al-Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān], after mentioning the two implied forms without attributing them to al-Zamakhsharī, said: "Or: «قدَّر له منازل» (He determined stations for it); then [the preposition] was omitted and the verb reached it directly, so it became accusative. According to these implied forms it is accusative as an adverb, a ḥāl or an object, as in His words: {والقمر قَدَّرْنَاهُ مَنَازِلَ} [Yā Sīn: 39]." Abū al-Baqāʾ had also preceded him in that.
The pronoun in «قَدَّرناه» refers to the moon alone, because it is what the Arabs relied on in their reckoning of dates. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It may be that He intends both of them together, in that both play a role in knowing the number of years and the reckoning, but mention of one of them sufficed, as in the words of the Exalted: {والله وَرَسُولُهُ أَحَقُّ أَن يُرْضُوهُ} [al-Tawba: 62], and as the poet said:
2572 - رماني بأمرٍ كنتُ منه ووالدي ... بريئاً ومِنْ أجل الطَّوِيِّ رماني
(He accused me of a matter of which I and my father were innocent, and on account of the well he accused me.)"
[Translator's note: the closing quotation mark of Ibn ʿAṭiyya's quotation is not marked in the source; its end is placed here as the most likely reading.]

semin-durr:6-6.t:
The words of the Exalted: {لِتَعْلَمُواْ}: attached to «قَدَّره». Abū ʿAmr was asked about «الحساب»: "Do you put it in the accusative or the genitive?" He said: "And who knows what the number of the reckoning is?" Meaning: he was asked whether you conjoin it to «عَددَ» and so put it in the accusative, or to «السنين» and so put it in the genitive; and it is as though he said: it cannot be in the genitive, since that would require that the number of the reckoning be known, and no one is able to know its number. «ذلك» points to what has preceded, i.e. Allah did not create that which has been mentioned except in conjunction with the truth; so [«بالحق»] is a ḥāl (circumstantial), either from the fāʿil (agent) or from the object. It was also said: the bāʾ has the meaning of the lām, i.e. «للحق» (for the truth), but there is no need for that.
Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read «يُفَصِّل» with the yāʾ of the third person, in accordance with the Name of Allah the Exalted; the rest read with the nūn of majesty, a shift (iltifāt) from the third person to the first person for magnification.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
The words of the Exalted: {واطمأنوا}: it may be conjoined to the ṣila (relative clause), and that is the apparent view; or the wāw may be circumstantial (wāw al-ḥāl), the implied form being «وقد اطمأنُّوا» (having become content). His words «والذين هم» may be a case of conjoining attributes, meaning that they combine not hoping for the meeting with Allah and heedlessness of the signs; or this relative noun may be other than the first, so that it is conjoined to the noun of «إن», i.e. «إن الذين لا يَرْجُون، وإن الذين هم» (indeed those who do not hope…, and indeed those who are…).
[Translator's note: the source has «عدم رجال لقاء الله», evidently a misprint for «عدم رجاء لقاء الله» (not hoping for the meeting with Allah); translated accordingly.]

semin-durr:8-8.t: And {أولئك} is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «مَأْواهم» is a second mubtadaʾ, and «النار» is the khabar (predicate) of this second one; the second and its khabar are the khabar of «أولئك», and «أولئك» with its khabar is the khabar of «إن الذين». «بما كانوا» is attached to what is contained in the clause «مَأْواهم النار»; the bāʾ is causal and «ما» is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), and the verb after it is brought in the imperfect to indicate the continuity of that at all times. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The bāʾ is attached to something omitted, i.e. «جُوزوا بما كانوا» (they were recompensed for what they used to…)."

semin-durr:9-9.t: The words of the Exalted: {تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِهِمُ الأنهار}: it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object of «يَهْديهم», or resumptive, or conjoined to what precedes it with the conjunction omitted. His words «في جنات» may be attached to «تَجْري», or be a ḥāl from «الأنهار», or be a khabar (predicate) after a khabar of «إنَّ», or be attached to «يَهْدي».

semin-durr:10-10.t:
The words of the Exalted: {دَعْوَاهُمْ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «سبحانَك», governed by an implied verb that may not be made overt, is the khabar (predicate); the khabar here is the mubtadaʾ itself, the meaning being that their supplication is this utterance. So «دعوى» may have the meaning of supplication (duʿāʾ), and «اللهم» indicates this, because it is a vocative meaning «يا الله» (O Allah). This «دعاء» here may also have the meaning of worship, so «دَعْوى» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) annexed to its agent. Then, if you wish, you may make this a case of verbal predication (isnād lafẓī), i.e. their supplication in Paradise is this very utterance, so that «سبحانك» itself is the khabar, brought in as a quotation in its accusative form [governed] by that verb; or, if you wish, you may make it a case of semantic predication (isnād maʿnawī), so that it is not required that they say only this utterance; rather they say it and whatever conveys its meaning of all the attributes of transcendence and sanctification. You have had the like of this before at the words of the Exalted: {وَقُولُواْ حِطَّةٌ} [al-Baqara: 58], so turn to it.
«تحيَّتُهم» is a mubtadaʾ and «سَلامٌ» its khabar, and it is like what precedes it.
